item.title: India Does Not Seek to Occupy Any Country’s Territory, But Will Safeguard Its Security and Strategic Autonomy When Threatened: Rajnath Singh
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Defence
item.description: Ministry of Defence India Does Not Seek to Occupy Any Country’s Territory, But Will Safeguard Its Security and Strategic Autonomy When Threatened: Rajnath Singh As a Civilizational Power, India’s Rise is in the Interest of the Entire World India Moving from Defence Importer to Trusted Global Defence Supplier National Unity is Essential for National Security: Rajnath Singh Posted On: 27 SEP 2026 1:40PM by PIB Delhi “India believes in peace and does not seek to occupy the territory of any country. However, peace should not be mistaken for weakness. We seek global…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
India Does Not Seek to Occupy Any Country’s Territory, But Will Safeguard Its Security and Strategic Autonomy When Threatened: Rajnath Singh
As a Civilizational Power, India’s Rise is in the Interest of the Entire World
India Moving from Defence Importer to Trusted Global Defence Supplier
National Unity is Essential for National Security: Rajnath Singh
Posted On: 27 SEP 2026 1:40PM by PIB Delhi

“India believes in peace and does not seek to occupy the territory of any country. However, peace should not be mistaken for weakness. We seek global stability, but not at the cost of our strategic autonomy. We are firmly committed to safeguarding our security and strategic autonomy when threatened,” said Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh while addressing a Defence Conclave in New Delhi on September 27, 2026.

Raksha Mantri underlined that there can be no scope for dialogue with any country that promotes terrorism against India. “Countries that use terrorism as an instrument of state policy or provide shelter and support to terrorists must be firmly reminded that terrorism cannot be a strategic asset for any nation. He asserted that as long as a neighbouring country continues to pursue a policy of supporting terrorism, India remains fully entitled to take all necessary measures against terrorism”, he said, referring to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s remarks at the recent SCO meeting.

Emphasising national unity as a key pillar of national security, the Raksha Mantri stated that the security of the country is not solely the responsibility of the armed forces but a collective responsibility of every citizen. He urged citizens to rise above divisions based on religion, caste, creed, language, region and other identities, and to place national interest above personal and narrow interests.

Shri Rajnath Singh described India as a civilizational power whose rise is based on inclusive development rather than confrontation or disruption. He outlined three foundations of India’s approach: its long democratic and civilizational traditions, the principle of ‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam’ and the vision of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas’, and five strategic pillars—respect, dialogue, prosperity, security and culture.

Focusing on the Global South, Raksha Mantri highlighted India’s growing role as a trusted partner and ‘Vishwa Bandhu’. He noted that under Vaccine Maitri, India supplied more than 30 crore COVID-19 vaccine doses to over 100 countries and has supported developing nations through medicines, digital payment solutions, expertise and resources. He also highlighted initiatives such as the Voice of Global South Summits to advance the interests of developing countries. Emphasising responsible use of power, he called for cooperation even amid competition and inclusive participation in global development.

Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted India’s significant progress towards self-reliance in defence, noting that the country is developing indigenous capabilities ranging from aircraft and drone engines to fifth- and sixth-generation fighter jets. India’s defence exports have grown from just ₹686 crore in 2013–14 to a record ₹38,424 crore in 2025–26, reaching more than 100 countries. After achieving the ₹30,000-crore export target last year, India has now set a target of ₹50,000 crore by 2029.

He emphasised that growing international demand for Indian missiles, radars, ammunition and defence platforms reflects global confidence in India’s technology, quality and delivery capabilities. Consequently, “Made in India” is increasingly emerging not merely as a manufacturing label, but as a symbol of trust in Indian defence capabilities.

Raksha Mantri highlighted the significant increase in defence allocation, which has reached ₹7.85 lakh crore in 2026-27, compared to around ₹2.53 lakh crore in 2013-14. He noted that around 75% of the capital acquisition budget, amounting to ₹1.39 lakh crore, has been earmarked for procurement from the domestic defence industry, thereby strengthening indigenous manufacturing and associated MSME supply chains.

Shri Rajnath Singh stated that the nature of warfare is rapidly changing, with modern conflicts extending beyond conventional domains to cyber, space, electronic and information warfare, alongside emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, drones, autonomous systems, quantum technology and hypersonic systems. He underlined the need for India to develop future-ready capabilities across these domains.

Highlighting India’s efforts to address strategic vulnerabilities in areas such as technology, energy, data and supply chains, the Raksha Mantri said that initiatives are underway to strengthen domestic capabilities in semiconductors and critical minerals, diversify energy sources and enhance energy security.

Emphasising the importance of self-reliance, the Raksha Mantri stated that 509 defence equipment, weapon systems and platforms have been included in five positive indigenisation lists issued by the Armed Forces. DPSUs have also released six indigenisation lists covering 5,417 items, including strategically important LRUs, subsystems, spares and components, of which around 3,300 have been indigenised.

He highlighted the growing participation of the private sector, startups and MSMEs in defence manufacturing. India’s defence ecosystem now includes DPSUs, private industries, more than 16,000 MSMEs, startups, universities and research institutions, with defence manufacturing capabilities emerging across several regions of the country. Investment proposals of about ₹70,000 crore have been received in the Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu Defence Industrial Corridors, with around ₹10,000 crore already invested.

Raksha Mantri also highlighted the role of the SRIJAN and SRIJAN DEEP portals in strengthening indigenous defence supply chains. He stated that around 33,000 imported items have been identified for import substitution through SRIJAN, of which approximately 15,700 have been indigenised. SRIJAN DEEP has created a national digital database covering more than 40,000 manufacturers and sellers and lakhs of products.

Shri Rajnath Singh underlined the transformation of the DPSU and Ordnance Factory ecosystem, noting that corporatisation of the Ordnance Factories has enhanced their technology orientation, output and accountability. He stated that all 16 DPSUs are currently operating without losses and are increasing their focus on research, development and exports.

Highlighting the role of youth and innovation, he said that iDEX and iDEX-Prime are providing opportunities for startups and innovators to contribute to national security, while programmes such as ADITI are supporting advanced defence technologies. As of March 2026, 676 startups and innovators had been engaged through iDEX and 551 contracts signed. The Ministry has also approved procurement worth more than ₹2,400 crore from startups/MSMEs and development projects worth over ₹1,500 crore.

A significant announcement was the decision to transfer DRDO-developed technologies for conventional missile systems to eligible Indian industries, enabling qualifying private companies to undertake production. Shri Rajnath Singh said the move would strengthen the preparedness of the Armed Forces and facilitate timely delivery of missiles. He added that DRDO is increasingly being positioned to focus on research and development while industry assumes a greater role in production.

Raksha Mantri concluded that India’s objective is to build indigenous capabilities across the entire defence spectrum—from individual components to complete weapon systems—and to develop technologies domestically rather than remain dependent on imports. He stressed that this approach is aimed at strengthening strategic autonomy, defence preparedness and a resilient indigenous defence-industrial ecosystem.

****

VK/SR/Kamlesh

(Release ID: 2315516)

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
English rendering of PM’s address in the 138th Episode of Mann Ki Baat on 27.09.2026
Posted On: 27 SEP 2026 11:40AM by PIB Delhi

My dear countrymen, Namaskar.

I am getting an opportunity to meet you once again for the September edition of ‘Mann Ki Baat’. I welcome all the people of the country. In ‘Mann Ki Baat’, we provide a platform for the positive efforts of our countrymen… discuss the nation's achievements. One such major, historic achievement of India is set to mark its 10th anniversary in just a day – this achievement is the ‘Surgical Strike’. Ten years ago, on September 28-29, 2016, the Indian Army carried out surgical strikes on terrorist hideouts in Pakistan. The world was astonished to see the manner in which our brave soldiers crossed the Line of Control (LoC) to take action against terrorism.

The surgical strike boldly demonstrated to the entire world a new example of India’s counter-terrorism policy. The ‘Surgical Strike’ was our decisive response to the long-standing pain India had endured due to terrorist attacks. Over the past decade - from the Balakot airstrike to ‘Operation Sindoor’ - India has repeatedly sent a clear message: if terrorists dare to cast an evil eye on India, they will be met with a befitting response.

Friends,

India has long suffered wounds inflicted by terrorist attacks. There was a time when serial blasts had become a common occurrence in the country. It was in this very month of September - specifically on September 13, 2008 - that many innocent lives were lost in the serial blasts in Delhi. Just a few weeks later, the massive 26/11 attack took place in Mumbai. Friends, in the past too, there used to be demands for action against Pakistan following every terror attack, but such calls were often not given due attention; time to pass by was simply awaited. Today, India pursues a zero-tolerance policy against terrorism, and we are witnessing the results of that.

Friends,

This year also marks 25 years since the 9/11 terrorist attacks. Among the innocent lives lost at the World Trade Center in the US, the highest number of victims—after Americans - was Indians. I recall that after becoming Prime Minister in 2014, when I visited the US, I had reached New York to pay my homage to those innocent citizens. Today, once again, I extend my condolences to the bereaved families on behalf of crores of Indian citizens.

My dear countrymen,

A grand picture of the nation is currently emerging. This picture includes you, your family and even your neighbours. I am referring to India's census. The first phase of this exercise is nearly complete across all states and union territories;

data of over 32 crore families has already been recorded. Work is currently underway also in the remote, snow-clad regions of Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, and Uttarakhand. Many inspiring experiences have emerged from these areas. In Uttarakhand, the census process began in the village of Mana in Chamoli; Mana is known as the country's first village. The process there started with 83-year-old Purnima Rawat ji. In Bagori village, Uttarkashi, Hardev Singh Rana ji—who runs a homestay—entered his details himself using digital means.

Friends,

The census is a national responsibility for all of us. On 15th August also, I had urged my countrymen to take time out for that. The facility to self-register your census details is very convenient. You can register information about yourself and your family from your mobile itself. Along with Hindi, this facility is available in 16 languages.

Friends,

To do this, you need to visit the census online portal. The portal is se.census.gov.in… log in using your mobile number, enter your location, fill in the details regarding your family and submit the information. The entire process takes about 15 to 20 minutes. And for that you do not need to upload any document. After submitting the information, you will receive a special ID. You can share this ID with the census enumerator when they visit your home. After the information you provided is verified, it will become part of the census record.

Friends,

So far, more than 2 crore 60 lakh people have already entered their details on the census portal via mobile - completing the self-enumeration. It will take a little of your time, but it is important for the nation, as accurate information about you and your family helps create a precise picture of the country's future.

My dear countrymen,

Today - the date 27th of September - has become even more special for a special reason. Today marks the 100th birth anniversary of a great personality who had dedicated his entire life to culture, society, and the nation. I am speaking of the revered late Ashok Singhal ji, the former International Working President of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad. He was born on this very day - September 27, 1926 - in Agra. Living amidst society, he led life like an ascetic. The very direction and energy he imparted to the Ram Janmabhoomi movement veritably resulted in us witnessing the magnificent temple in Ayodhya today. I’ve been greatly fortunate… I’ve not only observed his life closely but also have had the opportunity to join him in this mission. It was only natural for me to be reminded of Ashok ji repeatedly while participating in the Pran Pratishtha ceremony at the Ram Mandir.

Friends,

There are so many aspects about Ashok ji that do not receive much attention. Alongside the Ram Mandir movement, he also waged a major battle against social discrimination and inequality. He was born into a very affluent family; his father was a civil services official, and most of his siblings held high-ranking positions. He himself was a graduate of IIT BHU. Yet, despite all that, he dedicated his life to society and culture - this is the hallmark of great individuals. Today, on the occasion of his birth centenary, I bow to him on behalf of his millions of admirers… I offer my heartfelt tribute, on my part.

My dear countrymen,

We began this year with a grand celebration of national pride – This festival was the "Somnath Swabhiman Parv". A thousand years ago, in 1026, Mahmud of Ghazni had demolished the Somnath Temple for the first time. However, those who came to destroy Somnath and erase India's identity have no existence at all today, whereas the Somnath Temple stands in all its grandeur by the vast sea, bestowing the blessing of immortality upon India. That is why we celebrated the 'Somnath Swabhiman Parv' this year with immense pride.

Friends,

Why I am bringing this up again in 'Mann Ki Baat' today - there is a special reason for that. In 1026 AD when Somnath was destroyed by Ghazni; the same year, the famous Sun Temple in Modhera, Gujarat, was also attacked and destroyed. This means that a thousand years have passed since the destruction of the Modhera temple as well, whereas the temple then had been built just a year ago. King Bhimdev had got it built in 1025.

Friends,

Imagine that era; a massive invasion had taken place, a major center of faith like the Somnath Temple had been vandalised, and attacks were occurring at multiple locations - any society or administration could have had its morale shattered. Yet, King Bhimdev The First not only confronted the forces of Ghazni but also had the Modhera Sun Temple rebuilt within a short time. It is because of this very resilience that the Somnath Temple, too, was rebuilt every time despite facing repeated destruction.

Friends,

The attacks on the Modhera Sun Temple did not cease in later periods either. Alauddin Khilji later destroyed this temple, the magnificent architectural marvel once again. However, friends, we, the people of India, do not worship the Sun solely through architecture and temples; for us, Sun worship also signifies light, energy, science, and the inspiration for continuity. That is why Modhera is known today not just for its Sun Temple; this village in Gujarat has become the country's first ‘Surya Gram’ 'Solar Village.'

Modhera now runs entirely on solar energy, setting an example of sustainability for the nation. Several attractions and amenities for tourists have also been introduced in Modhera. The Modhera Dance Festival is held there in January, following Makar Sankranti, featuring magnificent performances of India's cultural and classical dances. I would urge all of you to visit Modhera at least once and witness this glorious Indian heritage.

Friends,

Our connection with the past remains very much alive today. This is driven by the dedication and hard work of individuals who are deepening this bond. A unique initiative of this kind is underway in Manapparai, Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu. A. Selvaraju ji, associated with the Department of Tamil Studies at a college, is spearheading this effort. During a lecture, he learned about some ancient sculptures from a student. Following a discussion on the subject, he planned a field visit. During this visit, he discovered several sculptures and ancient temples at various locations. This is a fascinating way to connect with the past; this way, we can understand our heritage even better. Similar initiatives can be undertaken in other parts of the country as well… they offer us the opportunity to observe and comprehend our history more closely.

My dear countrymen,

In just a few days, it’s the 2nd of October - the birth anniversary of revered Bapu. Bapu has given us many guiding principles for life… cleanliness is one of them. We often see numerous efforts related to cleanliness around us. These efforts are very inspiring and uplifting. Such photos, videos, and reels frequently catch our attention on social media as well. I have witnessed many such initiatives recently. At a place in Madhya Pradesh, young people are working to clean up a river; the entire community is joining in their small effort. Similarly, in Andhra Pradesh, the youth are cleaning up old stepwells and wells, thereby helping to restore our ancient heritage. In Mumbai, some young people are taking the initiative to keep beaches clean; every week, hundreds of young friends gather at one beach or the other to serve through cleanliness drives... Swachhata Se Sewa. Here in Delhi, children and the youth are raising awareness about segregating waste and maintaining cleanliness in their surroundings. In West Bengal, young students are collaborating with locals to clean up market areas at picnic spots.

Friends,

Across all these efforts, one aspect is easily observed… somewhere it starts with a single individual, other people join in, and the movement grows - this is precisely what 'Jan-Bhagidari' is all about. Indeed, cleanliness is the most beautiful tribute we can pay to Bapu.

My dear countrymen,

When we protect the environment, we do not merely save plants or animals; we strengthen that entire ecosystem. Some initiatives taking place in various parts of the country are beautifully highlighting this sentiment.

Friends,

There is the Sonai Rupai Wildlife Sanctuary in Assam. There was a time when elephants used to inhabit this area, but as human interference on forest land increased, the elephants moved away. Three years ago, this land was cleared of encroachment, and the results have been remarkable - the elephants have returned here again. Herds of elephants are once again being spotted in areas where they had not been active for years. Friends, another wonderful initiative has taken place in Assam itself - this effort is to save a tiny creature, the Pygmy Hog. Once, its very existence was under threat; at that time, a conservation program was launched with just six Pygmy Hogs, and they were reintroduced into the wild. Grasslands were also curated for their living. Today, thanks to this program, the Pygmy Hog population has risen to over 190.

Friends,

Our relationship with nature is not limited merely to its preservation; often, when we care for nature, it becomes a source of sustenance for our own lives. In the Sundarbans of West Bengal, some women are setting an inspiring example of this very bond. These women from Jharkhali are creating mangrove forests.

Most of them are women who lost their husbands to tiger attacks. After losing their husbands, they found a means of livelihood within the Sundarbans itself. The mangroves they have planted are now serving as a natural protective shield for their villages, while also providing them with an income. Friends, let us conserve the environment, respect the balance of nature, and safeguard its diversity. Every such effort of ours is a responsibility we owe to future generations.

My dear countrymen,

Millions of young people across the country have recently taken a significant resolve against substance abuse and drugs. They have vowed to stay away from drugs themselves and have also taken up the responsibility of spreading this message to others - all under the 'Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan'. This campaign will run for 100 weeks… it includes volunteers from 'MY Bharat'. Our youth associated with the NSS are part of this; schools, colleges, and universities have joined in; and numerous social and spiritual organizations are also involved. In just the last few days, thousands of pledge ceremonies and awareness programs have taken place across the country. Friends, there is one aspect of this campaign that I particularly appreciate: the ‘Nasha-Mukti Ka Sandesh.’ Our youth are propagating this message in their own language and in their own way.

I had urged young people in ‘Mann Ki Baat’ as well, to join this campaign using their creativity, and I am delighted that thousands of youth have stepped forward in response to this call. Various competitions - such as anthem - slogan writing, and street plays - have been organized on the ‘MY Bharat’ platform. Similarly, young people are sharing creative content on social media using the hashtag ‘#NashaMuktYuva’; in essence, the message, the medium, and the driving energy behind it all come from the youth themselves. In the coming days, activities such as health check-ups and meditation camps will also be conducted as part of this campaign.

Friends,

Several of our festivals are approaching soon. This time amidst the festive celebrations, let us also look around us. If any young person is drifting towards a harmful habit, talk to them. If someone is trying to break free from addiction, support them. Let us all work together to advance the resolve of a drug-free youth and a Viksit Bharat.

My dear countrymen,

I announced a talent hunt campaign for sports from the Red Fort this time. To ensure India continues to perform excellently, it is essential to reach out to villages and towns to discover sporting talent. At the same time, there are many individuals who have dedicated themselves to this very cause. Their sole passion is to discover talent and shape it.

In our Punjab, Rajinder Singh ji is doing exactly this work. Rajinder Singh ji is one such individual who also carries the title ‘Senior’ as part of his name. He was part of the team that won the gold medal in hockey at the 1980 Olympics. He shone at the 1982 World Cup. In 2001, India won the Men’s Junior World Cup title for the first time, whereas in 2003, the country clinched the Senior Asia Cup title. He played the role of the coach in both these tournaments. Now, he is pursuing his passion through the Round Glass Hockey Academy. Thanks to his efforts, new hockey astro-turfs are being laid in villages. Rajinder ji has a very clear focus: identifying children in villages that lack access to excellent coaching facilities. Through such initiatives, many players are securing spots at India's junior and senior levels. No matter how much Rajinder Singh ji’s dedication is lauded, it’s not enough.

My dear countrymen,

Amla, the Indian gooseberry is very familiar to all of us. Pickles and preserves i.e. murabba made from it are used in most households. Many people like Amla juice and Chyawanprash becomes an essential part of our daily routine during winter. Our elders have long spoken about the qualities of Amla across generations. Friends, this very Amla is now becoming a source of new possibilities in Pratapgarh, Uttar Pradesh. The bond between Pratapgarh and Amla is very old; farmers here have been growing it for generations.

Amla has given Pratapgarh a strong identity, and now, this long-standing identity is bringing new opportunities for local farmers and women. The 'One District One Product' (ODOP) has boosted local entrepreneurs involved in the Amla trade there. Today, around 100 units related to Amla processing are operational in Pratapgarh, with women connected with self-help groups playing a significant role. One such group is from Devgarh Kamasi village; women associated with the Savitri Phule Self-Help Group are producing Amla candy, preserves, and juice. Access to new markets through the ODOP scheme has also led to an increase in their income.

Similarly, there is a 'Vindhyavasini Self-Help Group' in a village. The women of this group are producing many such items like Amla pickle and digestive powder. These women received machinery for processing and access to loan facilities. They also got the opportunity to participate in local trade fairs, and in no time, their income saw a significant rise.

Friends,

Every region of our country certainly possesses some such unique specialty - be it a specific fruit, a traditional art form, or a unique skill. The 'One District, One Product' campaign aims to promote these very specialties.

Our endeavour should be to ensure that the identity of our villages and small towns is not confined merely to local markets; these products should reach other parts of the country and even global markets. This also strengthens the 'Vocal for Local' campaign… it inspires the nation to become self-reliant. Even during the upcoming festive season, we must never forget the 'Vocal for Local' mantra.

My dear countrymen,

The month of September is dedicated to the fight against malnutrition. During the Nutrition Month, individuals and organizations from various sectors come together for this noble cause.

Several commendable initiatives have been launched this year to combat malnutrition. Chhattisgarh, for instance, has started the 'Har Ghar Munga - Ghar Ghar Munga' campaign… through this, people are being encouraged to include the nutritious Munga i.e. Moringa in their diet. Gujarat has also launched a 'Vangi Spardha' - a competition featuring dishes made from millets. This initiative promotes affordable and nutritious local cuisine. So far, more than two lakh people have participated in this contest. Maharashtra is also making commendable efforts in this direction; teachers, Anganwadi workers, and parents are joining awareness campaigns there. In Mizoram as well, people have come together this year to launch a campaign for the upkeep of 'Poshan Vatikas'. This aligns with the Mizo tradition of 'Talo-Mad-Yana,' which signifies selfless service and always being at the forefront of helping others.

Such efforts are truly praiseworthy. I am also proud of everyone associated with Anganwadi centres who has been part of such initiatives. These Anganwadi centres are now digitally connected via the 'Poshan Tracker,' with approximately nine crore beneficiaries registered on the platform. This has enabled better care for children, pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers. We must continue this fight against malnutrition with the same spirit; we have to make our society completely free from malnutrition.

Friends,

All of us have celebrated Ganesha Utsav this month with great devotion and enthusiasm. Ganpati Bappa was welcomed across the country with deep reverence. This sacred occasion fills the entire atmosphere with joy and exuberance. Friends, Vighnharta Bhagwan Shri Ganesha symbolizes knowledge, wisdom, and the auspicious beginning of any endeavour. Deep reverence for Him exists not only in India; take the example of Shriman Panthoun Thirkhanon ji - he hails from Thailand. There, Lord Shri Ganesha is worshipped as 'Phra Phikanet.' When he was 19 years old, his father gifted him a photograph of Bhagwan Shri Ganesha. It was then that a profound sense of devotion awakened within him. He has spent over four decades studying traditions associated with Bhagwan Shri Ganesha. He has travelled across several Asian countries, including India and Nepal. He has held a special affection for Maharashtra.

After learning about the Ashtavinayak tradition, he has visited the region numerous times. Through his efforts, the Ashtavinayak yatra has gained popularity among devotees in Thailand as well. In 2002, he established the Ganesha Himal Museum in Chiang Mai, northern Thailand. Today, it houses more than 10,000 idols of Ganesha. The museum also has Ashtavinayak idols for devotees who are unable to travel to India. Worship rituals for Ganesha ji are conducted here every Sunday morning around 10 o'clock. Also, on special occasions connected with Ganesha, celebrations are held. This demonstrates how India's faith, art, and cultural traditions are gaining popularity in other countries as well. I wish that the blessings of Ganpati Bappa remain with everyone always.

Friends,

After every episode of ‘Mann Ki Baat,’ I receive messages from you on myriad topics. Do continue to share such inspiring stories. When you appreciate the initiatives taking place around you, the enthusiasm of those involved grows even further. Learning about these efforts through ‘Mann Ki Baat’ inspires people in other parts of the country as well. May this journey continue to move forward with your support. Celebrate the upcoming festivals with great joy and enthusiasm with your family and friends. I extend my best wishes to all of you once again.

Thank you very much.

Namaskar.

***

MJPS/SS/ST/VK

(Release ID: 2315491)

item.content:encoded:
PIB Backgrounder
Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool
Strengthening India’s Maritime Sovereignty
Posted On: 27 SEP 2026 11:35AM by PIB Delhi

India relies heavily on maritime trade, with most of cargo and energy supplies transported through sea routes. The Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool (BMIP) offers marine insurance to Hull & Machinery risks in respect of vessels that are Indian flagged or are owned, managed or controlled by Indian entities or cargo vessels destined to or starting from India. It was launched in May 2026 with coverage up to ₹13,906.50 crore (USD 1.5 billion). It provides domestic insurance coverage for Hull, Cargo, Protection and Indemnity (P&I), and War risks. BMIP reduces dependence on foreign insurers and ensures affordable, uninterrupted coverage during global disruptions. Policies are issued by domestic insurers, with risks collectively reinsured based on members’ commitments. Claims up to USD 100 million are settled through reserves, while larger claims use sovereign guarantees. Since launch, BMIP has issued War-risk and P&I policies for coastal vessels, reduced premiums, and strengthened India’s maritime sovereignty.

Overview

India stands among the world’s leading trade nations, with the majority of its trade flowing through maritime routes. The sea is not merely a transport medium for India; it is the backbone of commerce. It supports energy security and drives economic growth across diverse sectors of the national economy. From crude oil imports to merchandise exports, maritime connectivity underpins virtually every sector of India’s economy. Coastal shipping and inland waterways further strengthen this lifeline, ensuring resilience and efficiency in trade.

India's maritime trade has expanded, but key marine insurance services remain largely dependent on foreign providers. This leads to an annual outflow of USD 45–60 million in Protection and Indemnity (P&I) premiums, besides higher marine insurance payments abroad.

Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool (BMIP) has been conceived as a sovereign solution to this strategic gap in domestic maritime insurance capacity. Approved on 18 April 2026 and formally launched on 12 May, 2026, the BMIP is India’s first domestic maritime insurance pool of ₹13,906.50 crore (USD 1.5 billion). It assures sovereign backing of ₹12,980 crore (USD 1.4 billion). For the first time, Indian companies are insuring Indian ships independently for higher-value vessels. The coverage spans Hull & Machinery, Cargo against War perils in High-Risk Area and Protection & Indemnity.

India’s Maritime Sector: A Nation of the Seas    

India operates 12 Major and 217 Non‑Major Ports, handling diverse cargo types nationwide. India's major and non-major ports handled 1,668 million metric tonnes of cargo during 2025–26, a figure rising with economic growth and trade expansion.

  • India’s coastline extends around 11,098 kilometres, among the world’s longest, with natural harbours and port sites.
  • Exclusive Economic Zone spans 2.4 million square kilometres, granting sovereign rights over marine resources and fishing activities.
  • Inland waterways exceed 14,500 kilometres, offering rivers, canals, and backwaters for cost‑effective freight movement.
  • Coastal states and territories border the sea, positioning population and industry to benefit from maritime trade.
  • Maritime livelihoods support over 30 million people, including fishers, port workers, seafarers, and shipbuilders.

Why India needs BMI Pool

The Indian-flag fleet has grown to 1,609 ships and 14.33 million GT as of mid-2026, a roughly 36% increase in tonnage since 2015. 95% of India's trade value and 70% of trade volume flows through maritime routes.

  • Maritime Insurance: The Invisible Lifeline

Marine insurance is mandatory for global trade. Hull and machinery policies protect vessels, cargo insurance safeguards goods, and Protection and Indemnity (P&I) covers liabilities like pollution or crew injury. War Risk insurance shields against piracy and conflict. Together, these make insurance a legal and commercial necessity for India’s shipping economy.

  • v Overdependence on Foreign P&I Clubs

The International Group of Protection and Indemnity Clubs is made up of thirteen main clubs. Together, they insure about 90% of the world’s large ships against risks like cargo loss, pollution, collisions, and crew injuries.

 India, has been dependent on foreign insurers for the insurance value chain. Indian shipowners rely almost entirely on 13 international P&I clubs, mostly based in the West. This dependence leaves India vulnerable to sudden coverage withdrawal or politically influenced decisions, underscoring the importance of a homegrown alternative.

  • Geopolitical Volatility and Trade Disruption

Conflicts in the Red Sea and tensions near the Strait of Hormuz have disrupted vital routes. With a major share of crude oil imported by sea, India’s energy security depends on uninterrupted coverage. During this period, foreign insurers increased insurance premiums or stopped providing cover. This increased costs sharply for ship owners, raising the need for a domestic safety net.

  • Absence of Domestic Expertise

Earlier, India did not have institutional depth in marine underwriting and claims management. BMIP builds this expertise indigenously, laying the foundation for a world‑class domestic insurance sector and reducing reliance on foreign hubs like London or Switzerland.

The Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool (BMIP) ensures affordable, sovereign coverage for vessels and cargo, enhancing resilience against global risks.

BMI Pool: Design, Structure and Coverage

The pool provides marine insurance cover to safeguard vessels and cargo on trade routes. It functions through collective insurer participation and structured governance to manage large maritime risks.

  • Sovereign guarantee: Government-backed support of ₹12,980 crore (USD 1.4 billion) ensures financial strength. This guarantee meets obligations even during catastrophic losses.
  • Underwriting capacity: The Pool can insure risks worth ₹ Rs.13,906.5 crore, i.e., USD 1.5 billion, backed up by the Sovereign Guarantee, increasing its ability to cover large maritime losses.
  • Risk coverage: Hull & Machinery, Cargo, Protection & Indemnity (P&I), and War Risk are included.
  • Vessel eligibility: Vessels that are Indian flagged or are owned, managed, or controlled by Indian entities, or cargo vessels destined to or starting from India, qualify.
  • Duration: It has a duration of 10 years, which is extendable up to 15 years.
  • Joint policy issuance: Policies will be issued by domestic insurers that are members of the Pool, using their combined underwriting capacity. The risks covered under these policies will then be reinsured collectively by all Pool members, in proportion to the capacity each has committed.
  • Claims management: Claims up to USD 100 million are met from accumulated reserves and reinsurance recoveries. For larger claims, the sovereign guarantee activates only after complete exhaustion of pool reserves.
  • Administration: General Insurance Corporation of India serves as the Pool Administrator, managing daily operations. It submits performance reports and supports the Pool’s efficient functioning.
  • Governance: A Governing Body oversees and regulates pool operations, ensuring compliance and smooth functioning.
  • Underwriting discipline: An Underwriting Committee ensures sound and consistent risk evaluation, supporting long-term financial sustainability.

  • v Coverage Types and Scope:

BMIP has been designed to provide comprehensive coverage across the full spectrum of maritime risk categories. It ensures that no vessel or cargo involved in Indian trade is left without domestic insurance protection, regardless of the route or nature of the risk.

  • Hull and Machinery War coverage: It protects vessels from damage to hull structure (main body of the ship), propulsion systems (machinery that powers the ship’s movement), and installed equipment. This ensures the capital value of India’s merchant fleet remains secure and domestically insured.
  • Cargo War coverage: It safeguards goods transported across international sea routes against loss or damage to shipments. Indian exporters and importers benefit even in high-risk or conflict-affected maritime corridors.
  • Protection and Indemnity coverage: It addresses liabilities, including pollution, oil pollution clean-up, wreck removal, crew injury, and cargo damage. Indian shipowners gain domestic access to coverage previously available only through foreign clubs.
  • War Perils coverage: It insures against losses from armed conflict, piracy, terrorism, and hostile vessel seizure. This protection is vital for Indian trade routes crossing sensitive corridors like the Red Sea, Strait of Hormuz, etc., besides the other High-Risk Areas.

Outcome & Impact

The launch of Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool in May 2026 marks a significant milestone in India’s maritime insurance sector. Since its operational launch, the BMIP has ensured uninterrupted War-risk insurance for Indian maritime stakeholders. War-risk insurance premiums have fallen by about 35–40% since the peak of the West Asia conflict. As on 7th September 2026, the Pool has issued 3000 Cargo War, 92 Hull War-risk and 3 Protection & Indemnity insurance policies.

  • A Strong Start: What the Launch Delivered
    • India’s First P&I Policy: On 30 July, 2026, India’s first Protection & Indemnity insurance policy under BMIP was issued to Shipping Corporation of India Limited. Issued by New India Assurance Company Limited, it provides financial protection against third-party liabilities.
    • First Hull and Machinery War-risk policy: On 12 May 2026, the pool's very first policy was given for a vessel sailing through conflict zones. New India Assurance issued this Marine Hull and Machinery War Policy to M/s. Hoger Offshore and Marine Private Limited. In simple terms, an Indian ship now sails with home-grown protection against War risks.
    • Cover for goods coming into India: A Marine Cargo War Policy was issued to M/s. Vedanta Sterlite Copper Limited. It protects the company's import of cable wires into India. This shows the pool can serve India's large industrial importers. It keeps the supply chains feeding Indian industry safely insured.
    • Beyond shipping companies: A policy was also issued to Balrampur Chini Mills Limited, a sugar manufacturer. This proves the pool is not for shipowners alone. Farms, factories, and commodity traders moving goods by sea can all seek cover. The pool, therefore, works for the wider Indian economy.
    • Governance and systems in place: The Governing Body and Underwriting Committee have been set up since the launch. General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC Re) has taken charge as the Pool Manager/Administrator. Systems for underwriting, claims, and regulatory compliance are also put in place. The pool is operating at full commercial scale.

Way Forward

The Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool marks a major step in India’s maritime financial independence. Its role is to ensure credible operations, competitive pricing, and reliable claims handling for stakeholders. Medium-term focus remains on strengthening human capital, legal frameworks, and reinsurance partnerships. These efforts enhance resilience while keeping reliance on sovereign backing minimal.

In the long term, the pool emerges as a regional anchor for maritime insurance in the Indian Ocean Region. India gains recognition as a provider of financial services and a shaper of maritime risk norms. As shipbuilding expands and ports handle larger cargo volumes, the pool will grow alongside India's maritime ambitions. Its capacity and coverage stand as a lasting pillar of India’s maritime infrastructure.

item.title: Two-Day National Conference on Rabi Campaign 2026 to Begin Tomorrow in New Delhi
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
item.description: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare Two-Day National Conference on Rabi Campaign 2026 to Begin Tomorrow in New Delhi Conference to Focus on Strengthening Centre–State Coordination and Evolving an Outcome-Oriented Strategy for Agriculture State Agriculture Ministers, senior officials of the Central and State Governments, ICAR and other stakeholders to deliberate on key priorities and preparedness for the forthcoming Rabi season Posted On: 27 SEP 2026 10:19AM by PIB Delhi The Department of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers’…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Two-Day National Conference on Rabi Campaign 2026 to Begin Tomorrow in New Delhi
Conference to Focus on Strengthening Centre–State Coordination and Evolving an Outcome-Oriented Strategy for Agriculture
State Agriculture Ministers, senior officials of the Central and State Governments, ICAR and other stakeholders to deliberate on key priorities and preparedness for the forthcoming Rabi season
Posted On: 27 SEP 2026 10:19AM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, Government of India, will organise the National Conference on Agriculture for Rabi Campaign 2026 on 28–29 September 2026 at the Bharat Ratna C. Subramaniam Auditorium, NASC Complex, Pusa, New Delhi. The Conference will be inaugurated by Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Union Minister of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, and will bring together State Agriculture Ministers, senior officials of the Central and State Governments, ICAR and other stakeholders to deliberate on key priorities and preparedness for the forthcoming Rabi season.

The two-day Conference will focus on strengthening Centre–State coordination and evolving a coordinated, outcome-oriented strategy for enhancing agricultural production, productivity, sustainability and farmers’ incomes. The deliberations will also build upon the key learnings and outcomes of the recently held Zonal Conferences on Agriculture.

The first day will comprise three rounds of parallel thematic group discussions covering three broad areas: Atmanirbharta, Diversification and Production Growth; Sustainability and Climate-Resilient Agriculture; and Digital Agriculture, Infrastructure, Financing and Risk Management. Key issues to be deliberated upon will include the Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses, oilseeds and oil palm, horticulture, cotton, seed availability and reforms in the seed value chain, natural farming, soil health, farm mechanisation, FPO financing and infrastructure, marketing reforms, PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana, Kisan Credit Card coverage, Digital Agriculture, PM Fasal Bima Yojana, plant protection and agricultural statistics.

The thematic discussions are aimed at identifying key implementation challenges, State-specific priorities and actionable strategies for the Rabi season, with particular emphasis on improving convergence among schemes, strengthening delivery mechanisms and ensuring effective outcomes at the field level.

The second day will focus on the key learnings from the Zonal Conferences and outcomes of the thematic discussions held on the first day. The agenda will include the Rabi season weather outlook, fertilizer availability and balanced use of fertilizers, Digital Agriculture Mission, Farmer Registry, Digital Crop Survey and AgriStack, Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses, National Mission on Edible Oils, crop and seed status, varietal adoption, PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana, marketing reforms and preparation of Agriculture Plans through ATMA and KVKs.

The Conference will also provide an opportunity for State Agriculture Ministers to share their views/experiences, state priorities and suggestions for agricultural development and Rabi season preparedness. The inputs from States, along with the outcomes of the thematic deliberations, are expected to contribute towards a coordinated and outcome-oriented strategy for the Rabi Campaign 2026.

The concluding session will focus on summarizing the deliberations and preparing a robust roadmap for enhancing the crop production of Rabi crops and empowering farmers to fulfil the vision of ‘Atmanirbharta & Viksit Bharat’ ensuring food & nutritional security.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah attends 73rd birthday celebrations of Mata Amritanandamayi Ji in Kollam, Keralam, as Chief Guest
Even an insensitive person, upon visiting this place, is filled with a sense of gratitude for the service done by Amma
Amma has made wiping the tears of the suffering her spiritual practice and dharma for five decades; that is why her birthday, too, should be celebrated through acts of service
Amma has bestowed her blessings upon Prime Minister Modi resolve for a drug-free India; with her blessings, the entire nation will become drug-free, and we will certainly achieve this goal
Born in an impoverished village in Kollam, Amma dispelled deprivation, sorrow, and despair from the lives of millions and paved the way for liberation for countless beings
Amma's life has three parts – ‘Bhava’, ‘Karma’ and ‘Karuna’ and her affection, which runs even deeper than that of a mother, stirs the soul
Amma's affection made millions of people realize that they are not alone in their sorrow—that Amma is with them
At the time of the 2001 Gujarat earthquake, Amma built 1,200 houses and established an entire village, which is known today as 'Amma's Village'
The revered Amma transformed her spirit of service into an institutionalized global movement; for her, the 'Seva Diwas' never ends—it continues 365 days a year
If one examines Amma's life closely, it can be divided into three parts: ‘Bhava’, ‘Karma’, and ‘Karuna’
Very few people dedicate their entire lives to selfless service, and Amma has spent her entire life in selfless service
Be it the Gujarat earthquake, the tsunami, the Uttarakhand disaster, the Wayanad landslide, or the challenges posed by COVID—Amma and her followers have set an exemplary standard of service in every instance
Amma has conveyed the message of Hindutva and service on various platforms, such as the United Nations Millennium World Peace Summit and the Parliament of the World's Religions
Posted On: 26 SEP 2026 8:16PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah attended the 73rd birthday celebrations of Mata Amritanandamayi Ji in Kollam, Keralam, today as the Chief Guest.

In his address, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah stated that being in Amma's presence allows one to understand the true meaning of being human—transcending all worldly responsibilities. He said that even an insensitive person, upon visiting this place, is filled with a sense of gratitude for the service done by Amma. We are celebrating Amma's birthday—observed as 'Vishwa Seva Dinam' with all our hearts. The celebrations of one who has made wiping the tears of the suffering her sadhana (spiritual practice) and dharma (duty) for five decades should indeed be in the form of service.

Shri Amit Shah said that while systems sustain society, it is compassion—personified by Amma—that binds it together. It is a luminary like Amma who imparts the wisdom and empathy to understand the sorrows of others to millions of people, not just in India but across the globe. Amma’s embrace has instilled a profound realization in millions worldwide that they are not alone in their suffering; rather, Amma stands with them.

Union Home Minister said that he had the privilege of meeting Amma on September 27, 2015, April 3, 2016, and June 4, 2023. He said that receiving Amma's blessings on 'Vishwa Seva Dinam' is a significant achievement in his life. He first witnessed Amma's compassion during the devastating earthquake in Gujarat in 2001, when she established an entire village by constructing 1,200 beautiful homes. She developed the settlement by providing essential amenities such as a town hall, educational facilities, and a hospital for healthcare services. Today, the village is known as 'Amma's Village'.

Shri Amit Shah said that for Amma, 'Seva Dinam' never ends, as her service continues throughout the year—all 365 days. Amma was born on September 27, 1953, into an impoverished family in the village of Parayakadavu in Kollam district. No one knew then that this child would become the instrument to dispel deprivation, sorrow, and despair from the lives of millions, and pave the way for the liberation of countless beings.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that if one closely examines Amma's life, it can be divided into three facets: Bhav (devotion), Karma (action), and Karuna (compassion). An innate compassion is the defining charm of Amma's personality. Anyone who has received the blessing of Amma's embrace knows that it stirs the soul with an affection even deeper than that of a mother. While everyone engages in selfless service at some point in their lives, very few dedicate their entire existence to it; Amma has spent her whole life in selfless service. Although many possess a spirit of service, few are able to institutionalize that spirit; the revered Amma not only institutionalized her service-oriented nature but also transformed it into a global movement.

Shri Amit Shah said that there are currently 86 Amrita Vidyalayas across the country. Whether it was the Gujarat earthquake, the tsunami, the Uttarakhand disaster, the Wayanad landslide, or the challenges posed by COVID-19, Amma and her followers have set an exemplary standard of service during every crisis. Amma has accomplished significant work—ranging from planting over a million trees and fostering initiatives in health, education, and livelihoods to making 101 villages completely self-reliant. Shri Shah said that Amma has conveyed the message of Hindutva and service on various global platforms, such as the United Nations Millennium World Peace Summit and the Vishwa Dharma Sansad.

Union Home Minister said that when India held the G-20 presidency, Amma presided over Civil-20. Amma has also extended her blessings to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's 'Drug-Free India' campaign; with this blessing, the entire nation will become free from drugs, and we will certainly achieve this goal. Embracing the scriptural mantra of "Sarvajan Hitay, Sarvajan Sukhay," Amma has dedicated her entire life to following that very path.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Finance
item.description: Ministry of Finance CBN conducts anti-drug awareness programme for students under Mission Yuva Raksha for Nasha Mukt Bharat in Jaora, Madhya Pradesh CBN also conducts Jan Sunwayi programmes at Neemuch and Mandsaur for prompt and accessible redressal of grievances of opium cultivators CBN is actively conducting awareness programmes and direct engagements to disrupt illicit drug supply networks, preventing drug abuse and contributing towards a healthier and drug-free society Posted On: 26 SEP 2026 7:16PM by PIB Delhi The Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) conducted a…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
CBN conducts anti-drug awareness programme for students under Mission Yuva Raksha for Nasha Mukt Bharat in Jaora, Madhya Pradesh
CBN also conducts Jan Sunwayi programmes at Neemuch and Mandsaur for prompt and accessible redressal of grievances of opium cultivators
CBN is actively conducting awareness programmes and direct engagements to disrupt illicit drug supply networks, preventing drug abuse and contributing towards a healthier and drug-free society
Posted On: 26 SEP 2026 7:16PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) conducted a series of significant anti-drug awareness programmes to raise awareness against illegal trafficking and possession of narcotic drugs under Mission Yuva Raksha during the past weeks. Alongside enforcement, CBN continued its preventive awareness and stakeholder outreach initiatives towards the vision of a Nasha Mukt Bharat.

Under Mission Yuva Raksha, an awareness programme was organised at G.T. Polytechnic College, Jaora, to sensitise students about the harmful effects of drug abuse, prevention measures and the role of youth in building a drug-free society. Presentations, awareness videos and quiz activities were organised, followed by an anti-drug pledge by the participants.

In follow-up to the MoU between CBN and Brahma Kumaris, an awareness programme was organised at Mandsaur, which was attended by approximately 50 opium cultivators and 40 CBN officers. The participants were sensitised about the harmful effects of drug abuse and their role in making India drug-free. The programme concluded with the Nasha Mukt Bharat anti-drug pledge.

    

Students taking and signing of Nasha Mukt Bharat Pledge at Jaora, Dist- Ratlam, MP

CBN also conducted Jan Sunwayi programmes at Neemuch and Mandsaur for the prompt and accessible redressal of grievances of opium cultivators. More than 450 cultivators participated in the two programmes. Their grievances and queries, including issues relating to name corrections, Namantaran and eligibility for the upcoming Settlement Operation 2026-27, were heard diligently and addressed promptly. Cultivators were also advised to remain vigilant against middlemen/intermediaries and to approach CBN directly for clarification and assistance.


Jan-Sunwayi held at CBN offices of Mandsaur and Neemuch Districts

The Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) remains firmly committed to the vision of “Safe Use and Prevent Abuse of Drugs or Medicines” and “Nasha Mukt Bharat” and continues to engage with cultivators for their grievance redressal and preventive awareness initiatives against the illegal trafficking, diversion and abuse of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances.

The sustained enforcement operations, coupled with awareness programmes and direct engagement with opium cultivators and youth, reflect CBN’s continued commitment to disrupting illicit drug supply networks, preventing drug abuse and contributing towards a healthier and drug-free society.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
CBN Rajasthan Unit seizes nearly four tonnes of contrabands in intensified enforcement operations across Rajasthan
Posted On: 26 SEP 2026 7:13PM by PIB Delhi

In a series of significant anti-drug operations conducted during the past weeks, the Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) has achieved major breakthroughs against illegal trafficking and possession of narcotic drugs. The operations resulted in the seizure of  3,937 kg Poppy Straw (Doda Chura), 9.6 kg Opium and 1.9 kg Hydroponic Cannabis (Ganja), along with ₹18.42 lakh in cash, six vehicles and one country-made pistol loaded with three live rounds. Four persons have been arrested in connection with the cases.

Key seizures at a glance

  • Poppy Straw (Doda Chura): 3,937 kg
  • Opium: 9.6 kg
  • Hydroponic Cannabis (Ganja): 1.9 kg
  • Cash: ₹18,42,000/-
  • Vehicles Seized: 06
  • Country-made Pistol: 01, loaded with 03 live rounds
  • Arrests: 04 persons

The CBN Rajasthan unit intercepted a truck carrying a concealed consignment of 2,292.460 kg Poppy Straw packed in 118 bags. The contraband was found concealed beneath a cover cargo of cement bags. Two persons were arrested and the truck was seized. During follow-up action, a motorcycle and a register were also recovered from the residential premises of one of the arrested persons.

Poppy Straw seized during the operation

In another operation, CBN Rajasthan unit recovered 1,037 kg Doda Chura packed in 56 bags from a premises where a Fortuner car loaded with the contraband was found. A country-made pistol loaded with three live rounds was also recovered from the vehicle.

Pistol with loaded rounds recovered during the operation.

CBN also recovered 340 kg Poppy Straw packed in 23 bags from a Tata Harrier car. In another interception, 156.7 kg Poppy Straw packed in nine bags was recovered from a Honda Amaze car after its occupant abandoned the vehicle and fled from the spot.

Further, 110 kg Poppy Straw was recovered from a Creta car, leading to the arrest of one person.

Intercepted Car with Poppy straw Loaded in it.

In another operation, CBN recovered 9.6 kg Opium along with ₹18.42 lakh in cash from residential premises. One person was arrested in the case.

Seized illicit opium recovered during operation

In another significant action, CBN Rajasthan Unit searched an international parcel received from the USA at the Foreign Post Office, Jaipur. The search resulted in the recovery of 1.9 kg Hydroponic Cannabis (Ganja) concealed in four packets inside an air circulator box.

Hydroponic Cannabis recovered at FPO, Jaipur

All the recovered contraband, vehicles and other articles have been seized under the relevant provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985.

Further intensive investigation is underway in all the cases to identify the sources, destinations, supply channels and other persons/entities associated with the illegal trafficking and distribution of narcotic drugs.

The Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) remains firmly committed to the vision of “Safe Use and Prevent Abuse of Drugs or Medicines” and “Nasha Mukt Bharat” and continues to undertake intelligence-driven enforcement and preventive awareness initiatives against the illegal trafficking, diversion and abuse of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances.

item.title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah launches various initiatives related to women empowerment and cooperation in Kollam, Keralam
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Cooperation
item.description: Ministry of Cooperation Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah launches various initiatives related to women empowerment and cooperation in Kollam, Keralam Empowerment of women through cooperation is one of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s core objectives, because when the woman of a household prospers, the entire family prospers Our objective is to ensure that the benefits of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’ reach the rural and poor women of the country: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah inaugurates ‘Vanitham She-Mart Shops’ and launches the sale…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Cooperation
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah launches various initiatives related to women empowerment and cooperation in Kollam, Keralam
Empowerment of women through cooperation is one of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s core objectives, because when the woman of a household prospers, the entire family prospers
Our objective is to ensure that the benefits of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’ reach the rural and poor women of the country: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation
Shri Amit Shah inaugurates ‘Vanitham She-Mart Shops’ and launches the sale of NCCF’s ‘Janah’ products
It is a matter of immense satisfaction that ‘She-Mart’ is being launched from Keralam, which has more than 23,000 active cooperative societies and a well-organised cooperative movement dating back to the pre-Independence era
She-Mart is an important initiative to directly connect women Self-Help Groups and rural women entrepreneurs with markets and consumers: Shri Amit Shah
Farmers and women entrepreneurs will benefit across the entire value chain — from procurement and processing to branding, packaging and direct access to retail markets
Along with NCCF’s more than 2,500 retail outlets, over 300 ‘She-Marts’ will be opened across Keralam, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, providing farmers and women entrepreneurs the benefit of direct market access
Under Modi Ji’s leadership, women-led development has received sustained impetus; women’s participation in the labour force has risen from 23% in 2014-15 to 40% today
Bank accounts of 36 crore women have been opened, Triple Talaq has been prohibited, more than 11,000 daughters are serving as officers in the Armed Forces, and 3 crore women have become Lakhpati Didis — a number targeted to reach 6 crore by 2029
Keralam has immense potential in the Blue Economy; the Modi Government has introduced numerous schemes to strengthen it through cooperation
Greetings to all Malayali sisters and brothers on the journey from Kerala to Keralam
Posted On: 26 SEP 2026 7:12PM by PIB Delhi

In line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of “Sahkar se Samriddhi”, and as an important step towards strengthening the rural economy through cooperation and giving fresh impetus to women-led development, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today launched various initiatives related to women empowerment and cooperation at the Pavithram Convention Centre in Kollam, Keralam. Union Minister of State for Petroleum and Natural Gas and Tourism Shri Suresh Gopi, along with several dignitaries and representatives associated with the cooperative sector, was present on the occasion.

At the outset of his address, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah congratulated and extended his best wishes to all Malayali brothers and sisters on the journey from Kerala to ‘Keralam’. He said that during the Amrit Kaal of Independence, farmers and people associated with the cooperative sector had long demanded the creation of a separate Ministry of Cooperation at the Centre. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi took a major step towards the country’s rural development, agricultural development and women empowerment by establishing the Ministry of Cooperation at the Centre, infusing new energy and momentum into the cooperative sector.

Highlighting Keralam’s rich cooperative legacy, Shri Amit Shah said that Keralam is among those states where the cooperative movement has remained strong and well-organised since even before Independence. Regions such as Travancore, Kochi and Malabar have had a strong tradition of cooperation since the pre-Independence era, making Keralam’s cooperative movement an important example for the entire country. He said that the ‘She-Mart’ initiative being launched today in the cooperative sector was announced by the Union Finance Minister in the Budget, and it is a matter of great satisfaction that the initiative is being launched from Keralam.

Elaborating on the initiatives launched to make affordable food products available to the people and farmers, the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that an initiative has also been launched in Keralam to make onions, Bharat Atta and Bharat Rice available to farmers and the general public through NAFED’s mobile vans. He said that under the Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses, urad and gram seeds are being provided to women farmers. Similarly, under the NAFED-Kalyan Scholarship Scheme, scholarships are being provided to girl children from nearly 2,000 families.

Underscoring the significance of ‘She-Mart’ for women Self-Help Groups and rural women entrepreneurs, Shri Amit Shah said that the most important aspect of today’s programme is the launch of ‘She-Mart’. The concept of She-Mart is an important initiative aimed at directly connecting women Self-Help Groups and rural women entrepreneurs with markets and consumers. He said that institutions such as NAFED, Kendriya Bhandar and Amul will also help women-led enterprises expand on a much larger scale.

Referring to the expansion of ‘She-Mart’ and the new opportunities it will create for farmers and women entrepreneurs, the Union Minister of Cooperation said that there are plans to establish more than 300 She-Mart stores across Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, where local products, along with Bharat Brand products, will be made available to consumers. He said that farmers and women entrepreneurs will benefit at every stage of the value chain — from procurement, processing, branding and packaging to direct access to the retail market.

Appreciating Keralam’s robust cooperative ecosystem, Shri Amit Shah said that the state has a very old, extensive and strong cooperative structure, with more than 23,000 cooperative institutions functioning effectively. Inviting Keralam’s Minister of Cooperation to visit Delhi, he said that the Union Government would be happy to ensure that Keralam receives the maximum possible benefit from all Government of India schemes. He added that the Union Government can also extend the necessary support to Keralam in organic agriculture and other related sectors.

Highlighting the central role of women empowerment in Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’, the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that empowering women through cooperation is one of the Prime Minister’s key objectives and forms an important foundation of his larger vision and core goals. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has consistently guided that when the woman of a household prospers, the entire family prospers. When a woman in the household is empowered, its impact is reflected in the empowerment of the entire family. Therefore, the Government’s objective is to ensure that the greatest benefits of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’ reach the rural and poor women of the country.

Referring to the role of NAFED and NCCF in strengthening cooperation at the national level, Shri Amit Shah said that both NAFED and NCCF are important institutions operating across the country. At present, around 8 lakh farmers are associated with NAFED and nearly 6 lakh women farmers are associated with NCCF. He said that efforts will be made in the coming days to further increase these numbers and strengthen both institutions.

Highlighting the steps taken in recent years towards women empowerment and the outcomes achieved, the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that several important initiatives have been undertaken under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to promote Nari Shakti and women empowerment. Women’s labour force participation, which stood at around 23 percent in 2017-18, has now increased to approximately 40 percent. He said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, bank accounts of nearly 36 crore women have been opened.

Referring to the measures taken by the Union Government to expand women’s rights, dignity and opportunities, Shri Amit Shah said that the important decision to prohibit Triple Talaq was taken to protect the rights of Muslim women. Earlier, there were restrictions on Muslim women undertaking Haj without a male companion, but now Muslim women can perform Haj independently. He said that today more than 11,000 women officers are serving in the Indian Armed Forces, while the Union Government has also made provision for 26 weeks of maternity leave for women.

Referring to the goal of further expanding women’s economic empowerment, the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that the target of creating nearly 3 crore ‘Lakhpati Didis’ was achieved before 2024, and the target now is to make 6 crore women Lakhpati Didis by 2029.

Highlighting the vast economic potential inherent in Keralam’s Blue Economy, Shri Amit Shah said that the state’s long coastline, backwaters, rivers and rich maritime tradition provide it with immense opportunities in the Blue Economy. Numerous schemes are available in the fisheries sector, ranging from providing large trawlers to production, processing, packaging, branding and exports. He urged Keralam’s Minister of Cooperation to take the initiative in this direction, obtain details of these schemes and ensure that Keralam derives the maximum possible benefit from them. Emphasising the need for joint efforts by the Centre and the State to transform the potential of the fisheries and marine sectors into a major economic opportunity, the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that Keralam has enormous potential in these sectors and, if the Centre and the State work together to take these opportunities forward, the fisheries and marine sectors can be transformed into a major economic opportunity.

During the programme, the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation flagged off the NCCF and NAFED mobile vans providing onions at a subsidised price of Rs 35 per kg and inspected various stalls. On the occasion, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was exchanged between NCCF and The Central Financial Credit and Investment Co-operative (India) Limited (CFCICI). MoUs were also exchanged for supply-chain logistics integration of fisheries products of the Bharatiya Matsya Pravartak Sangham with NCCF’s ‘Janah’ brand, and between NCCF and Bharat Lajhna Sahakari Samiti for opening 300 She-Mart shops across Keralam, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.

Shri Amit Shah also launched the sale of NCCF’s ‘Janah’ products and remotely inaugurated the ‘Vanitham She-Mart Shops’, developed through collaboration between NCCF and CFCICI. He also launched the sale of ‘Bharat Atta’ and ‘Bharat Rice’ to women customers through the Vanitham She-Mart Shops. In addition, free urad and gram seed kits were distributed to women farmers under the Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses, while scholarship cheques were presented to daughters of registered farmers under the NAFED-Kalyan Scholarship Scheme.

****

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
ICAR Institutes Promote Cleanliness and Sustainable Waste Management
Posted On: 26 SEP 2026 7:00PM by PIB Delhi

As part of the Swachhata Hi Seva activities, the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) organised awareness and cleanliness initiatives focused on post-Ganesh Visarjan cleanliness, clean public spaces and responsible waste management at ICAR institutions. The initiatives aimed to promote environmental protection, safe practices and community participation in maintaining clean surroundings after Ganesh Visarjan.

An awareness programme on post-Ganesh Visarjan cleanliness was organised at a local Ganesh pandal, where participants were sensitised about the use of eco-friendly clay idols and advised to avoid immersion of Plaster of Paris idols and idols containing harmful chemical colours in drinking water tanks. Participants were encouraged to use designated immersion sites and avoid immersing idols and Puja Samagri in natural water bodies. Emphasis was also laid on proper collection and disposal of flowers, Puja Samagri, plastic, thermocol and other decorative waste.

The programme also highlighted the importance of maintaining cleanliness at immersion sites, preventing littering and following safety precautions near water bodies. The areas surrounding the local Ganesh pandal were cleaned, with garbage collected and segregated to facilitate safe and responsible waste management. The initiative highlighted the importance of collective responsibility and community participation in protecting water resources and maintaining clean public spaces.

As part of the activities, biodegradable offerings including flowers and other Puja Samagri were collected and segregated at ICAR-NISA, Ranchi, Jharkhand, and ICAR-CIRCOT, Mumbai, Maharashtra. The compostable material was processed at composting facilities for preparation of organic manure. The initiative resulted in the cleaning and segregation of biodegradable waste generated during Ganesh Visarjan and its conversion into a useful resource through composting.

The activities contributed to promoting awareness on cleanliness, sanitation, environmental protection and responsible waste management, while encouraging the adoption of clean, safe and environmentally responsible practices during and after Ganesh Visarjan.

item.category: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
