Patil Calls for Collective Action to Strengthen Climate-Resilient and Sustainable Water Management at IIWW 2026 IIWW 2026 Brings Together Global Water Community to Advance Innovation, Knowledge and Sustainable WASH Solutions India International WASH Conference Highlights Community-Led Approaches, Digital Innovation and Stronger Institutions for Sustainable Water Services Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 7:54PM by PIB…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
9th India International Water Week 2026 Concludes with Focus on Climate-Resilient Water Management and Sustainable Water Services
Shri C. R. Patil Calls for Collective Action to Strengthen Climate-Resilient and Sustainable Water Management at IIWW 2026
IIWW 2026 Brings Together Global Water Community to Advance Innovation, Knowledge and Sustainable WASH Solutions
India International WASH Conference Highlights Community-Led Approaches, Digital Innovation and Stronger Institutions for Sustainable Water Services
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 7:54PM by PIB Delhi

The 9th India International Water Week (IIWW) 2026 concluded today at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, with the Valedictory Ceremony chaired by Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C R Patil. Held from September 22–25 under the theme “Climate Resilient Water Management”, the deliberations brought together policymakers, government officials, international organisations, development partners, researchers, academia, industry, water-sector practitioners, innovators and young professionals to discuss emerging challenges and solutions for water security.

The valedictory session was graced by Ministers of State for Jal Shakti; Shri V. Somanna, Shri Raj Bhushan Choudhary, Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Shri Ashok K. K. Meena, Secretary, Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, Smt. Archana Varma, Director General, National Mission for Clean Ganga, Shri Rajeev Kumar Mital, AS & MD, NJJM, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Chairman, Central Water Commission, Shri Anupam Prasad, and Director General, National Water Development Agency, Shri Baleshwar Thakur.

Addressing the gathering, Shri C. R. Patil, Union Minister of Jal Shakti underscored that IIWW 2026 provided a platform for governments, experts, institutions, academia, industry and youth to deliberate on climate-resilient water management. He highlighted three key takeaways: people’s participation in water conservation, taking science and technology to the ground, and strengthening international and institutional cooperation. Highlighting the Jal Jeevan Mission’s impact since its launch in 2019, he said expanded access to household tap water has contributed to improved health, dignity and quality of life in rural communities, while reducing the time and effort spent by women in fetching water. Referring to a WHO assessment, he said that improved access to safe drinking water under the Mission has the potential to prevent a significant number of deaths among children and reduce the health burden associated with unsafe water. He stressed that the next phase of JJM must focus on ensuring adequate, regular, safe and sustainable drinking water services, with community participation, source sustainability and appropriate technology central to sustaining these gains.

Speaking at the Valedictory Ceremony, Shri V. Somanna, Minister of State, Ministry of Jal Shakti, said that water security fundamentally means ensuring a better quality of life through safe and reliable drinking water, sanitation, clean surroundings and effective wastewater management. Highlighting the transformation brought about by the Jal Jeevan Mission under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, he said the focus must now be on ensuring that drinking water services are safe, adequate, regular and sustainable. He underlined that drinking water, and sanitation must be addressed through an integrated approach, with safe management of greywater, wastewater and solid waste essential for protecting water sources and public health. He highlighted the progress under Swachh Bharat Mission-Grameen, including ODF Plus and solid and liquid waste management, as an important foundation for this approach. He said the learnings from deliberations during the India International Water Week would translate into practical action towards sustainable, people-centric water services and the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

Speaking at the event, Minister of State for Jal Shakti, Shri Raj Bhushan Choudhary, highlighted India’s efforts towards climate resilient water resources management through irrigation development, modernisation of command areas, dam rehabilitation, groundwater management and recharge, river rejuvenation, river interlinking, flood management, hydrological forecasting, reservoir management and improved water information systems. He stressed timely completion and effective utilisation of water resources projects and emphasised that investments must ultimately translate into measurable outcomes for people, agriculture, the economy and ecosystems.

Addressing the Valedictory Session, Shri Ashok K. K. Meena, Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS) emphasised that climate resilience begins with water resilience. He highlighted the hydrological cycle as a global common good and described it as nature’s most successful water management system. He stressed the collective responsibility to maintain this cycle and manage water in harmony with nature, with a focus on conserving, reusing and replenishing every drop of water to strengthen community resilience in the face of a changing climate. He further underscored that the long-term success of water programmes would depend on translating the knowledge and solutions discussed at IIWW into implementation and measurable outcomes on the ground.

 

The Brief Report and Important Recommendations of IIWW 2026 were presented by Shri Rajeev Kumar Mital, Director General, National Mission for Clean Ganga. The Water Week witnessed 7,224 delegates, 227 exhibitors and 119 paper presentations, with participation of two Partner Countries and 14 Partner States and Union Territories. The recommendations emerging from the seven thematic areas called for stronger and more participatory water governance, safe reuse of treated wastewater, deeper international cooperation, data driven governance, community led groundwater recharge, wider use of digital and emerging technologies, strengthened multi hazard early warning systems and river basin scale approaches for climate adaptation. He also emphasised innovative financing and enabling frameworks for public private partnerships, improved water use efficiency, sustainable sediment management, preservation of reservoir storage, scientific aquifer mapping, environmental flows and community led ecosystem-based water management.

 

An important component of IIWW 2026 was the 2nd India International WASH Conference 2026, organised by DDWS in collaboration with the Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee National Institute of Water and Sanitation (SPM-NIWAS), Kolkata.

During the Valedictory Session, Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, NJJM, highlighted the outcomes of the Second WASH Conference, which brought together academic, research and field perspectives on water, sanitation and hygiene. He noted that 57 research papers were presented during the course of 4 days at the event, with additional papers presented at the SPM-NIWAS. He said the deliberations highlighted priorities including source sustainability, operation and maintenance, water quality, climate resilience, digital technologies, sustainable sanitation and zero-waste management. He emphasised that sustainable WASH outcomes require active community participation, alongside technical and institutional interventions, and highlighted the India–Africa Round Table as an important platform for knowledge exchange and continued cooperation.

The India-Africa Roundtable on WASH, organised by DDWS, witnessed participation from Ambassadors, High Commissioners and senior diplomatic representatives from 22 African countries, alongside development partners and WASH-sector stakeholders. The Roundtable explored opportunities for cooperation in capacity building, water-quality surveillance, digital platforms, community-led approaches, climate-resilient infrastructure and exchange of implementation experiences.

The participation of young technical professionals was another feature of the Conference. In partnership with the All-India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), more than 50 engineering students participated in the WASH Conference, providing an opportunity to connect emerging technical talent with real-world challenges in water and sanitation.

A key highlight of the Valedictory Function was the release of eight Capacity Building Modules developed under the Jal Jeevan Mission for Gram Panchayat representatives, Village Water and Sanitation Committee (VWSC) members and Sujalam Shakti Group members. The modules were released by Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C. R. Patil.

The modules use relatable village situations to explain key aspects of rural drinking water service delivery: institutional roles and responsibilities, source sustainability and water quality, operation and maintenance, technology, community participation and climate resilience. The modules are aimed at strengthening the capacity of local institutions and community stakeholders to manage water services and sustain infrastructure over the long term.

The release of the modules comes as the Jal Jeevan Mission moves towards a greater emphasis on assured, reliable and sustainable service delivery, building on the significant expansion of rural drinking water infrastructure across the country.

The Valedictory Session reiterated the importance of collaboration across governments, communities, scientific institutions, development partners and the private sector in addressing India's evolving water challenges. The deliberations of IIWW 2026 reinforced the need for evidence-based planning, technological innovation, institutional strengthening, climate-resilient infrastructure and community participation to advance India's water-security goals.

The 9th India International Water Week concluded with a shared commitment to carry forward the knowledge, partnerships and solutions emerging from the four-day platform and strengthen collective efforts towards water security, sustainable services and climate-resilient communities.

During the Valedictory Ceremony, several important publications, reports, protocols and capacity building modules were released. These included two books by NERIWALM on emerging trends and advances in sustainable and efficient irrigation, the Protocol for Riverine Macroplastics Monitoring by the National Mission for Clean Ganga, capacity building modules under Jal Jeevan Mission, the Reports on the 1st Census of Major and Medium Irrigation Projects, 7th Minor Irrigation Census, 2nd Census of Water Bodies and 1st Census of Springs. The Irrigation Atlas developed by the Central Water Commission was also e-launched. Awards under various categories of the IIWW 2026 exhibition were also presented.

 

Earlier in the day 3 sessions were held as part of IIWW 2026 with focus on Digital Transformation, Innovation and Stronger Water Governance. At the centre of these conversations were three sessions convened by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS): “Digital Public Infrastructure in the Water Sector,” “Water Quality and Cost-Effective Technology,” and “Rural Water Supply Governance and Implementation Framework.” Together, the sessions brought diverse perspectives on digital public infrastructure, water-quality management, emerging technologies, research, governance and practical solutions for strengthening rural water services.

The session on “Digital Public Infrastructure in the Water Sector” brought together senior government, international and technology experts to explore how interoperable data, AI, geospatial technologies and citizen-centric platforms can transform water governance and service delivery. Chaired by Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, NJJM, and co-chaired by Mr. William Rex, World Bank, the session highlighted the vision of “Water as One Data”, with Sujalam Bharat positioned as the digital public infrastructure for rural drinking water. Discussions covered trusted and authenticated datasets, geospatial asset mapping, citizen feedback, Jal Seva Analytics, the Rural Data Stack and the evolution of sectoral DPI from foundational platforms such as Aadhaar, DigiLocker and UPI to applications supporting leakage detection, predictive maintenance and asset management.

 

In his opening remarks, Shri Kamal Kishore Soan highlighted that Digital Public Infrastructure is increasingly being recognised as an important foundation for delivering public services at scale. Drawing on India's experience with Aadhaar and UPI, he noted that common digital platforms can connect systems, support innovation and facilitate delivery of services to millions of citizens. He observed that the water sector presents a distinctive challenge as water services are closely linked with sources, infrastructure, institutions, geography and communities. With the Jal Jeevan Mission increasingly focusing on sustainable water services, improved governance and informed decision-making, the ability to connect and use data across these dimensions assumes greater significance.

Highlighting the broader vision of “Water as One Data”, Shri Soan stated that integrated data can strengthen planning, management and service delivery. Within this vision, Sujalam Bharat has been developed as the digital public infrastructure for rural drinking water. He emphasised that its significance lies not merely in digitising existing processes but in creating a common digital foundation on which future applications, analytical systems and decision-support capabilities can be developed. He stressed that the real value of DPI would not be determined by the volume of data generated, but by its ability to enable institutions to take better decisions and ultimately improve outcomes for citizens.

Speaking on the role of DPI in transforming the drinking water sector, Ms. Swati Meena Nayak highlighted the need to move beyond fragmented datasets and create an integrated, trusted and interoperable digital ecosystem. She noted that the drinking water sector already generates millions of data points through IoT devices, SCADA systems, field-level reporting and other digital platforms. The challenge is to ensure that these datasets are interoperable, authenticated, consistent and capable of supporting governance and policy decisions.

 

The session also explored how digital infrastructure can enable more responsive, proactive and citizen-centric water services. Ms. Sunita Jain highlighted Meri Panchayat for accessing water-service information and reporting issues through geo-tagged evidence, while Mr. Jean Martin shared Singapore's experience of advancing from SCADA and automation to GIS, smart metering, AI and digital twins. The session concluded with a demonstration of Google's Global Flood Hub, showcasing AI-enabled riverine and urban flash-flood forecasting. The discussions underscored that the value of DPI lies not merely in generating data, but in connecting trusted information across systems and translating it into better decisions, proactive management and improved services for citizens.

The second DDWS session, Water Quality and Cost-Effective Technology, brought together researchers and practitioners exploring innovations across water quality, ecological restoration, climate adaptation, groundwater assessment and water-sector instrumentation. Mr. Abhilash Tiwari presented a microalgae-based phytoremediation pilot that reported improvements in DO, BOD, COD, pH, biodiversity and odour, alongside carbon sequestration and lower operating costs. Mr. Suresh Sharma presented research on extensive green roofs, demonstrating increased rainfall retention and reduced peak runoff across different soil, biochar and manure configurations. The session also highlighted microplastics as an emerging water-quality concern, with Mr. Srinivas Bilakanti calling for stronger sampling, analytical and monitoring protocols.

Mr. Birendra Pratap presented borehole geophysical electrical logging as a cost-effective approach to assess basic groundwater-quality parameters such as EC, TDS and chloride where conventional sampling may be difficult. Dr. Muhammed Faisal Rahman highlighted the role of IP testing at CWPRS, Pune, in validating water-resource instrumentation exposed to environmental stresses. The discussion underscored how scientific innovation, appropriate monitoring and robust instrumentation can strengthen water-quality assessment, improve reliability of water-sector systems and support more sustainable resource management.

The session on “Rural Water Supply Governance and Implementation Framework” examined the shift under Jal Jeevan Mission from rapid infrastructure creation to reliable, sustainable and accountable water-service delivery.

Addressing the participants, Shri Ashok K. K. Meena, Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), emphasised that with the substantial expansion of rural drinking water infrastructure under Jal Jeevan Mission, the focus is now shifting from asset creation to assured, reliable and sustainable service delivery. He highlighted the need to strengthen Gram Panchayats as local water-service institutions, supported by suitable service providers and robust O&M arrangements, so that rural households consistently receive safe and adequate drinking water. Underscoring the importance of community-led service assessment, he noted that initiatives such as Jal Seva Ankalan are enabling Gram Panchayats to evaluate service levels, identify gaps and prepare improvement plans through participatory processes. He further stressed the need to professionalise rural water services, strengthen source sustainability and climate resilience measures, leverage digital platforms for monitoring and accountability, and promote continuous capacity building and knowledge sharing. He stated that the ultimate success of JJM should increasingly be measured by the quality, reliability and sustainability of drinking water services and the ability of local institutions and communities to manage and improve them over time.

Speakers highlighted the central role of Gram Panchayats and Pani Samitis in operation and maintenance, supported by clear institutional responsibilities, financing mechanisms, service providers and capacity building. Discussions highlighted groundwater sustainability and source protection, climate-resilient planning, seasonal demand and the need for locally appropriate supply models. Madhya Pradesh's 2026 O&M rules were presented as an example of clarifying Gram Panchayat responsibilities, financial powers and institutional structures, while experiences from Gujarat and Bihar demonstrated the importance of community ownership, transparent tariff systems, professionalised services and digital tools for sustaining schemes.

The session also emphasised continuous learning, data-driven governance and community-led assessment as critical to long-term service outcomes. Initiatives such as eGram Seva, Avani and digital dashboards were highlighted for improving transaction visibility and enabling near real-time decision-making, while ECHO India's learning model demonstrated how practical, continuous and locally contextualised capacity building can strengthen problem-solving at the grassroots. The discussion on Jal Seva Ankalan further highlighted the transition towards Gram Panchayats assessing and validating their own service levels, identifying gaps and developing improvement plans. Overall, the session underscored that the next phase of JJM will be defined not by the number of assets created, but by the reliability, quality and sustainability of services, strengthened local institutions and the ability of communities to continuously assess and improve their water systems.

The 9th India International Water Week (IIWW) 2026 concluded with a strong focus on the technologies, innovations and governance approaches that can shape the future of water management.

“Ek ped maa k naam” Campaign Held at AQCS Campus under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026

Singh Baghel, Hon’ble MoS, DAHD, organized “एक पेड़ मां के नाम” campaign under the Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, at Animal Quarantine and Certification Services (AQCS) campus, New Delhi on 25.09.2026.

During the campaign, Hon’ble MoS stated that “एक पेड़ मां के नाम” campaign, launched by our respected Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, this campaign connects nature's nourishment with our mothers' affection. When we plant a tree in our mother's name, we don't just plant a tree, we plant life for the future. Hon’ble MoS also emphasized that these plants shall be taken care like our own child, so that in the future, that tree can care for us like our mother.

The cleanliness drive was also carried out in the AQCS Campus under the leadership of Hon’ble MoS with a motive to adopt the cleanliness in our lifestyle.

This year, the theme of SHS 2026 is "Participation in Cleanliness; Clean India, Developed India." Our goal is clear—the promise of a developed India cannot be achieved without public participation.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Department of Social Justice and Empowerment Organises Swachhata se Sabhyata Session
Session Held in Collaboration with Brahma Kumaris under Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026
Focus on Cleanliness, Inner Values and Jan Bhagidari
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 7:39PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment , Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, organised a special awareness session titled Swachhata se Sabhyata in collaboration with the Brahma Kumaris at the Ministry’s Manan Conference Room, in the National Capital here today.

The session was held as part of the Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026, being observed across the country from September 17 to October 2 with a focus on Jan Bhagidari.

Addressing officers and staff, Sister Vidarthi of the Brahma Kumaris spoke about the connection between inner values and the cleanliness of one’s surroundings.

Citing the principle Jaisi Awastha, Waisi Vyavastha, she explained that a person’s state of mind shapes the order they create around them, whether at home, in the workplace or in the wider community.

 

Referring to the maxim Cleanliness is next to Godliness, Sister Vidarthi encouraged participants to regard cleanliness as a practice rooted in self-respect and inner purity, alongside their civic responsibilities.

She emphasised respect for nature, social sensitivity and simple living, and observed that lasting physical cleanliness is supported by cleanliness in thought, speech and conduct.

Sister Vidarthi also highlighted recycling as a practical habit that promotes responsible use of resources and contributes to better waste management.

At the conclusion of the session, officers and staff of the Department reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining cleanliness in their workplaces and communities throughout the year.

The occasion was graced by, Hon’ble Union Cabinet Minister of Heavy Industry and Steel Shri H. D. Kumarswamy, Hon’ble…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Heavy Industries
ICAT Marks 20 Years of Excellence with PM e‑Drive Dialogue with the industry and Launch of Agri Machinery Test Facility 
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 7:36PM by PIB Delhi

The International Centre for Automotive Technology (ICAT), Manesar, celebrated a landmark milestone today 20 years of service to India’s automotive industry, with a high‑profile event attended by senior dignitaries, industry leaders, and media representatives. 

The occasion was graced by, Hon’ble Union Cabinet Minister of Heavy Industry and Steel Shri H. D. Kumarswamy, Hon’ble Minister of State for Heavy Industry and Steel Shri Bhupathi Raju Srinivasa Varma, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Heavy Industries, Dr. Hanif Qureshi, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Heavy Industries Shri Prem Chandra Maurya, Senior officials from MHI, MoRTH, MoA&FW, MEITY, MoP, MNRE, CAQM, BEE, and along with BIS  past Presidents of SIAM and ACMA, along with senior industry delegates and media representatives.
 

The event featured an industry dialogue on the PM e‑Drive scheme, a flagship initiative envisioned under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to accelerate India’s transition towards clean, sustainable, and self‑reliant mobility. 

A major highlight was the inauguration of ICAT’s indigenous Agri Machinery Test Facility, a first‑of‑its‑kind initiative aimed at supporting farmers by ensuring reliable, certified equipment for agricultural modernization. This expansion marks ICAT’s evolution into a multi‑sectoral testing and certification hub, bridging automotive and agricultural technologies.  

Director ICAT Shri Saurabh Dalela in his opening remarks mentioned  that over the past two decades, ICAT has emerged as a pillar of India’s automotive ecosystem, contributing to innovation, safety, and sustainability.

 

The celebration also acknowledged the invaluable contributions of the Ministry of Heavy Industries, Ministry of Transport, nodal ministries, CMVR test agencies, ICAT’s suppliers, collaborators, partners, consultants, past CEOs of NATRiP/NAB, former Directors of ICAT, and the dedicated colleagues of ICAT who have collectively enabled this achievement. 

 

 

The celebration also acknowledged the invaluable contributions of the Ministry of Heavy Industries, Ministry of Transport, nodal ministries, CMVR test agencies, ICAT’s suppliers, collaborators, partners, consultants, past CEOs of NATRiP/NAB, former Directors of ICAT, and the dedicated colleagues of ICAT who have collectively enabled this achievement.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
ICG to strengthen maritime cooperation through QUAD‑at‑Sea Ship Observer Mission
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 7:22PM by PIB Delhi

As part of the QUAD‑at‑Sea Ship Observer Mission, Indian Coast Guard (ICG) Ship Shaunak sailed from Chennai on September 25, 2026 for Perth, Australia. This marks an important step in advancing maritime cooperation and interoperability among QUAD nations - India, Australia, Japan, and the United States.

Six Sea Riders - two officers each from India and Japan, and one officer each from Australia and the United States - embarked onboard Shaunak to participate in shipboard activities and professional exchanges designed to enhance interoperability, strengthen coordination, and build mutual trust.

The initiative, aligned with the Quad Foreign Ministers’ Joint Statement of  May 26 2026, reflects the shared commitment of the QUAD countries to uphold a free, open, inclusive and rules‑based maritime order in the Indo‑Pacific.

This mission underscores India’s maritime vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions), and ICG’s dedication to collective engagement, professional linkages, and a secure maritime environment across the Indo‑Pacific.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Waste Picking to Greater Financial Security Ms. Komaragiri Ankamma’s Journey
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 6:59PM by PIB Delhi

For 25 years, Ms Komaragiri Ankamma has worked as a waste picker in Guntur, earning a modest income while supporting her family.

Assistance under the Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY) has helped her improve her livelihood and build greater financial security.

Ms. Ankamma, 45, is a member of the Scheduled Tribe community. She began accompanying her parents in waste-picking work as a child because her family could not afford her education. Limited income, difficult living conditions and social exclusion made it hard for her family to meet household needs or save for emergencies.

Working six days a week, Ms. Ankamma earned approximately Rs. 150–200 a day from waste picking. She hoped to improve her family’s living conditions and establish a more dependable source of income.

On 19 June 2023, Ms. Ankamma received support through Navajeevan Organisation as part of a five-member group project under SUY. The project cost Rs. 49,96,925, comprising a loan of Rs. 31,22,695 and an upfront capital subsidy of Rs. 18,74,230. The support helped her pursue improved livelihood opportunities.

Ms Ankamma while expressing her contentment for the support she received through the Scheme said, “Additional monthly income of approximately Rs 10, 000 has helped me strengthen family’s financial security.”

The case record reports an additional income of approximately Rs. 10,000 per month following the assistance. Using its before-and-after income figures, her monthly earnings increased from approximately Rs. 8,000 to Rs. 18,000. She can now meet household expenses more comfortably and set aside money for future needs.

For Ms. Ankamma and her family, the increase in income has brought greater stability and confidence. Her journey shows how financial support for waste pickers can help strengthen livelihoods and improve everyday living conditions.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
40th Webinar of the National Good Governance Webinar Series held on the theme ‘Sustainability and Replication of the Awarded Initiatives under PMA’ 
Presentations made on Project PATHA initiative of Mehsana District by Shri M. Nagarajan, State Project Director, Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan, Government of Gujarat, its Sustainability by Shri S. K Prajapati,  Collector & District Magistrate, Mehsana District and its expansion & replication by Dr. Sharad K Trivedi, District Primary Education Officer, Education Department, to national audience.
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 6:47PM by PIB Delhi

The 40th National Good Governance Webinar was held on 25th September 2026 in which the initiative of Project PATHA, awarded the PM’s Award for Excellence in Public Administration, 2022, was presented under the theme ‘Sustainability and Replication of the Initiatives Awarded under PMA’.

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi had directed Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DARPG), in April 2022, to hold virtual conferences/ webinars with District Collectors and other officers in which past award winners of PM’s Awards (PMA) for Excellence in Public Administration be invited to present their experiences with the objective of greater dissemination and replication.

Since then, 39 webinars have been held so far. Each webinar is attended by about 1000 officials from Line Departments, State Governments, District Collectors, State Administrative Training Institutes and Central Training Institutes.

Today’s presentations included:

(i)The awarded initiative presented by Shri M. Nagarajan, State Project Director, Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan, Gujarat:

Shri M. Nagarajan presented Project PATHA, an initiative for Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN) implemented across all 994 elementary schools of Mehsana district. The FLN Task Force developed teacher guides, an assessment ladder, and Gujarati and Mathematics worksheets based on identified learning gaps. The material was subsequently reviewed by GCERT and made available through the DIKSHA platform.

(ii)Sustainability aspects of the initiative presented by Shri S. K. Prajapati,     Collector & District Magistrate, Mehsana:

Shri S. K. Prajapati highlighted the institutionalisation of the PATHA approach beyond the award period through regular orientation, monitoring, review and handholding of teachers and education functionaries. He also highlighted the evolution of the initiative from FLN to Grade-Appropriate Learning (GAL), with continued use of learning material, school-level data analysis and integration with subsequent educational initiatives.

 

(iii) Implementation of the key aspects and further scaling up of the initiative by Dr. Sharad K. Trivedi, District Primary Education Officer, Education Department, Mehsana:

Dr. Sharad K. Trivedi highlighted the expansion of the PATHA model through training and handholding of other districts and dissemination of its FLN Teacher Guide, worksheets and instructional videos through GCERT and DIKSHA. The Mehsana model and its learning material have subsequently been taken up at the State level under Nipun Gujarat, including the state-level Tracker, ‘Kadam’ and ‘Pagla’ learning resources.

The Webinar was chaired by Shri Puneet Yadav, Additional Secretary, DARPG and was attended by senior officers of the Department. The Webinar was attended from more than 900 locations across India with Senior Officials of Administrative Reforms Departments of States/UTs, District Collectors, State and District field officers, and Officers of Central and State Administrative Training Institutes.

The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, has appointed him for a tenure of three years…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Shri Narayan Dewasi Assumes Charge as Member of DWBDNC Governing Body
Reaffirms Commitment To The Welfare And Development Of De-Notified, Nomadic And Semi-Nomadic Communities
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 6:45PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Narayan Dewasi assumed charge today as a Member of the Governing Body of the Development and Welfare Board for De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Communities (DWBDNC).

The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, has appointed him for a tenure of three years from the date of joining or until further orders, whichever is earlier.

On assuming charge, Shri Dewasi expressed gratitude for the responsibility entrusted to him and reaffirmed his commitment to the welfare and betterment of De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic (DNT) Communities.

He said he would work towards fulfilling the objectives of the Board and contribute to addressing the needs and aspirations of DNT Communities.

DWBDNC is mandated to address the welfare and development concerns of DNT Communities and supports initiatives aimed at their socio-economic development and empowerment.

Shri Dewasi’s joining is expected to strengthen the Governing Body as it carries forward the Board’s mandate for the welfare and empowerment of De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Communities.

Earlier, Shri Swaroop Singh Banjara assumed charge as Member of the Governing Body of DWBDNC on 17th of this month.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Cooperation
item.description: Ministry of Cooperation National-Level Agenda-Setting Consultation on National Cooperative Training Framework (NCTF) 2026 held in New Delhi NCTF 2026 to strengthen the cooperative sector’s human-resource ecosystem in line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of “Sahkar se Samriddhi” Under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, emphasis being laid on building professional, skilled and future-ready cooperative institutions Consultation sets broad directions for developing a coherent, quality-assured, accessible and outcome-oriented national…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Cooperation
National-Level Agenda-Setting Consultation on National Cooperative Training Framework (NCTF) 2026 held in New Delhi
NCTF 2026 to strengthen the cooperative sector’s human-resource ecosystem in line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of “Sahkar se Samriddhi”
Under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, emphasis being laid on building professional, skilled and future-ready cooperative institutions
Consultation sets broad directions for developing a coherent, quality-assured, accessible and outcome-oriented national architecture for cooperative training and skilling
Focus of cooperative training must be on quality and outcomes, and not merely on increasing the number of training programmes: Shri Krishan Pal Gurjar
NCTF to promote convergence, quality, relevance, reach and continuity across cooperative training and capacity-building institutions
National consultation to be followed by five Regional-Level Consultations covering North, South, East, West and North-East India
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 6:44PM by PIB Delhi

In furtherance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of “Sahkar se Samriddhi” and under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, sustained efforts are being undertaken to strengthen, modernise and professionalise the cooperative sector and build robust institutional capacities across the cooperative ecosystem. Strengthening training, skilling and capacity building of cooperative personnel and stakeholders constitutes an important component of this endeavour.

In this direction, the National-Level Agenda-Setting Consultation on the National Cooperative Training Framework (NCTF) 2026 was organised by “Tribhuvan” Sahkari University (TSU) in collaboration with the Ministry of Cooperation, Government of India, at Atal Akshaya Urja Bhawan, New Delhi, on 24 September 2026.

The Consultation meeting was inaugurated by Shri Krishan Pal Gurjar, Minister of State for Cooperation. It brought together senior officials of the Ministry of Cooperation and Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, representatives of States and Union Territories, national-level cooperative federations, State Cooperative Unions, cooperative training institutions, sectoral developmental organisations, universities and other institutions engaged in training, skilling and capacity building in the cooperative sector.

Addressing the Consultation, Shri Krishan Pal Gurjar emphasised that the focus of cooperative training must be on quality and outcomes, and not merely on increasing the number of training programmes. He underlined the need for training interventions to result in stronger institutional capabilities, improved professional competencies and better outcomes for cooperative institutions and their members.

Speaking on the occasion, Prof. (Dr.) S. P. Singh, Vice-Chancellor, “Tribhuvan” Sahkari University, highlighted the importance of the National Cooperative Training Framework as an important enabler for realising the vision of “Sahkar se Samriddhi”.

He emphasised the need to bring together and strengthen the capabilities of institutions engaged in cooperative training and capacity building through a common and future-ready architecture capable of ensuring greater convergence, quality, relevance, reach and continuity, while remaining responsive to the diverse requirements of different States and regions.

The Agenda-Setting Consultation is the first of two National-Level Consultations envisaged under the NCTF process. It will be followed by five Regional-Level Consultations covering North, South, East, West and North-East India.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
Government’s Borrowing Plan for the second half of FY 2026-27
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 6:34PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India, in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), has decided to borrow ₹7,86,000 crore in the second half (H2) of FY 2026-27. This includes Sovereign Green Bonds (SGrBs) issuance of ₹15,000 crore

During FY 2026-27, Government of India is expected to have Market Borrowing of ₹15,99,506 crore through dated securities, as compared to Budget Estimates of ₹17,20,000 crore for FY 2026-27.

The gross market borrowing of ₹7,86,000 crore in H2: 2026-27 shall be completed through 23 weekly auctions. The market borrowing will be spread over securities of tenor 3, 5, 7, 10, 15, 30, 40 and 50 years. The share of borrowing (including SGrBs) under different maturities will be: 3-year (6.9%), 5-year (12.1%), 7-year (9.1%), 10-year (26.3%), 15-year (17.6%), 30-year (9.2%), 40-year (8.9%) and 50-year (9.9%).

The Government will continue to carry out switching/buyback of securities to smoothen the redemption profile.

The Government will continue to reserve the right to exercise greenshoe option to retain an additional subscription of up to ₹2,000 crore against each of the securities indicated in the auction notifications.

During the third Quarter of FY 2026-27, Government is expected to borrow ₹23,000 crore per week in 13 auction weeks through issuance of Treasury Bills (T-Bills). The break up would be ₹8,000 crore under 91-day T Bills, ₹8,000 crore under 182-day T-Bills and ₹7,000 crore under 364-day T-Bills.

To take care of temporary mismatches in Government accounts, if any, RBI has fixed the Ways and Means Advances (WMA) limit for H2 of FY 2026-27 at ₹50,000 crore.

More details may be seen in the detailed Press Releases available on the websites of the Ministry of Finance and the RBI.

item.title: The Ministry of Minority Affairs strengthens its infrastructure, entrepreneurship and monitoring drive through partnerships with strategic institutions at IISc Bangalore on September 25, 2026
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Minority Affairs
item.description: Ministry of Minority Affairs The Ministry of Minority Affairs strengthens its infrastructure, entrepreneurship and monitoring drive through partnerships with strategic institutions at IISc Bangalore on September 25, 2026 Collaborations with CUBE, IIT Madras, IISc-FSID, IIM Bangalore and IIMB Innovations to strengthen quality assessment, independent monitoring, entrepreneurship, innovation and economic opportunities for minority communities Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 6:26PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Minority Affairs, Government of India, entered into a number of…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Minority Affairs
The Ministry of Minority Affairs strengthens its infrastructure, entrepreneurship and monitoring drive through partnerships with strategic institutions at IISc Bangalore on September 25, 2026
Collaborations with CUBE, IIT Madras, IISc-FSID, IIM Bangalore and IIMB Innovations to strengthen quality assessment, independent monitoring, entrepreneurship, innovation and economic opportunities for minority communities
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 6:26PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Minority Affairs, Government of India, entered into a number of Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with prominent academic, research and innovation institutions at IISc Bengaluru on 25 September 2026, in the presence of Dr. Srivatsa Krishna, Secretary, Ministry of Minority Affairs and other senior officials of the Ministry and institutions. Through these, the Ministry has made significant strides in strengthening the implementation and impact of key initiatives of the Ministry, with a focus on infrastructure quality, independent monitoring, entrepreneurship, innovation, skilling and sustainable economic opportunities for minority communities.

The collaborations bring together the institutional strengths of the Centre for Urbanization, Buildings & Environment (CUBE), IIT Madras; Foundation for Science Innovation and Development (FSID), IISc Bengaluru; Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIM Bangalore); and IIMB Innovations (NSRCEL).

These partnerships will enable the Ministry to access specialised technical and academic expertise, strengthen evidence-based decision-making, improve monitoring and assessment mechanisms, support innovation and entrepreneurship, and create stronger institutional pathways for capacity building and enterprise development.

Independent third-party monitoring of PM VIKAS training

In a bid to strengthen transparency and accountability under the Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan (PM VIKAS) Scheme, the Ministry of Minority Affairs, Government of India, and Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB) signed an agreement for independent third-party monitoring of PM VIKAS training across the South zone.

Under this partnership, IIMB will conduct field-level inspections and concurrent monitoring, assessing training delivery, infrastructure, beneficiary and trainer participation, attendance, certification and placement outcomes through on-ground verification and stakeholder consultations.

The evidence-based insights generated through the partnership will help the Ministry strengthen implementation quality, identify and address gaps, improve monitoring mechanisms and enhance outcomes under PM VIKAS.

Independent third-party assessment of PMJVK infrastructure projects

The Ministry of Minority Affairs signed an MoU with CUBE, IIT Madras, for independent third-party quality (technical & social) assessment of infrastructure projects under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK).

The assessment will cover selected completed and ongoing PMJVK projects across the sectors of education, health, skill development, and women & child development. It will focus on key parameters, including infrastructure quality, functionality, accessibility, utilisation, maintenance and sustainability.

 

This partnership will provide the Ministry with independent, evidence-based assessments and actionable recommendations, enabling better asset management, identification of implementation gaps and more informed planning for future PMJVK projects. It will also deepen the understanding of the functionality and utilisation of infrastructure assets and contribute to more sustainable outcomes.

Strengthening entrepreneurship and innovation ecosystems

The two tripartite MoUs signed by the National Minorities Development & Finance Corporation (NMDFC) with the Foundation for Science Innovation and Development (FSID), promoted by the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, and IIMB Innovations (NSRCEL), the entrepreneurship and incubation centre of the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore, will establish a framework of cooperation to strengthen the startup and innovation ecosystem and promote economic growth of minority communities.

The collaboration with FSID, IISc Bengaluru focuses on startup ecosystem development, innovation promotion and technology commercialisation, along with data governance, digital transformation and public interest technology.

The MoU with IIMB Innovations (NSRCEL) focuses on strengthening the startup ecosystem, along with skilling and capacity building, innovation and entrepreneurship promotion, research studies, policy support and evidence-based decision-making.

Under the Prime Minister Minority Venture Fund (PM-MVF) framework, these collaborations envisage entrepreneurship awareness and capacity-building programmes, innovation challenges and startup identification, incubation and mentoring, investor connect, market access and enterprise development. They also provide access to knowledge networks, institutional support, industry linkages and innovation ecosystems, with a focus on developing scalable, sustainable and innovationdriven enterprises.

The two collaborations bring together the complementary strengths of IISc-FSID in deep-science and deep-technology incubation, technology commercialisation and innovation promotion, and IIMB-NSRCEL in entrepreneurship, incubation, marketoriented opportunities and fintech. Together, they seek to support minority entrepreneurs and strengthen their access to startup and innovation ecosystems.

A collaborative approach to inclusive development

The signing of these MoUs represents a collaborative approach towards strengthening the impact of initiatives of the Ministry by bringing together technical expertise, academic knowledge, research capabilities and established entrepreneurship ecosystems.

While addressing the gathering, Dr. Srivatsa Krishna said, “The focus of the government is EEE to enable employment through entrepreneurship. The focus of the MoUs with premier technology institutions in the country, namely:

- Indian Institute of Science Bangalore

- Indian Institute of Management Bangalore

 - CUBE of Indian Institute of Technology Madras

is to synergise and bring together their expertise to make this mission possible. 

The end goal is to select, curate and fund those startups which can create employment through entrepreneurship and ensure that the quality of built assets for the minority community and their utilisation is at par with the best. "

Speaking on the occasion, Professor U Dinesh Kumar, Director-in-charge, IIM Bangalore, said, “IIMB values the responsibility entrusted to it through such efforts, particularly where its expertise can help strengthen public programmes and their outcomes. Through our Centres of Excellence, both of which have over 25 years of experience in creating impact on the ground, we are keen to bring our understanding, knowledge and capabilities to initiatives that can expand opportunities for minority communities as well as enable pathways for enterprise.”

While the partnership with CUBE, IIT Madras strengthens independent assessment and evidence-based improvement of PMJVK infrastructure, the collaborations with IIM Bangalore, IISc-FSID and IIMB Innovations (NSRCEL) create institutional pathways for entrepreneurship, innovation, incubation, skilling and enterprise development.

Through these partnerships, the Ministry has undertaken another positive step in strengthening its institutional capacity for quality assessment, independent monitoring, data-driven decision-making, innovation, entrepreneurship and enterprise development, while building enabling ecosystems that support sustainable economic opportunities for minority communities.

item.content:encoded:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported suicide of a woman gang-raped in Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh
Issues notices to the District Magistrate and Senior Superintendent of Police, Jhansi, for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 6:24PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report that a 19 year-old woman committed suicide after being gang-raped by six people, including three minors. Reportedly, the woman went to a cattle barn for some work when the six accused allegedly caught her and gang-raped her.

The Commission has observed that the contents of the media report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued notices to the Senior Superintendent of Police and the District Magistrate, Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks. The report is expected to include the status of the investigation and compensation, if any, paid to the next of kin of the deceased.

According to the media report, carried on 23rd September 2026, the victim was distressed by the threats to circulate the video and consumed poison.

item.content:encoded:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India’s Online Short-Term Internship Programme for September 2026 concludes, 95 university-level students from diverse academic backgrounds, shortlisted out of 1008 applicants, completed the programme
Chairing the valedictory session, NHRC Member, Justice (Dr.) Bidyut Ranjan Sarangi encourages interns to practise and share human rights values in everyday conduct
Member, Smt. Vijaya Bharathi Sayani calls upon interns to make human rights a way of life
Secretary General, Shri Piyush Goyal urges interns to become torch bearers of human rights
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 6:22PM by PIB Delhi

The two-week Online Short-Term Internship Programme (OSTI) of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India concluded today with 95 university-level students completing it. The internship began on 14th September 2026. The interns were shortlisted out of 1008 applicants from 19 states and union territories across the country.

Chairing the valedictory session, NHRC Member, Justice (Dr.) Bidyut Ranjan Sarangi, congratulated the interns on successful completion of the programme. He emphasised that the two-week training programme was not merely a journey but a valuable learning experience. Urging the interns to ensure that their efforts do not go in vain, he highlighted the importance of “Preach, Practice and Perform”, stressing that learning about human rights should continue throughout life and that the knowledge gained must be practised and shared with others.

Calling upon the interns to demonstrate human rights values in their everyday conduct, Justice Sarangi urged them to be compassionate towards others, including senior citizens and persons with disabilities and to extend appropriate consideration to their needs. He said that as young people, the interns carried great expectations for the development of the country and society.

Addressing the interns, NHRC Member, Smt. Vijaya Bharathi Sayani said that the conclusion of the internship marked not an end but the beginning of a new responsibility. She urged them to carry forward a commitment to human rights, the Constitution and the nation, stressing that human rights are about dignity, justice, compassion and responsibility towards one another and should become a way of life.

Emphasising that human rights and patriotism complement each other, Smt. Sayani urged the interns to respect the Constitution, protect human dignity, serve the vulnerable and stand for justice. Drawing on Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam and Sarve Bhavantu Sukhinah, she called upon them to become human rights ambassadors in their communities and highlighted “knowledge, compassion and service” as guiding principles for contributing to a stronger, more just and humane India.

In his address, NHRC Secretary General, Shri Piyush Goyal, congratulated the interns and emphasised the importance of developing sensitivity towards human dignity in everyday life. He said that academic learning is meaningful when translated into practice. Highlighting the value of teamwork and communication skills, he said that the team activities helped inculcate team spirit and collaborative skills. He urged the interns to become torch bearers of human rights by creating greater awareness of its practical dimensions in society.

Before this, NHRC Joint Secretary, Shri Samir Kumar, presented an overview of the internship programme, highlighting the opportunity provided to the interns to interact with NHRC Members, senior NHRC officers, eminent experts, academicians, Core Group members and representatives of civil society organisations. He expressed hope that the programme enriched the interns’ understanding of human rights. He also announced the winners of competitions, including book review, group research project presentation and declamation. Smt. Monika Joon delivered the vote of thanks.

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Textiles
Ministry of Textiles Undertakes Cleanliness Drives and Awareness Initiatives Across Organisations under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 6:09PM by PIB Delhi

As part of the ongoing Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 campaign, Divisional Heads inspected their respective Sections on 24 September 2026 at GPOA-3, Netaji Nagar, New Delhi, with a view to reviewing the prevailing standards of cleanliness, hygiene and general upkeep of the workplace. During the inspections, emphasis was laid on maintaining clean and orderly workspaces, ensuring proper disposal of waste, removing unwanted and obsolete materials, and promoting a clean, hygienic and conducive working environment. The exercise also aimed to sensitise officials towards the importance of cleanliness and to reinforce their collective responsibility for sustaining the principles of Swachhata in day-to-day office functioning.

The Jute Corporation of India Limited (JCI)

As part of the “Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026,” the Jute Corporation of India Limited (JCI) undertook various cleanliness and awareness initiatives under the themes of “Clean Public Places,” “Jan Bhagidari Advocacy,” and “Swachh Paathshala .

As part of these initiatives, cleanliness drives, awareness programmes, and various community engagement activities were organized at multiple locations across different areas, with the active participation of JCI officials and employees, as well as members of the public.

These activities were aimed at promoting cleanliness, hygiene, civic responsibility, environmental awareness, and active public participation in creating and maintaining clean, hygienic, and sustainable surroundings. Through these collective efforts, JCI reinforced its commitment to fostering a culture of cleanliness and encouraging greater community involvement in the Swachhata Hi Seva campaign.

Cleanliness activities in Public Places:

  • Jute Corporation of India Limited (JCI), Kharupetia Departmental Purchase Centre (DPC), Darrang District, under the Guwahati Regional Office, Assam, in association with Govt. Model Women’s College, Mangaldai, Assam, organized cleanliness activities and installed dustbins at public places to promote awareness about cleanliness, sanitation, hygiene, waste management, and environmental responsibility.

  • Samsi, Departmental Purchase Centre (DPC), Malda Region, conducted a cleanliness drive in the market area in front of the SBI ATM, with the objective of promoting cleanliness, hygiene, proper waste management, and environmental responsibility among the public.

  • Lakhipur Departmental Purchase Centre (DPC), Golapara district, Assam, under Guwahati Regional Office, conducted a cleanliness drive at Kharubucha Point Bus Stop. The activity focused on cleaning the public area and promoting awareness about cleanliness, sanitation, hygiene, and responsible waste management among the local community and commuters.

 

 

 

  • A cleanliness drive was conducted at Abhayapuri Rajbari Main Road, Abhayapuri, Bongaigaon District, Assam, under the Gauripur Region. The activity focused on maintaining cleanliness in the public area and promoting awareness about sanitation, hygiene, proper waste management, and environmental responsibility among the local community.

Jan Bhagidari Advocacy

  • The Jute Corporation of India organized various sports activities at different locations across India under the “Jan Bhagidari Advocacy” initiative. The activities encouraged active participation, teamwork, fitness, and awareness among employees and members of the public, fostering a spirit of community participation and collective responsibility.

 

National Jute Board (NJB)

As part of the Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 campaign, Employees of the National Jute Board (NJB) undertook a cleanliness drive at the Jute Diversified Product (JDP) units, with the objective of promoting cleanliness, hygiene and proper waste-management practices in the jute sector.

The cleanliness drive was conducted at Recrust International and SL Packaging, wherein the employees/workers of the respective units actively participated along with the Employees of the National Jute Board in cleaning.

During the visit, the premises of the units were inspected and cleanliness and waste-management practices were reviewed. It was encouraging to observe that the premises were already being maintained in a clean and hygienic condition, reflecting the commitment of the workers and management towards maintaining a healthy and sustainable working environment. The existing practices demonstrated awareness among the workers regarding cleanliness, proper handling of waste and maintenance of the workplace.

The National Jute Board appreciated the efforts of the management and workers of the participating JDP units in maintaining high standards of cleanliness. The activity reinforced the message that cleanliness is a continuous collective responsibility and encouraged all stakeholders to sustain these practices as part of the objectives of the Swachhata Hi Seva campaign.

The cleanliness drive concluded with a positive appreciation of the efforts undertaken by the participating units towards maintaining a clean, hygienic and environmentally responsible workplace.

 

THE COTTON CORPORATION OF INDIA LTD.

As part of the Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 Campaign, a Clean Desk and Clean Campus activity was conducted at the Head Office and Branch Offices with active participation from all employees. Employees cleaned and organized their workspaces, cupboards, and surrounding areas, while unwanted materials were identified and segregated.

Under the “Kabad Se Jugaad” initiative, scrap and unusable materials were segregated for systematic disposal, promoting the 3R principles – Reduce, Reuse and Recycle, while also exploring the potential for revenue generation through recyclable scrap.

The initiative strengthened awareness among employees about cleanliness and encouraged collective responsibility towards maintaining a clean, organized, and hygienic workplace.

 

 

National Handloom Development Corporation Limited (NHDC)

राष्‍ट्रीय हथकरघा विकास निगम लिमिटेड, नोएडा -  दिनांक 24 सितम्‍बर 2026 को अपराह्न 2.30 बजे, स्‍वच्‍छता नोडल अधिकारी द्वारा स्‍वच्‍छता व्यवस्था का औचक निरीक्षण किया गया। निरीक्षण के दौरान कार्यालय/परिसर में साफ-सफाई, कूड़ा निस्तारण, शौचालयों की स्वच्छता तथा आसपास के क्षेत्र की स्थिति का जायजा लिया गया। नोडल अधिकारी ने संबंधित कर्मचारियों को स्वच्छता व्यवस्था नियमित रूप से बनाए रखने, कूड़े का उचित निस्तारण करने तथा किसी भी प्रकार की गंदगी न होने देने के निर्देश दिए। उन्होंने कहा कि स्वच्छ एवं स्वस्थ वातावरण बनाए रखना सभी की सामूहिक जिम्मेदारी है और इसमें किसी भी प्रकार की लापरवाही स्वीकार नहीं की जाएगी।

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Recovery to Renewed Purpose
Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts in Hailakandi Assam Support Helps Sandeep Rebuild Family Ties and Return to Work
Now Employed at the Centre That Supported His Recovery
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 5:51PM by PIB Delhi

Sandeep (name changed), 33, grew up in a supportive family in Assam. After studying through Class 9, he moved to Guwahati to stay with his aunt and seek work. He learned to drive and began earning a living, but substance use, which began under peer influence, gradually developed into dependency.

His health, work and relationships suffered. Much of his income went towards substance use, leaving him under financial strain and increasingly isolated. Sandeep wanted to recover, regain his family’s trust and become financially independent. His family continued to encourage him to seek help.

On 6 September 2025, Sandeep received support through the Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA) run by South Borbond Gram Unnayan Samity in Hailakandi.

The centre provided medical care, psychological and family counselling, rehabilitation support, and motivational and behavioural guidance. Group activities and life-skills guidance helped him build healthier routines, manage stress and reconnect with others.

Sandeep while expressing his emotions and happiness said, “With my family's support and the care I received at IRCA, I am rebuilding my life and working again”.

Following his treatment, Sandeep has made positive progress in his recovery. He is working to maintain a life free from substance use and has reconnected with his family. He now works as a multi-tasking staff member at IRCA Hailakandi, giving him greater financial stability and a chance to contribute to the centre that supported his recovery.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah inaugurates fourth edition of the Uttar Pradesh International Trade Show in Greater Noida
Modi Ji has made political stability his hallmark, by winning people’s trust as Prime Minister for three consecutive terms, he has implemented policies on the ground
By making changes in policies based on experience, formulating new policies, and demonstrating clarity in all of them, Modi Ji has made India an attractive manufacturing hub for the entire world
Amidst so much upheaval and unrest around the world, and despite numerous obstacles, India’s growth rate is rising today
Those who see India as a ‘dead economy’ have, in fact, a dead mindset themselves — that is why they cannot see India’s vibrancy and growth
Due to the double-engine government, UP is today becoming fear-free, a centre of investment, and the engine of the country’s development
For a favourable investment climate — good law and order, a conducive industrial policy, a proactive government, and the enthusiasm to facilitate — all four of these are present in UP
This trade fair will make it easier for producers across UP to expand their trade and production, and will help take UP’s identity to the world
The same UP, whose law-and-order situation forced the investment summit to be held in Delhi in 2013, is today setting a target of a $1 trillion economy — this is the magic of the double-engine government
Where earlier a cottage industry of vehicle theft and chain-snatching used to thrive, today defence corridors, vehicle manufacturing, and medical device parks are coming up
BrahMos missiles manufactured in UP keep Pakistan on edge, while the AK-203 assault rifles manufactured in Amethi have already struck fear into the hearts of Naxalites and terrorists
‘One District, One Product’ initiative has brought about significant progress for the youth, small entrepreneurs, and small-scale industries, and has emerged as a key driver of State’s economic development
Paying tribute to Pt.  Deendayal Upadhyaya Ji on his 110th birth anniversary, Union Home Minister said that
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 5:47PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today inaugurated the fourth edition of the Uttar Pradesh International Trade Show (UPITS) in Greater Noida. On this occasion, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath and many other dignitaries were present.

In his address, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that today is a very important day. He said that 12 years ago, on 25 September itself, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi had announced the ‘Make in India’ mission. Today’s programme is one that paves the way for ‘Make in India’. Over the past 12 years, the Central Government and the State Governments together have walked the path of ‘Make in India’ and worked to make India a global hub of production, design and innovation. Shri Shah said that 12 years ago the Indian economy was counted among the Fragile 5, and today the Indian economy is among the Top 5, which is the result of Prime Minister Modi’s ‘Make in India’ policy.

Shri Amit Shah said that 25th September is the 110th birth anniversary of Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya ji. He said that for the first time after independence Deendayal Upadhyaya ji placed before the country a free trade and free agriculture-based economic policy. The same economic policy later became the foundation of India’s development, first under Atal ji and thereafter under the leadership of Shri Narendra Modi. Deendayal ji also laid the foundation of organisation-based politics.

Union Home Minister said that a fear-free Uttar Pradesh is emerging as an investment hub and the engine of India’s development today. This transformation has taken place because of the double-engine government. Due to this change, we can set the target of making Uttar Pradesh’s economy a 1-trillion-dollar economy. He said that buyers from across the world are present at trade fair today, and this will certainly lead to a massive increase in investment, production and sales in Uttar Pradesh. This is the fourth edition of the Uttar Pradesh International Trade Fair. In the first edition, the world was introduced to the transformation that had taken place in Uttar Pradesh. In the second edition, an intent to invest in Uttar Pradesh was expressed. In the third edition, investors came to Uttar Pradesh, and today, in the fourth edition of the trade fair, they will work as partners in the state’s development towards building a 1-trillion-dollar economy. He said that the year 2025 was a year of impact, in which more than 5 lakh people visited the trade fair, more than 2,400 MoUs were signed, investment worth thousands of crores of rupees came in, and trade agreements were also concluded. Shri Shah expressed confidence that the fourth edition of the trade fair being organised in 2026 will succeed in breaking all the records of 2025.

Shri Amit Shah said that with a population of nearly 24 crore, Uttar Pradesh is the largest state in the country. It has abundant water resources, land, hardworking artisans, and now a favourable environment for industry as well. There was a time when the mafia ruled Uttar Pradesh, but in 2017 our party formed the government here and Shri Yogi Adityanath became the Chief Minister of the state. The Yogi government has eliminated the mafia across Uttar Pradesh, and it is because of this that an investment-friendly climate has been created in the state today. He said that the first conditions for an investment climate are good law & order, a favourable industrial policy, a proactive government, and the enthusiasm to facilitate industry. All four of these are present in Uttar Pradesh today, which is why an atmosphere for investment has been created here. Prime Minister Modi has made political stability his hallmark. By winning the people’s trust for three consecutive terms as Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi has not only formulated policies but has also implemented them continuously on the ground. Along with putting policies into practice, Prime Minister Modi has refined them on the basis of experience and framed new policies, thereby making India an attractive manufacturing hub for the entire world.

Union Home Minister said that some people even try to dispute India’s GDP figures. Moody’s has raised India’s growth forecast from 6% to 7%. Japan’s leading rating agency Japan Credit Rating Agency (JCR) has upgraded India’s sovereign rating from BBB+ to A-. In the last quarter, India maintained its record by achieving a growth rate of 7.8%. Today, among the world’s major economies, India’s is the fastest-growing. He said that amid so much upheaval and unrest around the world, and despite numerous obstacles, India has not only sustained its growth rate but has also accelerated it further. Shri Shah said that we will fulfil the resolve given by Prime Minister Modi to the people of the country to build a ‘Viksit Bharat’ by 2047.

Shri Amit Shah said that our electronic exports have increased 11 times compared to 2015. In July, GST collection stood at ₹2.11 lakh crore, which is the highest collection for the month of July so far. There are 12 semiconductor projects in 6 states with an investment of more than ₹1.64 lakh crore, and our capital expenditure has broken records by crossing ₹12.2 lakh crore. All these achievements are a testament to the foundation of India’s development. He said that some people find the Indian economy a “dead economy,” but those whose thinking itself is dead cannot see its vibrancy. Shri Shah said that some people cannot see India’s development. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi, we have signed Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) with Mauritius, UAE, Austria, the organisation of four European countries, UK, Oman, New Zealand, and European Union. These FTAs have multiplied the export potential of our industries many times over. Shri Shah said that despite various adversities, the Indian economy has sustained its growth rate.

Union Home Minister said that today investment is flowing into defence manufacturing at the six nodes of the Defence Corridor in Jhansi, Chitrakoot, Lucknow, Agra, Aligarh and Kanpur in Uttar Pradesh. As a result, not only Uttar Pradesh but defence products across the country have developed, and our defence production stands at ₹1,78,000 crore. Compared to 2013-14, we have increased the export of defence products by 56 times, and today Indian defence products are being exported to 80 countries. He said that Uttar Pradesh has made a very significant contribution to this. The Yogi government has not only established the Defence Corridor but has also done extensive work to facilitate it, link it with infrastructure and create favourable policies. The BrahMos missiles manufactured in UP keep Pakistan on edge, while the AK-203 assault rifles manufactured in Amethi have already struck fear into the hearts of Naxalites and terrorists.

Shri Amit Shah said that during the tenure of previous governments, a crime industry was thriving in Uttar Pradesh, and the state had become a hub for the manufacture of country-made pistols and illegal firearms. Vehicle theft operated like a cottage industry in the cities of the state, and chain-snatching even provided an opportunity for the youth to show off their skills. Today, after 10 years, the country-made pistols industry has been replaced by a Defence Corridor, vehicle theft by vehicle manufacturing, and the chain-snatching industry by Medical Device Parks. He said that today Uttar Pradesh has become a major destination for attracting investment, and this transformation has taken place due to the double-engine government. He said that the very Uttar Pradesh - whose law & order situation had necessitated holding the 2013 investment summit in Delhi - is today setting a target of becoming a $1 trillion economy; this is the magic of the 'double-engine' government.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that after the formation of the Yogi government, the complete goondaism of the previous governments’ tenure has been wiped out, and this has created a favourable environment for setting up industries here. Uttar Pradesh has achieved good results through its lucrative industrial policy, prompt resolution of industries’ problems, and by rolling out the red carpet to attract industries from across the country to the state. Through this, the government of Yogi Adityanath has created employment opportunities for crores of youth in the state.

Shri Amit Shah said that the Noida Airport, expressways and various infrastructure projects have created a conducive environment for investment in the state. As a result, today Uttar Pradesh is progressing at a rapid pace. The metro is currently operational in seven cities of Uttar Pradesh, which is the highest in any state in the country. We have launched the ‘One District, One Product’ (ODOP) scheme here. Due to the nurturing of traditional crafts and industries along with the ODOP initiative, there has been a significant rise among the youth, small entrepreneurs and small-scale industries of the state, which has become the pivot of Uttar Pradesh’s economic development.

Union Home Minister said that there was a time when people from Uttar Pradesh used to migrate to other states of the country in search of employment, and today the youth of the same Uttar Pradesh are getting employment in their own state due to the ‘One District, One Product’ scheme. Whether it is the carpets of Bhadohi, the brassware of Moradabad, the glass of Firozabad, the woodcraft of Saharanpur, the perfume of Kannauj or the silk sarees of Banaras — all these have carved a distinct identity across the country. Just now, the website of ‘One District, One Cuisine’ (ODOC) was also launched here, through which Varanasi’s Malaiyo and Tiranga Barfi, Agra’s Petha, Mathura’s Peda and Meerut’s Gajak will be made available to the people of the entire country — from Kashmir to Kanyakumari and from Dwarka to Kamakhya. Shri Shah said that this trade fair will greatly facilitate the trade and production of producers across Uttar Pradesh and help in establishing UP’s identity worldwide.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Operation Drishti: AFMS conducts 220 sight-restoring surgeries during 2-day Mega Eye Surgical Camp at Tangdhar along LoC
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 5:46PM by PIB Delhi

          Surgeons of the Armed Forces Medical Services (AFMS) carried out 220 sight-restoring surgeries during the 10th edition of first-of-its-kind Mega Eye Surgical Camp, held under Operation Drishti, at an underground operation theatre in Tangdhar in Kupwara, a shelling prone zone, in Jammu & Kashmir along the Line of Control on September 24 & 25, 2026. Most interventions were cataract surgeries, along with selective retinal procedures and minimally invasive glaucoma surgery.

          Over the two days, the camp was visited by Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth who interacted with patients and distributed medicines & gifts. DG AFMS Air Marshal Sandeep Thareja also visited the camp and appreciated the surgeons and the local team for their exceptional skills & efforts.

          The camp was led by Head of Ophthalmology at Army Hospital (Research & Referral), Delhi Cantonment Brigadier Sanjay Kumar Mishra, whose team carried advanced phacoemulsification, vitreoretinal and glaucoma equipment across mountainous terrain. Patients from Khawarpora, Tangdar, Tadd, Bagbela, Yangdar and neighbouring hamlets came after screening and a broadcast on Radio Rooh-e-Karnah, with the Indian Army guiding each one from arrival to recovery.

AFMS’ series of mega surgical eye camps envisaged by Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh have, so far, screened over 1.50 lakh patients. Over 3,500 surgeries have been conducted across 10 cities. The 11th camp in this series will be held in Srinagar from September 27 to 29, 2026. The formal closing ceremony will be graced by Lieutenant Governor of Jammu & Kashmir, Shri Manoj Sinha on September 30, 2026.
