item.dc:creator: Ministry of Jal Shakti
item.description: Ministry of Jal Shakti Climate Resilience, Water Finance and Innovation in Focus on Day 3 of India International Water Week 2026 Deliberations span climate risk assessment, early warning systems, glacial lake monitoring, water-use efficiency and innovative financing India-Netherlands cooperation advances through two tripartite MoUs Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 10:16PM by PIB Delhi The third day carried the 9 th India International Water Week 2026 deeper into its technical programme, into the forward-looking questions of climate risk, early warning, glacial lake monitoring,…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
Climate Resilience, Water Finance and Innovation in Focus on Day 3 of India International Water Week 2026
Deliberations span climate risk assessment, early warning systems, glacial lake monitoring, water-use efficiency and innovative financing
India-Netherlands cooperation advances through two tripartite MoUs
Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 10:16PM by PIB Delhi

The third day carried the 9th India International Water Week 2026 deeper into its technical programme, into the forward-looking questions of climate risk, early warning, glacial lake monitoring, water pricing and the financing of resilient water infrastructure. Sessions ran in parallel across the Water Leaders' Forum, Country Forum, Practitioners' Forum, Thematic Forum and Start-Up Forum. The Thematic Forum closed the third of its seven sub-themes and moved through the fourth and fifth.

The day also widened the Week's international reach. The Start-Up Forum gave startups, MSMEs and academia a platform to pitch problem-driven water solutions. On the sidelines, a bilateral meeting advanced India-Netherlands cooperation, with two tripartite MoUs signed.

India-Netherlands Bilateral Meeting

On the sidelines of the 9th India International Water Week-2026, a bilateral meeting between the Shri C R Patil, Minister of Jal Shakti and H.E. Mr. Jaap Slootmaker, Vice Minister for Infrastructure and Water Management, Netherlands, was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Shri Raj Bhushan Choudhary, Minister of State, Ministry of Jal Shakti, Shri Ishwarsinh Patel, Minister of State for Water Resources and Water Supply (Independent Charge), joined the meeting, along with H. E Marissa Gerard, Ambassador of the Kingdom of the Netherlands to India.

During the event, a tripartite MoU was signed between Central Water Commission, Kalpasar, Deptt. Govt. of Gujarat and Deltares, Netherlands for technical support. Another tripartite MoU was signed between CWC, Kalpasar Deptt. of Govt. of Gujarat and TU Delft Netherlands for capacity building and trainings. The MoUs will facilitate technical collaboration through sharing of Dutch expertise and advanced engineering practices for the planning, design and implementation of the project.

 

 

Country Forum (CF)

CF-4 on Private Capital Mobilisation in the Water Sector, convened with the World Bank, was chaired by Shri Baldeo Purushartha, Joint Secretary, DEA, GOI and co-chaired by Smt. Roshika Singh, Principal Country Officer, IFC India. The session opened with a keynote by Shri Saroj Kumar Jha, Global Water Director, World Bank, and was moderated by Mr. William Rex, Practice Manager for Water, World Bank, with Jain Irrigations, IFC India, Coca-Cola,VA Tech Wabag, Tata Capital, the Maharashtra Institution for Transformation (MITRA) and the Uttar Pradesh State Transformation Commission, on the reforms and financing mechanisms needed to unlock private investment in urban water, wastewater and irrigation.

 

Water Leaders’ Forum (WLF)

WLF-3 on Improving Water Use Efficiency Using State-of-the-Art Technology in the Water Resources Sector, convened with the CII Water Institute, was chaired by P. C. Vyas, Principal Secretary, (Water Resources) Government of Gujarat, and co-chaired by Smt. Shilpa Nischal, Executive Director, CII Water Institute, with Grundfos, Murugappa Water Technology, Ion Exchange, Kritsnam Technologies and NITI Aayog, on smart metering, monitoring and technology for water-use efficiency.

 

WLF-4 on Climate Risk Assessment for Water Security, convened with the National Institute of Hydrology, Roorkee, was chaired by Prof. Nagesh Kumar, Professor, IISc Bangalore, and co-chaired by Dr. Y. R. S. Rao, Director, NIH Roorkee, with ICHARM (Japan), IIT Bombay, IISc Bangalore, CWC and IIT Delhi, on integrating climate risk assessment into water governance and planning frameworks.

 

WLF-5 on Embedding Climate Action in Water Governance and Policies, convened with CEEW, was chaired by Shri Jogindra Singh IAS, Project Director, State Mission for Clean Ganga, Govt. of Uttar Pradesh, and co-chaired by Ms. Noa Amsalem, Water Attache, Embassy of Israel, with IIT Guwahati, WELL Labs Bengaluru, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, Google, Council on Energy, Environment and Water and DCM Shriram, on shifting from managing climate risk to building resilience through governance reform.

WLF-6 on Climate-Resilient Adaptation Measures in Water Resources, convened with the National Dam Safety Authority was chaired by Shri Rakesh Kashyap, Chairman, National Dam Safety Authority and co-chaired by Shri Manoj Kumar Acharya, Former Chief Engineer, BODHI, Madhya Pradesh Water Resources Department, with IIT Delhi, HCL Foundation, IMD, GIZ and NDMA, addressed hydrological modelling for dams under a changing climate, glacial lake outburst floods, and the structural rehabilitation of earthen and rockfill dams, drawing on international financing experience for climate-resilient dam infrastructure.

 

Practitioners’ Forum (PF)

PF-5 on Session on Best Practices, convened with the National Water Mission, was chaired by Shri Rajesh Toppo, Secretary, Water Resources, Government of Chhattisgarh, and co-chaired by Shri Atul Jain, Former Chairman, Central Water Commission, with district collectors and municipal commissioners from Tripura, Telangana and Surat; and Himalayan Environmental Studies and Conservation Organization, Ministry of Rural Development and The Rainwater Project, on integrating global best practices with the Ministry of Jal Shakti's efforts; the Jal Jeevan Mission now reports about 81.5% of rural households with tap water connections.

PF-6 on Water Disputes and Resolution, was chaired by Dr. Srinivas Chokkakula, President and Chief Executive, Centre for Policy Research and co-chaired by Shri P. Dorje Gyamba, Chairman, Godavari River Management Board, with the CWC, Supreme Court advocates, the National Water Academy, Pune, and river-basin management board representatives, examined Alternative Dispute Resolution mechanisms and the proposed Disputes Resolution Committee under the Inter-State River Water Disputes framework.

PF-7 on Jal-Sanskriti and HARIT Pathways: India's Water Heritage for a Resilient Future, was chaired by Dr. Murli Manohar Joshi, Padma Vibhushan, Former Union Minister, Ministry of Human Resource Development, on connecting India's traditional water culture, its sacred rivers, temple tanks and stepwells, with modern, climate-resilient water management, and on carrying that heritage into community-led conservation.

 

Thematic Forum (TF)

Six Thematic Forum sessions ran through the day, presenting shortlisted papers, closing the third of the Forum's seven sub-themes and moving through the fourth and fifth.

Sub-theme 3 and Sub-theme 4, Water in Climate-Related Risk: TF-9 Data-Driven Governance, chaired by Shri Sher Singh, Chairman, Ganga Flood Control Commission and Member (Floods), CWC, and co-chaired by Shri S. G. Bhartariya, Member (SAM), Central Ground Water Board with the National Water Informatics Centre, BISAG-N and the Government of Andhra Pradesh; TF-10 Early Warning System for Climate Risk Reduction, chaired by Dr. Krishna Vatsa, Member, National Disaster Management Authority, and co-chaired by Dr. D.R. Pattanaik, Scientist-G, India Meteorological Department; TF-11 Monitoring of Glacial Lake Outburst, chaired by Shri D. P. Mathuria, Chief Engineer (P&DO), Central Water Commission, and co-chaired by Dr. Surjeet Singh, Scientist 'G' & Head Centre for Cryosphere & Climate Change Studies (C4S), NIH Roorkee; and TF-12 Climate Change: Erratic Precipitation, was chaired by Dr. D.S. Pai, Scientist-G, India Meteorological Department and co-chaired by Dr. Ankur Srivastava, Scientist E, Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology, Pune with the India Meteorological Department, CWPRS Pune, NIH Roorkee and CWC. Papers ranged over water informatics and AI-assisted data governance, drought and flood forecasting, AI-powered dam-safety early warning, glacial lake outburst flood vulnerability and monitoring across the Himalaya, and long-term rainfall and temperature trends under a changing climate. Among the papers were the indigenous HIM JHEEL NETRA glacial-lake monitoring system, a national-scale flood forecasting system, erosion modelling on the Brahmaputra, and geophysical investigations for dam safety.

 

Sub-theme 5, Innovative Financing Models: TF-13 Public-Private Partnerships for Water Finance and Innovative Financing Models, was chaired by Mr. Takeshi Ueda, Director, South Asia, Sector Department 2, Agriculture, Food, Nature, and Rural Development Sector Group, Asian Development Bank with co-chair Shri Rajesh Advani, Senior Water Specialist, World Bank, with the Asian Development Bank; and TF-14 Policy for Water User Charges, was chaired by Shri Sanjay Marwah, Member, Haryana Water Resources Authority, and co-chaired by Shri Subrata Singh, Executive Director, Foundation for Ecological Society. Papers examined green finance for WASH infrastructure, solar power potential along the Ken-Betwa link, and the restructuring of water user charges, including a comparative analysis of CGWA guidelines and AI-based canal-release optimisation, and made the case for water user charges as a lever for the long-term sustainability of irrigation.

Start-Up Forum (SUF))

The Start-Up Forum, chaired by Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science and Technology and co-chaired by Col. Saurabh Sanyal, Secretary General, ASSOCHAM showcased problem-driven solutions from startups, MSMEs and academia across water resources management, wastewater treatment, irrigation efficiency and smart water systems, including prototypes developed through partnerships between startups, industry and academia. The forum also provided startups with an opportunity to present practical, deployable solutions to a panel of experts and investors.

The Ministry has also strengthened engagement with academic institutions and students to provide them with first-hand exposure to the challenges and opportunities in the water sector.

After having several meetings with the AICTE in coordination with Ministry of Education last year, Jal Seva Adhyayan initiative is being implemented in collaboration with AICTE. 49 teams, comprising students and faculty, visited 132 villages across the country from February till April 2026. They gained first-hand exposure to rural drinking water service delivery and submitted detailed field reports based on their observations. Around 50 participating students also joined the Roundtable Conference with African Ambassadors at Bharat Mandapam. Following the roundtable, a special interaction session titled “Peyjal Ki Baat: Jal Shakti Minister ke Saath” was organised, providing students a unique opportunity to engage directly with the leadership of the Ministry of Jal Shakti and discuss challenges, innovations and opportunities in the water sector.


The interaction highlighted the importance of youth participation, innovation and community engagement in strengthening the country's water sector. Students were encouraged to take their learnings beyond the classroom, apply their technical knowledge to real-world challenges and contribute towards building a Viksit Bharat 2047. The discussion focused on the transformative impact of the Jal Jeevan Mission on rural lives, the importance of safe drinking water, water quality surveillance through community participation, the growing role of digital technology and AI, and the need for innovative, practical and scalable solutions to address emerging water-sector challenges.

 


Addressing the students, Shri C R Patil, Union Minister of Jal Shakti, emphasised that the Jal Jeevan Mission is not merely an infrastructure programme but a transformational initiative linked to health, dignity, women's empowerment and quality of life. He urged students to develop innovative and cost-effective technological solutions for the water sector and stressed the importance of dialogue and consensus in resolving water-related challenges.

Shri Raj Bhushan Choudhary, Union Minister of State for Jal Shakti, encouraged students to study global best practices, leverage AI, digital technologies and social media, and identify solutions emerging from rural communities and grassroots innovators.

Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, underlined the need to expose engineering students to ground-level realities of rural water supply systems and informed that, in collaboration with AICTE, efforts are underway to introduce water governance-related academic courses and expand the outreach of Jal Seva Adhyayan to engineering institutions nationwide.

Smt. Archana Varma, Secretary, Ministry of Water Resources, highlighted the transformative potential of information technology and artificial intelligence in water governance and called upon students to apply their technical expertise in public service, innovation and sustainable water management for national development.

Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Additional Secretary and Mission Director, National Jal Jeevan Mission, welcomed the panelists and the students to the interactive session. He briefed about the Jal Seva Adhyayan, and the upcoming water management course by AICTE.

 

Technical Sessions

The first technical session, “Water Supply Systems: O&M, Infrastructure & Source Sustainability,” focused on strengthening the long-term sustainability of rural water supply systems. Four papers were presented covering themes including GIS-based assessment of water supply infrastructure, water pricing strategies, water footprint assessment for sustainable water resources management, and approaches to strengthening community ownership in piped drinking water systems. The discussions highlighted the importance of effective operation and maintenance, infrastructure and asset management, financial sustainability, and community participation in ensuring reliable water services.

 

The second technical session, “Water Quality, Safety & Emerging Contaminants,” focused on water safety and quality management in the context of emerging challenges. Five papers examined community-led climate-resilient interventions for water security, evaluation of field test kits for water safety planning, emerging contaminants and environmental laws, water quality challenges in India, and the use of digital tools for tracking water refill stations. The presentations highlighted the need for stronger water quality monitoring, water safety planning, community participation, and technology-enabled approaches.

 

Another session, “Financing, Economic Models & Techno-Economic Solutions,” deliberated on approaches to improving the financial and technological sustainability of water and sanitation services. Four papers covered innovative models for rural water supply, wastewater treatment and cost recovery, local economic models for sustaining rural drinking water services, and low-cost atmospheric water harvesting solutions. The session highlighted the role of appropriate technologies, local economic models, capacity building, and innovative approaches in supporting sustainable water services.

The fourth technical session, “Climate Resilience, Nature-Based Solutions & Sanitation/Other,” focused on approaches for strengthening the resilience of WASH systems in the face of climate-related challenges. Four papers covered digital intelligence and machine learning applications in sewage sludge management, sanitation innovation through start-ups and public-private partnerships, approaches to building water consciousness, and AI-enabled mechanised and robotic operation and maintenance of WASH infrastructure. The discussions highlighted the role of technology, innovation, partnerships and systems strengthening in addressing emerging challenges in water and sanitation.

 

 

*****

 

PS/ND/HM/AK

item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
11th Ayurveda Day 2026: Ayush Institutions Undertake Nationwide Awareness, Wellness and Community Outreach Activities
Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 10:01PM by PIB Delhi

The 11th Ayurveda Day 2026 was observed across the country through a range of public awareness, community outreach, academic, wellness and student engagement activities organised by Ayush institutions.

Central Ayurveda Research Institute (CARI), Jhansi

The Central Ayurveda Research Institute (CARI), Jhansi, conducted Ayurveda pledge and yoga camps, educational visits, cleanliness and medicinal plant drives, “Run for Ayurveda”, webinars, public awareness programmes and competitions in painting, rangoli and quiz. The activities engaged students, youth, staff and the public on Ayurveda, yoga and healthy lifestyles.

 

R.R.A. Podar Central Ayurveda Research Institute (RRAP-CARI), Mumbai

R.R.A. Podar Central Ayurveda Research Institute (RRAP-CARI), Mumbai, conducted a webinar on “Research Innovation, Patenting and Entrepreneurship in Ayurveda”, Ayush wellness programmes for CISF personnel and an Ayurveda Walkathon at Kharghar, with more than 200 participants. The institute also held an Ayurveda Aahar cooking competition, drawing competition for school children, Ayush Food Festival and cleanliness activities, besides distributing more than 100 medicinal plant saplings. The celebrations concluded with a valedictory programme on September 23.

 

Regional Ayurveda Research Institute (RARI), Gangtok

The Regional Ayurveda Research Institute (RARI), Gangtok, observed Ayurveda Day at ICAR, Tadong, with participation from researchers, healthcare professionals and scholars associated with Ayurveda, Homoeopathy, Sowa-Rigpa and other traditional systems. Technical sessions focused on Ayurveda’s role in health and well-being and contemporary healthcare needs, facilitating knowledge sharing among practitioners and scholars of different traditional healthcare systems.

Central Ayurveda Research Institute (CARI), Kolkata

The Central Ayurveda Research Institute (CARI), Kolkata, organised medicinal plant and raw drug exhibitions, yoga demonstrations, IEC distribution, medical camps, an Ayush Aahar Festival and competitions on rangoli, slogans, posters and quizzes. The institute also conducted awareness programmes through Akashvani and Doordarshan and a webinar on geriatric healthcare through Ayurveda. The celebrations concluded with Dhanvantari Puja and a programme focusing on Ayurveda, scientific research, evidence-based healthcare and holistic well-being.

 

Regional Ayurveda Research Institute (RARI), Ahmedabad

The Regional Ayurveda Research Institute (RARI), Ahmedabad, organised public awareness lectures on Ayurveda, healthy lifestyle, diet and disease prevention, along with poster-making and rangoli competitions. An Ayurveda quiz and elocution competition was also held for students in collaboration with Shri Balahnuman Ayurveda College, Lodara and Government Akhandanand Ayurveda College, Ahmedabad. The institute further conducted interactive sessions on Ayurveda and healthy living for staff of the Reserve Bank of India, CISF and ONGC.

 

Regional Ayurveda Research Institute (RARI), Itanagar

The Regional Ayurveda Research Institute (RARI), Itanagar, conducted awareness lectures, a “Selfie with 11th Ayurveda Day” campaign, besides distributing of 134 medicinal plant saplings from September 9 to 23. The institute also organised a health camp, essay competition and herbal garden initiative at PM Shri Kendriya Vidyalaya No. 2, Chimpu, along with a webinar, medicinal plant exhibition and cleanliness drive, engaging students, patients, visitors and the wider community. 

 

Regional Ayurveda Research Institute (RARI), Gwalior

The Regional Ayurveda Research Institute (RARI), Gwalior, organised lectures, public awareness activities, medicinal plant distribution and exhibitions, a “Run for Ayurveda” and other health-promoting activities as part of the 11th Ayurveda Day celebrations. The activities focused on Ayurveda’s role in healthy lifestyles, disease prevention and holistic well-being, with emphasis on integrating Ayurvedic principles with modern scientific research and promoting evidence-based knowledge. The celebrations concluded with Dhanvantari Puja on September 23, with participation from institute officials, scientists, staff and students.

 

North Eastern Institute of Ayurveda and Homoeopathy (NEIAH), Shillong

The North Eastern Institute of Ayurveda and Homoeopathy (NEIAH), Shillong, conducted activities from September 9 to 23, including free health camps, medicinal plant and plantation drives, student outreach, yoga sessions, academic lectures, competitions and public awareness programmes. The programme also featured an Ayush food festival, Open Day, radio talk, medicinal plant awareness campaign and student reel-making competition, culminating in Dhanvantari Puja, a plantation drive and valedictory programme.

 

National Institute of Naturopathy (NIN), Pune

The National Institute of Naturopathy (NIN), Pune, organised a plantation drive at its Nisarg Gram campus. Prof. (Dr.) Geetha Shetty, Director, NIN, inaugurated the drive. Faculty members and experts participated in planting medicinal plants including Bilva, Shatavari, Arjuna, Guduchi and Ghrita Kumari (Aloe vera).

 

Ayurveda Treatment Centre, Safdarjung Hospital, CCRAS-CARI, New Delhi

The Ayurveda Treatment Centre (ATC), Safdarjung Hospital, CCRAS-CARI, New Delhi, organised an academic lecture on “Alternative Systems of Medicine in India” on September 23, 2026, as part of the 11th Ayurveda Day celebrations. Dr. Shivshankar Rajput, In-charge, ATC, Safdarjung Hospital, delivered the lecture for 164 first-year MBBS students and faculty members of VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare.

The session provided an overview of Ayurveda, its fundamental principles and therapeutic approaches, and their relevance in contemporary healthcare. The participants were also sensitised to the role and organisational structure of the Ministry of Ayush, its key initiatives and schemes, major reforms, and ongoing research activities in the field of Ayurveda.

The nationwide activities reflect the focus of Ayush institutions on public health awareness, healthy lifestyles, nutrition, academic engagement, scientific research and community outreach under the theme “Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow.”

***

SR/SV/SG

(Release ID: 2314656)

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Legislative Department Hosts Expert Lecture on “Swachhata Se Samriddhi”
Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 9:48PM by PIB Delhi

 The Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice, organised an expert lecture on “Swachhata se Samriddhi” on 24 September 2026 as part of the Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026, being observed from 17 September 2026 to 2 October 2026, in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation.

The lecture was delivered by Ms. Kulvinder Kour, Director, Jan Shikshan Sansthan, West Delhi, Peeragarhi, along with Mrs. Archana, General Secretary, INDIA-AIDS (NGO), Dwarka, New Delhi, at Kartavya Bhawan-2, New Delhi. The officers and officials of this Department actively participated in the programme.

During the session, the speakers highlighted the importance of cleanliness, sanitation and hygiene in promoting a healthy and dignified life. They emphasised that cleanliness is a collective responsibility that requires sustained participation and behavioural change at the individual, institutional and community levels.

The speakers also elaborated on the broader message of “Swachhata se Samriddhi”, highlighting the interrelationship between cleanliness, health, productivity, dignity and sustainable development. The session sensitised participants towards adopting responsible and sustainable cleanliness practices in their workplaces and daily lives.

The programme provided an opportunity for officers and officials of this Department to reaffirm their commitment to cleanliness and to contribute towards creating clean, healthy and sustainable surroundings.

The Legislative Department is undertaking various activities during the Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026 to promote awareness and encourage active participation in cleanliness and sanitation initiatives, thereby contributing to the vision of a Swachh and Viksit Bharat.

****

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Steel
SAIL’s 54th AGM highlights strong value added steel growth and major nation-building deliveries
Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 9:47PM by PIB Delhi

Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) held its 54th Annual General Meeting (AGM) today on 24.09.2026, in hybrid mode at CSOI, New Delhi. Addressing the shareholders, Chairman & Managing Director Dr. A.K. Panda presented the Company’s performance for FY 2025–26 and outlined its strategic priorities for the years ahead.

SAIL CMD, Dr. Panda noted that despite a challenging global steel environment marked by geopolitical uncertainties and market volatility, India continued to lead global steel demand growth, retaining its position as the world’s fastest growing major steel producer. He stated that, “SAIL demonstrated strong resilience and adaptability, achieving new benchmarks driven by technological upgrades, financial prudence, digitalisation, HR initiatives and sustainability efforts.”

Dr. Panda emphasised that, “SAIL’s performance during the year was marked not only by best-ever crude steel, finished steel and saleable steel production, but also a strong focus towards value creation. The Company produced 10.7 Million Tonnes (MT) of value-added steel, which was 56% of total saleable steel, up by 7% over FY'24-25, and introduced 28 new products across infrastructure, automotive, energy and manufacturing sectors - significantly strengthening SAIL’s ability to meet evolving national and sectoral requirements. He added that this enhanced product capability directly reinforced SAIL’s nation-building role. In FY 2025–26, the Company dispatched the first consignment of indigenously developed Vande Bharat wheels and supplied steel for five Indian Navy ships - INS Arnala, Udaygiri, Himgiri, Androth and Anjadeep - commissioned during the year. Dr. Panda reiterated SAIL’s commitment to contributing to Viksit Bharat 2047, aligned with the National Steel Policy.

Highlighting the Company’s financial performance, Dr. Panda said, “Reflecting operational efficiency, in FY 2025–26 SAIL posted its highest ever revenue, surpassing ₹1,09,000 crore, an 8% increase over the previous year. Borrowings were reduced by more than ₹5,000 crore through judicious fund management. With higher sales volume, lower inventory and reduced borrowings, the Company’s profitability strengthened, and both PBT & PAT improved by 44% and 50.5% respectively. The Board has recommended a Final Dividend of ₹2.35 per equity share.”

Reinforcing the Company’s sustainability focus, CMD shared that SAIL generated 5.61 million units of green power from the first 4 MW floating solar plant at IISCO Steel Plant, with a 20 MW floating solar plant underway at Bhilai Steel Plant. Additionally, 278.5 MW of solar projects are under consideration across various plants. Looking ahead, Dr Panda stated that, “SAIL is focused on expanding crude steel capacity to ~35 MTPA by FY 2030–31, supported by green capacity creation, adoption of low-carbon technologies, digital enablement, enhanced customer engagement, increased share of value-added and special steels, and deeper integration with retail and MSME ecosystems.”

****

AG

Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Highlights India’s Expanding Global Economic Engagement and Growing Integration with Global Value Chain
India’s Semiconductor Demand Expected to Exceed $150 Billion Annually in Five Years: Shri Goyal
India Emerges as World’s Third-Largest Startup Ecosystem with More Than 120 Unicorns: Shri Goyal
Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 9:17PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal highlighted India’s expanding engagement with the global economy and its efforts to strengthen participation in global value chains and supply chains. Addressing the Leadership Dialogue at the 13th PAFI Annual Forum 2026 in New Delhi, Shri Goyal said India is negotiating trade and economic partnerships from the position of an economy that is expected to grow into a $30 trillion economy.

Shri Goyal said India today negotiates with the world as a $4 trillion economy, while its economy on a purchasing power parity basis is around $20 trillion, making it the third largest in the world. He said the gap between these measures would narrow as India progresses towards the vision of becoming a $30 trillion economy.

The Minister said India’s approach to trade negotiations reflects the country’s changing economic position and its objective of strengthening integration with global markets. He highlighted the potential for broader economic partnerships to facilitate seamless flows of goods, services, tourists, educational institutions and sports.

Shri Goyal said ongoing negotiations include engagements with Canada, Chile, Peru, the Southern African Customs Union (SACU), Mexico, Maldives, Eurasia, Central Asia, Russia, the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) and Israel. He said these engagements are aimed at expanding opportunities for India to participate in global value chains and supply chains and facilitating the movement of goods and services.

The Minister said India’s semiconductor consumption demand is expected to grow to over $150 billion annually in the next five years. He also highlighted the need to develop capabilities across the AI ecosystem, including large language models and agentic models.

The Minister also highlighted the growth of India’s startup ecosystem. He said that when Startup India was launched, the country had around 400–500 startups, while India has since become the world’s third-largest startup ecosystem, with more than 120 unicorns.

Shri Goyal said the focus is now on innovation and promoting Indian startups in the deep-tech ecosystem. He also highlighted India’s emergence as the third country to have a rocket launched into space by the private sector.

The Minister said India’s young population is increasingly informed about global developments and opportunities and expressed confidence in the ability of the youth to make informed choices about their future.

***

Abhishek Dayal/Shabbir Azad/Anushka Pandey

item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment NCSC Chairman Shri Kishor Makwana Conducts Spot Inquiry at IIT Bombay in Connection with Death of Scheduled Caste Student Commission Reviews Circumstances Surrounding Death of Shri Sahil Wakode; Directs Preservation and Examination of All Relevant Evidence Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 8:12PM by PIB Delhi The Hon’ble Chairman of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC), Shri Kishor Makwana, today conducted a detailed spot inquiry at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay (IIT Bombay) in connection with the death of Shri…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
NCSC Chairman Shri Kishor Makwana Conducts Spot Inquiry at IIT Bombay in Connection with Death of Scheduled Caste Student
Commission Reviews Circumstances Surrounding Death of Shri Sahil Wakode; Directs Preservation and Examination of All Relevant Evidence
Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 8:12PM by PIB Delhi

The Hon’ble Chairman of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC), Shri Kishor Makwana, today conducted a detailed spot inquiry at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay (IIT Bombay) in connection with the death of Shri Sahil Wakode, a Scheduled Caste student pursuing his second year of B.Tech. in the Department of Energy Science and Engineering.

The visit was undertaken in view of the allegations levelled by the family of the deceased regarding caste-based discrimination, harassment and the circumstances preceding his death. The matter is presently under investigation by the Mumbai Police Crime Branch. The Commission is examining the matter within the framework of the constitutional and statutory safeguards available to members of the Scheduled Castes.

During the visit, the Hon’ble Chairman held a detailed interaction with senior authorities of IIT Bombay, including the Director, Deputy Director, Registrar, concerned faculty members and other officials of the Institute. The Commission sought a comprehensive account of the sequence of events preceding the student’s death, including the incident reported to have occurred during a mid-semester examination on 18 September 2026, when the student was allegedly found involved in academic malpractice.

 

The Commission examined the circumstances in which the student was questioned during the examination, the procedure reportedly followed thereafter, the role of the concerned faculty and Institute authorities, and the institutional mechanisms available for addressing student grievances and safeguarding the welfare and rights of students belonging to Scheduled Castes.

The Hon’ble Chairman emphasized that all relevant records and material connected with the matter, including CCTV footage, electronic evidence, official communications, examination-related records and other documentary material, should be preserved and made available to the investigating authorities in accordance with law, so that the circumstances surrounding the student’s death can be established on the basis of evidence.

As part of the spot inquiry, Shri Kishor Makwana personally visited the Department of Energy Science and Engineering, where Shri Sahil Wakode was pursuing his studies. The Chairman also inspected the classroom/examination hall where the reported examination incident took place and sought information regarding the sequence of events during and immediately after the examination.

The Commission thereafter visited the hostel premises and the room occupied by the deceased student. The Hon’ble Chairman also interacted with classmates and fellow students of Shri Sahil Wakode to understand his academic and campus experience and to obtain information regarding the circumstances and events preceding his death. The Commission is seeking to consider such inputs along with official records and the findings of the ongoing investigation.

Following the spot inquiry at IIT Bombay, the Hon’ble Chairman held a high-level meeting with senior police authorities, including the Director General of Police, Commissioner of Police and senior officers associated with the investigation, including officers of the Crime Branch.

During the meeting, the Commission reviewed the status and progress of the investigation and sought details regarding the FIR, collection and preservation of evidence, CCTV footage, examination of witnesses and other relevant aspects of the case.

The Hon’ble Chairman directed the investigating authorities to ensure that the investigation is fair, impartial, comprehensive and expeditious, and that every relevant allegation and circumstance is examined strictly on the basis of available evidence and in accordance with law.

The police authorities were further asked to ensure proper collection, preservation and examination of all relevant documentary, electronic, forensic and testimonial evidence. The Commission also emphasized the need for recording the statements of students, faculty members, Institute officials and other persons who may possess relevant information, wherever required in accordance with law.

The Hon’ble Chairman directed the concerned authorities to furnish a detailed Action Taken/Investigation Report to the National Commission for Scheduled Castes at the earliest, for further examination by the Commission.

The Hon’ble Chairman subsequently met the parents and other family members of Shri Sahil Wakode and heard their grievances and concerns in detail. The family placed before the Commission their allegations regarding the circumstances preceding the death of the student and submitted a written complaint seeking appropriate intervention by the Commission.

Shri Makwana assured the family that the Commission would examine the matter in accordance with its constitutional and statutory mandate. The Commission will closely monitor the progress of the investigation and take appropriate action within its jurisdiction based on the facts and evidence that emerge.

The Commission reiterated that the constitutional and statutory safeguards available to members of the Scheduled Castes must be effectively protected and that institutions must maintain appropriate mechanisms for ensuring dignity, equality, non-discrimination, student welfare and effective grievance redressal.

The Commission also emphasized the importance of maintaining social harmony and cohesion while ensuring that all allegations are examined objectively, transparently and in accordance with due process.

The Hon’ble Chairman was accompanied by Dr. Sunil Kumar Babu, Director, NCSC State Office, Maharashtra; Dr. R. Stalin, Deputy Director, Atrocities & Protection of Civil Rights (APCR) Wing, NCSC Headquarters, New Delhi; and officials of the NCSC State Office.

*******

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
​​​​​​​MoS Shri Harsh Malhotra flags off Youth Safety & Smart Mobility Expedition 2026
Calls for greater awareness and responsible road behaviour to strengthen road safety
Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 8:10PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State for Road Transport & Highways Shri Harsh Malhotra today flagged off the Youth Safety & Smart Mobility Expedition 2026 from Transport Bhawan, New Delhi. Organised by the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PHDCCI) and JK Tyre, the expedition, involving a convoy of electric vehicles travelling towards Chandigarh, aims to sensitise youth about road safety, responsible driving behaviour and smart mobility.

On the occasion, Shri Mahmood Ahmed, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Road Transport & Highways; Dr. Ranjeet Mehta, CEO & Secretary General, PHDCCI; and Mr. B. S. Dagar, Vice President & Group Head – ER, EHS & CSR, POWERGRID, along with senior representatives from the Government and industry, were also present.

Addressing the participants, Shri Harsh Malhotra congratulated them for undertaking the expedition for the important cause of road safety. He emphasised that making roads safer requires continuous efforts across multiple dimensions, including responsible behaviour by road users, adherence to traffic rules, road engineering, timely assistance to accident victims and maintaining vehicles in good condition.

The Minister said that road safety is an important priority and requires collective efforts, as road accidents and fatalities continue to remain a major concern. He stressed that road users must follow the legal framework and traffic rules, as violations increase the risk of accidents.

Shri Harsh Malhotra highlighted the importance of providing timely assistance to accident victims during the golden hour. He said that under the PM-RAHAT scheme, efforts are being made to ensure that accident victims are taken to hospitals during the critical golden hour. He also highlighted the availability of technically equipped ambulances, including arrangements at toll centres, to provide necessary assistance in emergencies.

The Minister also underlined the importance of identifying and rectifying black spots corridors. He said that continuous introspection is undertaken to identify such corridors and take corrective measures. He added that engineering and structural interventions are undertaken wherever necessary, including correction of curves, turns and other road-related deficiencies, particularly at locations witnessing repeated accidents.

Emphasising the role of individual responsibility, Shri Harsh Malhotra said that people driving vehicles should ensure that their vehicles remain in good condition so that accidents do not occur due to vehicle-related issues. He said that road safety has several dimensions and awareness among young people can play an important role in addressing them. He appraised the gathering about the youth centric initiative of the Ministry - Sadak Suraksha Mitra which sensitized the youths about the road safety by transforming their behaviour on the road and also extend supporting hand to the road accident victims and become Raah-Veer.

The Minister appreciated the objective of the expedition to sensitise youth towards road safety and responsible behaviour. He observed that an individual's mistake on the road can put not only their own life but also the life of another road user at risk. He said that awareness initiatives such as the expedition can help reinforce the message that safe movement on roads is a shared responsibility.

Shri Harsh Malhotra also highlighted the importance of smart and electric mobility as part of the transition towards alternative fuels. He said that the Government is continuously promoting electric vehicles and supporting the development of alternative-fuel technologies.

Referring to the evolution of electric vehicles, the Minister said that the range of electric vehicles has increased significantly, from around 150–200 kilometres earlier to about 350–400 kilometres today on a single charge. He also referred to innovations such as flash charging in electric buses, stressing that technological advancements in the sector are continuing.

The Minister said that the Government is working with industry to facilitate the adoption of the latest and world-class innovations in India. He also highlighted the need to strengthen battery manufacturing and assembly in the country and said that the Government is ready to provide necessary facilities to industry in this regard.

Shri Harsh Malhotra said that the transition towards alternative fuels is important in the context of the country's goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2070. He emphasised that the transition requires continuous efforts to address technological and other challenges.

The expedition comprises a convoy of around 50–60 electric vehicles travelling along the approximately 500-kilometre New Delhi–Chandigarh corridor. Participants are being encouraged to act as road safety ambassadors, carrying the message of responsible road behaviour and safer mobility during the journey.

The expedition will include interactions with youth and stakeholders along the route, focusing on responsible driving behaviour, road discipline, road safety and electric mobility.

***

GDH/DS/HJ

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
INS SUDARSHINI ARRIVES AT ALEXANDRIA, EGYPT DURING LOKAYAN 26
Three-masted barque makes second visit to Alexandria during 10-month transoceanic expedition
Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 7:40PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Navy’s Sail Training Ship INS Sudarshini arrived at the historic port city of Alexandria, Egypt, on 23 Sep 2026, as part of her ongoing Lokayan 26 transoceanic expedition. The port call marks the ship’s second visit to Alexandria during the deployment.

The 10-month expedition commenced from Kochi on 20 Jan 2026(https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2216522&reg=3&lang=1), with INS Sudarshini scheduled to cover approximately 22,000 nautical miles across 18 ports in 13 countries. Since embarking on the voyage, the three-masted barque has traversed the Arabian Sea, Red Sea and Mediterranean, undertaken a transit of the Suez Canal and participated in the prestigious Escale à Sète maritime festival in France.

The ship subsequently undertook the historic first Atlantic crossing by INS Sudarshini, arriving at Antigua on 27 May 2026 after a 19-day passage from Cape Verde. During the passage, the ship crossed the milestone of 10,000 nautical miles since departing Kochi (https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2266274&reg=3&lang=1 ) . The ship subsequently sailed to the Azores and Portugal, with her arrival at Lisbon on 22 Aug 2026 marking her 15th port visit in seven months              (https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2302441&reg=48&lang=2 ).

During the ongoing voyage, the trainees have gained extensive exposure to long-range ocean navigation and traditional seamanship. The Mediterranean passage has provided further hands-on experience in open-sea manoeuvring, sail handling and traditional seamanship.

On arrival at Alexandria, INS Sudarshini was received by Rear Admiral Mohamed Abdel Aziz, Commander, Alexandria Naval Base, along with representatives of the Embassy of India. The port call will include courtesy calls, cross-deck visits and professional interactions with the Egyptian Navy, providing opportunities for professional exchange and further strengthening the maritime ties between India and Egypt.

Lokayan 26 represents the Indian Navy’s continued commitment to professional training, maritime outreach and strengthening bonds of friendship and cooperation with partner nations. Through the deployment, INS Sudarshini has served as a floating ambassador of India’s rich seafaring heritage, carrying the message of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam and the vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) across the oceans.

****

 

VM/AS

item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment NBCFDC Supports Entrepreneurship and Education Among Backward Classes Concessional Individual Loans of up to ₹25 Lakh Available for Income Generating Activities Education Loans Up To ₹25 Lakh Available At A Beneficiary Interest Rate Of 8% Per Annum, With A Repayment Period Of Up To 10 Years Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 7:24PM by PIB Delhi The National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), a Government of India undertaking under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, provides concessional financial…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
NBCFDC Supports Entrepreneurship and Education Among Backward Classes
Concessional Individual Loans of up to ₹25 Lakh Available for Income Generating Activities
Education Loans Up To ₹25 Lakh Available At A Beneficiary Interest Rate Of 8% Per Annum, With A Repayment Period Of Up To 10 Years
Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 7:24PM by PIB Delhi

The National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), a Government of India undertaking under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, provides concessional financial assistance to eligible members of Backward Classes through State Channelizing Agencies and banks.

A Senior Official in the Corporation informed that members of notified Other Backward Classes with an annual family income of up to ₹5 lakh may seek assistance for activities with the potential to generate sustainable income, subject to the applicable eligibility requirements and the channel partner’s processes.

He said under the Individual Loan Scheme, assistance can cover up to 85% of project cost, with a maximum loan of ₹25 lakh per beneficiary. Loans of up to ₹1.25 lakh carry a beneficiary interest rate of 7% per annum, while loans above ₹1.25 lakh and up to ₹25 lakh carry a rate of 8% per annum, he added.

The NBCFDC Official said that education loans of up to ₹25 lakh are available at a beneficiary interest rate of 8% per annum, with a repayment period of up to 10 years inclusive of the moratorium period, as per the conditions prescribed by NBCFDC.

He said the Corporation promotes economic and developmental activities, skill development and self-employment, which was incorporated on January 13, 1992,

The NBCFDC Official further said that the Group Loan Scheme provides assistance to self-help groups of up to ₹25 lakh per group, subject to a limit of ₹1.25 lakh per beneficiary adding that loans through State Channelizing Agencies or banks can cover up to 90% of project cost at a beneficiary interest rate of 7% per annum. He added that at least 60% of the group’s members must belong to Backward Classes; the other members may belong to eligible weaker sections.

It is pertinent to mention that NBCFDC’s published pattern of finance provides for an annual timely payment rebate of 1%, shared equally between the channel partner and beneficiary. Eligible applicants can approach the relevant channel partner in their district or submit a request through the registration portal on the NBCFDC website.

For scheme details and applications, the interested applicants may visit www.nbcfdc.gov.in/nbcfdc/web/.

item.description: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare FSSAI proposes draft amendment to ensure only milk-derived products are represented as ‘Paneer’ FSSAI Moves to Curb Misleading Marketing of Analogue Products as ‘Paneer’, Proposes Ban on Use of ‘Paneer’ Term for Non-Milk-Derived Products Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 7:23PM by PIB Delhi The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has proposed a draft amendment to the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations, 2011, to restrict the manufacture and sale of analogue products as “Paneer” and…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
FSSAI proposes draft amendment to ensure only milk-derived products are represented as ‘Paneer’
FSSAI Moves to Curb Misleading Marketing of Analogue Products as ‘Paneer’, Proposes Ban on Use of ‘Paneer’ Term for Non-Milk-Derived Products
Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 7:23PM by PIB Delhi

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has proposed a draft amendment to the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations, 2011, to restrict the manufacture and sale of analogue products as “Paneer” and prevent consumers from being misled about the nature and composition of such products.

The proposed Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Amendment Regulations, 2026 seek to insert a new clause under Regulation 2.1.1 of the existing regulations, specifically covering “paneer made of constituents not derived from milk.”

Under the proposed amendment, products already licensed or registered under the ‘Analogue in Dairy Context’ category would be required to discontinue the use of the term “Paneer” in their nomenclature, labelling or marketing.

The proposed amendment is aimed at ensuring that the nomenclature and presentation of food products accurately reflect their nature and composition, thereby enabling consumers to make informed choices.

As the notification is a draft regulation, FSSAI has invited objections and suggestions from stakeholders and members of the public. The draft regulations will be taken into consideration after the expiry of 60 days from the date on which copies of the Official Gazette containing the notification are made available to the public.

Objections or suggestions may be addressed to the Chief Executive Officer, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), FDA Bhawan, Kotla Road, New Delhi – 110002, or submitted through the email address specified in the notification.

The proposed amendment has been issued by FSSAI with the previous approval of the Central Government under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The principal Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations were notified in 2011 and have been amended from time to time.

The Official Gazette of the notification can be accessed through this link: https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2026/276430.pdf

*****

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Defence
item.description: Ministry of Defence DRDO inks first high-value deep tech project agreement with a start-up under TDF scheme for indigenous development of 20 mK Dilution Refrigerator for Quantum Applications Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 7:15PM by PIB Delhi Under the Technology Development Fund (TDF) scheme, Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) has signed the first high-value deep tech project agreement with the Industry (Start-up) Zero mK India Private Limited towards collaborative effort for indigenous development of a 20 mK Dilution Refrigerator for Quantum Applications.…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
DRDO inks first high-value deep tech project agreement with a start-up under TDF scheme for indigenous development of 20 mK Dilution Refrigerator for Quantum Applications
Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 7:15PM by PIB Delhi

Under the Technology Development Fund (TDF) scheme, Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) has signed the first high-value deep tech project agreement with the Industry (Start-up) Zero mK India Private Limited towards collaborative effort for indigenous development of a 20 mK Dilution Refrigerator for Quantum Applications. The signing of the agreement took place between Director, TDF and Zero mK India Private Limited, Alwar, Rajasthan in New Delhi. It is the first high value agreement under the Rs 500 crore corpus which was earlier approved by Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh for deep-tech and cutting-edge projects.

Dilution refrigerators are specialised cryogenic systems capable of achieving extremely low temperatures in the millikelvin range. Such ultra-low-temperature environment is essential for the operation and testing of several quantum computing platforms and associated quantum technologies. 

The indigenous development of 20 mK-class dilution refrigerator aligns with the National Quantum Mission and strengthens India’s capabilities in quantum technology, advanced cryogenics and strategic technologies, contributing towards a self-reliant, quantum-ready ecosystem. This will contribute towards reducing dependence on imported cryogenic infrastructure and strengthening the domestic quantum technology ecosystem.

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has complimented DRDO, industry and all stakeholders associated with this important project. He expressed confidence that the partnership will set an important precedent for future DRDO-Industry collaborations in emerging technology domains.

Congratulating the teams associated with the initiative, Defence Secretary and Secretary, Department of Defence R&D and Chairman, DRDO Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh wished them success in achieving the project objectives.

Director General, Micro Electronic Devices & Computational System and Cyber Security (DG MCC); Director General, Technology Management (DG TM); Director, Solid State Physics Laboratory (SSPL), and other stakeholders were present on the occasion. The project is being monitored, mentored and supported by Director, SSPL and his team.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
Indo-Africa Roundtable on WASH Held as part of Second India International WASH Conference During 9th IIWW 2026
The Roundtable Brings Together Ambassadors of 22 African Countries, International Delegates and Scientists to Explore Opportunities For Collaboration In WASH
The Deliberation Focus on knowledge exchange, capacity building, digital innovation, community-led service delivery and climate-resilient WASH solutions
Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 7:07PM by PIB Delhi

As part of the Second India International WASH Conference being organised during the 9th India International Water Week (IIWW) 2026, the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India, today convened a high-level Indo-Africa Roundtable on Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi to deliberate on shared water and sanitation challenges and explore opportunities for future cooperation.

The roundtable brought together Ambassadors and representatives of 22 African countries, senior officials of the Government of India, development partners, international organisations. AICTE-affiliated engineering students from the National Capital Region are called to witness the deliberations.

Setting the Context Shri Ashok K. K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS, highlighted that India's experience in rural water supply and sanitation extends beyond physical infrastructure and is fundamentally about public health, dignity, women's empowerment and community ownership. He emphasised that strong political commitment and local institutional ownership have been central to India's progress under the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) and Swachh Bharat Mission-Gramin (SBM-G). Drawing attention to the decentralised governance framework adopted in India, he underlined the critical role played by Gram Panchayats and Village Water and Sanitation Committees in planning, operation, monitoring and sustainability of rural services.

Shri Meena further highlighted that over 2.48 million women have been trained in the use of Field Testing Kits for water-quality surveillance, making women active participants in local water governance. He also recalled the transformative impact of Swachh Bharat Mission-Gramin, which converted sanitation into a nationwide people's movement through behavioural change, local leadership and community participation. Emphasising the importance of sustainability, he outlined five key lessons from India's experience: strong political leadership, empowered local governments, investment in people alongside infrastructure, planning for operation and maintenance from the outset, and the use of simple and interoperable digital systems for accountability and service delivery.

Secretary DDWS, said that India is honored to share its operational knowledge, digital approaches and experience in community governance, while learning from innovations and experiences emerging across Africa. The objective of this deliberation is to learn from one another and strengthen approaches that can deliver safe water, dignified sanitation and resilient services for communities. Such cooperation can contribute meaningfully to the achievement of Sustainable Development Goal 6.

Presenting India's experience in rural drinking-water service delivery, Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Additional Secretary and Mission Director, National Jal Jeevan Mission, highlighted the unprecedented scale of investments made that shows political will. Launch of Jal Jeevan Mission on 15 August 2019 marked a decisive shift towards ensuring functional tap-water connections for every rural household. The experience has reinforced the importance of political commitment, public investment, coordinated implementation and community participation.  He noted that these lessons can contribute to the wider exchange of knowledge among countries seeking to strengthen reliable and sustainable rural water services. He presented that tap-water coverage has increased from 32.4 million rural households in 2019 to over 159.4 million households today and explained how the Mission has addressed long-standing challenges of limited piped-water supply, non-functional schemes, excessive dependence on groundwater and water-quality concerns through a combination of infrastructure development, source sustainability measures, water-quality monitoring and community participation.

He informed that India's rural water-management strategy is increasingly focused on sustainability, including a gradual shift from groundwater dependence towards greater utilisation of surface-water sources. He also showcased Sujalam Bharat, India's emerging Digital Public Infrastructure for rural water governance, which aims to provide source-to-tap visibility, digital asset mapping, data-driven governance and improved service management through a common interoperable digital backbone.

Presenting India's sanitation journey, Ms. Aishvarya Singh, Joint Secretary and Mission Director, Swachh Bharat Mission-Gramin, highlighted how the the Mission transformed sanitation into a peoples’ movement through unprecedented community participation and behavioural change. She noted that more than 120 million household toilets have been constructed since 2014, helping India achieve universal sanitation coverage and attain SDG target 6.2 ahead of schedule.

She stated that SBM-G has now moved beyond toilet construction towards sustainable rural sanitation service delivery. The current focus includes solid and liquid waste management, visual cleanliness, ODF Plus Model Villages, digital monitoring systems and institutional mechanisms for regular assessment of sanitation services. She also highlighted recent initiatives such as Swachh Seva Aandolan and efforts to institutionalise sanitation service delivery through local governments, digital systems and community-led verification. Stressing the importance of behaviour change, she observed that sanitation outcomes can be sustained only when communities themselves become custodians of cleanliness and public-health gains.

Delivering the global perspective, Mr. Saroj Kumar Jha, Global Director-Water, World Bank, described India's water and sanitation transformation as one of the most significant examples of large-scale development change witnessed across developing countries. He observed that strong political leadership, institutional coordination, innovative financing, public investment and community participation were key factors behind the success.

Highlighting the global water-security challenge, he noted that billions of people worldwide continue to lack access to safe water and sanitation services. He emphasised that water security is fundamental to economic growth, employment generation, prosperity and social stability. He called for greater global investments in water and sanitation, stronger political commitment and enhanced partnerships, while also emphasising that Africa should be viewed not only through the lens of challenges but also as a source of innovation, enterprise and locally developed solutions. He welcomed the India-Africa dialogue and advocated for continued engagement and institutionalised cooperation between the two regions.

Representatives from the World Bank, World Health Organization (WHO), UNICEF, Sanitation and Water for All (SWA) and BISAG-N shared international experiences, innovations and best practices in WASH service delivery. Discussions highlighted the increasing role of digital technologies, geospatial tools, community institutions, water-quality surveillance, climate resilience and evidence-based policymaking in strengthening water and sanitation systems. Participants also emphasised the importance of partnerships among governments, communities, development organisations and technology institutions for achieving sustainable WASH outcomes.

Mr. Yvan J.-F. Hutin, representing the World Health Organization (WHO), underscored the close links between safe drinking water, sanitation and public health outcomes, and highlighted the importance of water-quality surveillance, preventive health measures and resilient WASH systems. Mr. Paulos Workneh, Chief WASH, India, UNICEF, shared experiences on community-centred service delivery, behaviour change, inclusion and strengthening WASH services for women, children and vulnerable populations. Ms. Ruchika Shiva, Director, Global & Asia Regional Programme, Sanitation and Water for All (SWA), emphasised the importance of multi-stakeholder partnerships, country-led action, accountability and collaborative approaches for achieving universal access to water and sanitation. Dr. Vinay Thakur, Director General, BISAG-N, showcased the use of geospatial technologies, GIS-based planning and digital mapping solutions for monitoring water infrastructure, improving asset management and enabling data-driven decision-making in the WASH sector. Collectively, the speakers highlighted the growing role of digital innovation, climate resilience, community participation and evidence-based governance in strengthening sustainable WASH systems.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Shivala Naik Mude, Additional Secretary, Ministry of External Affairs, highlighted India's longstanding development partnership with African countries and reaffirmed the country's commitment to supporting Africa through infrastructure development, institutional capacity building and knowledge exchange. He noted that Digital Public Infrastructure, water-resource management and technical cooperation present significant opportunities for future India-Africa collaboration. Recalling the historical and civilisational ties between India and Africa, he emphasised the importance of working together as partners of the Global South to address common development challenges.

During the interactive session, Ambassadors and representatives of African countries shared experiences and perspectives on water security, sanitation, irrigation, climate resilience and sustainable infrastructure development in their countries. They acknowledged India's achievements in expanding access to drinking water and sanitation and highlighted several common priorities, including water harvesting, groundwater management, wastewater treatment and reuse, source sustainability, affordable water-treatment technologies, waste management, digital water governance and climate-resilient infrastructure.

The discussions underscored the need for practical, affordable and locally adaptable solutions, particularly for rural, drought-prone and underserved communities. African representatives also highlighted the importance of sustainable financing, effective operation and maintenance systems, institutional capacity building, private sector participation and development of local technical skills. Several participants expressed interest in pursuing government-to-government cooperation, technical exchanges, pilot projects, research partnerships, academic collaboration and exposure visits to facilitate knowledge sharing and technology transfer.

The day started with welcoming the participants by Shri D. Senthil Pandian, Joint Secretary, DDWS. He called the roundtable as an important platform for strengthening cooperation among countries facing similar development challenges. Highlighting the global water challenge, he observed that access to safe drinking water is not merely an infrastructure issue but one of dignity, health and opportunity. Referring to India's experience under the Jal

In her concluding remarks, Smt. Swati Meena Naik, Joint Secretary, DDWS, said that the deliberations reaffirmed a common understanding that safe drinking water, sanitation and hygiene are fundamental to public health, dignity, gender equality and sustainable development.                                                                                                                                                                            

Focusing on the way forward, she stated that the deliberations had opened new avenues for India-Africa cooperation in water security and sanitation. She highlighted knowledge exchange, capacity building, water-quality management, digital public infrastructure for WASH, community-led governance, climate-resilient water systems and sustainable sanitation as priority areas for future engagement. She further noted that SPM-NIWAS could support this cooperation through training programmes, exposure visits and technical exchanges. Emphasising a partnership-based approach, she stated that the objective would be to jointly develop affordable, scalable and locally adaptable solutions for achieving sustainable WASH outcomes.

 

Jeevan Mission and Swachh Bharat Mission, he emphasised that long-term sustainability of water and sanitation services can only be achieved when communities themselves become active stakeholders and owners of the assets created. He underlined the importance of collective action and knowledge sharing at a time when the global community is working towards achieving Sustainable Development Goal 6 on Clean Water and Sanitation for All by 2030.

The roundtable concludes with a deepen India-Africa cooperation through sustained engagement, mutual learning and practical partnerships. The deliberations reaffirmed the importance of South-South cooperation in accelerating progress towards safe water, dignified sanitation and climate-resilient WASH services for all.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Waste Picking to Greater Financial Security
Andhra Pradesh’s Chevuri Anjaneyulu’s Story
Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 6:15PM by PIB Delhi

Assistance under the Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY) component of the NAMASTE scheme has helped Shri Chevuri Anjaneyulu, a waste picker in Guntur, Andhra Pradesh, earn additional income and improve his family’s financial security. He  had spent seven years working to support his wife and two children.

A 25-year-old member of the Scheduled Tribe community, Mr. Anjaneyulu began accompanying his parents in waste-picking work at an early age. Financial hardship kept him from attending school. He has also faced social discrimination and lived with limited access to basic amenities and services.

Before the assistance, his income from waste picking made it difficult to meet household expenses and plan for his children’s future. He aspired to improve the family’s living conditions and provide his children with a good education.

On 19 June 2023, Shri Anjaneyulu and three other members received support for a group project under SUY through the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation. The total project cost was Rs 35 lakh, comprising a loan of Rs 17.5 lakh and an upfront capital subsidy of Rs 17.5 lakh.

The assistance enabled him to strengthen his livelihood. He now earns approximately Rs 10,000 more per month through the scheme, helping the family meet its expenses more comfortably.

His two children are studying at an English-medium private school. The additional income has helped him support their education and work towards the better opportunities he had long hoped to provide.

For Shri Anjaneyulu, this support has meant greater economic stability and a more secure future for his family. His experience shows how access to livelihood assistance can help waste pickers improve their income and pursue their aspirations.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
Keralam’s Cultural Mementos Up for Auction at PM Mementos e-Auction 2026
A collection spanning traditional crafts, performing arts, maritime traditions and spiritual heritage
Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 6:13PM by PIB Delhi

A diverse selection of 32 mementos from Keralam is being offered at the PM Mementos e-Auction 2026, bringing together the state’s art, craftsmanship, performing traditions and cultural heritage. The collection features distinctive pieces ranging from a traditional Nettoor Petti and a miniature Chundan Vallam to Kathakali and Theyyam artefacts, Keralam mural art and a handcrafted model of the historic Beypore Uru.

The Orange Nettoor Petti - Keralam Traditional Jewel Box with Mural Art and Brass Detailing describes the Nettoor Petti as having been historically used in aristocratic households to store ornaments and sacred objects, reflecting the traditional craftsmanship associated with this form.

Keralam’s maritime traditions find representation in a finely crafted Chundan Vallam, the traditional snake boat associated with the state’s backwaters and the boat races of the Onam festival. Another notable piece is a miniature Beypore Uru, a traditional wooden maritime dhow. The model was handcrafted by the National Skill Training Institute (NSTI), Calicut, under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and replicates the wooden dhows traditionally built by master carpenters of Beypore.

 

The collection features several representations of Keralam’s performing arts. A Kathakali dancer display doll and a print of a Kathakali performer depict elements of the classical dance-drama, including its elaborate makeup, costumes, ornaments and headgear.

Another distinctive piece is the Bhairavan Theyyam Ritual Art Sculpture, representing Bhairavan Theyyam, described in the collection as an iconic manifestation of Lord Shiva from the ritualistic dance-art tradition of North Keralam. The sculpture features the characteristic headgear, facial makeup, breastplates and traditional attire associated with the form.

Kerala’s mural tradition is represented by a framed painting of Radha, Krishna and a Gopika, created by artists at the Institute of Mural Painting, Guruvayur Devaswom. The artwork depicts Lord Krishna playing the flute beneath a banyan tree, with Radha and a Gopika and is executed on a specially prepared cement sheet using the traditional five-colour Panchavarna formula.

 

 

The collection also includes works associated with Kerala’s spiritual and social heritage. These include a devotional portrait of Adi Shankaracharya, a carved wooden plaque featuring Sivagiri Mutt Commemorative Carved Wooden Temple, a framed print of Poykayil Sree Kumara Gurudevan and a framed photograph of Sree Vidyadhiraja Chattambi Swamikal.

A framed commemorative artwork marking 100 Years of Vaikom Satyagraha is also part of the collection. Other pieces include a traditional Nettipattam, a Kerala brass Vastu Vilakku, a carved wooden statue of Lord Guruvayurappan, a traditional Shankhu (conch) memento and many more.

The 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction 2026, live until 2 October 2026, brings together mementos representing Kerala’s rich cultural heritage and traditions. For auction dates, participation details and the complete catalogue, visit the official PM Mementos e-Auction portal: pmmementos.gov.in

item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
Sowa Rigpa Has Significant Potential in Education, Research and Healthcare: Ayush Secretary, Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha
Three-Day National Workshop in Leh Explores Opportunities and Challenges for Sowa Rigpa in Post-Recognition Era
Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 6:08PM by PIB Delhi

Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, has called for greater focus on education, research, healthcare, documentation and standardisation to further strengthen Sowa Rigpa and expand its recognition at the national and international levels.

He was addressing the valedictory function of the three-day National Workshop on the “Scope and Challenges of Sowa Rigpa Post-Recognition”, organised by the National Institute of Sowa Rigpa (NISR), Leh, at the New Academic Building, Saboo Thang, Leh.

Highlighting the growing scope and global relevance of traditional systems of medicine, Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha said that Sowa Rigpa has significant opportunities in education, research, healthcare, documentation and standardisation. He also emphasised the importance of wider recognition of the system at the national and international levels.

Encouraging students and young scholars of Sowa Rigpa, the Secretary urged them to approach emerging challenges with confidence, dedication and innovation. He encouraged them to “keep the sky as the limit” and explore new possibilities that can contribute to the advancement of Sowa Rigpa.

The workshop brought together experts, scholars, practitioners, administrators, students and other stakeholders from different parts of the Himalayan region to deliberate on the evolving scope, opportunities and challenges of Sowa Rigpa following its recognition as a system of medicine.

The technical sessions focused on institutional development, education, research, healthcare practices, preservation of traditional knowledge, standardisation, and emerging opportunities and challenges in the post-recognition era. The deliberations provided a platform for interaction and exchange of ideas among stakeholders and contributed to strengthening the academic, professional and institutional framework of Sowa Rigpa.

The programme was also organised as part of the National Ayurveda Day celebrations, providing an opportunity to highlight the rich heritage and contemporary relevance of India’s diverse traditional systems of medicine.

Dr. Padma Gurmet, Director, National Institute of Sowa Rigpa, welcomed Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha and expressed gratitude for his continued support towards the preservation and promotion of Sowa Rigpa.

Dr. Tenzin Kunphel, Chairman, Central Council of Tibetan Medicine (CCTM), Dharamsala; Dr. Dorje Damdul, Associate Professor and Dean, Faculty of Sowa Rigpa and Bhot Jyotish, Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Sarnath, Varanasi; and Dr. Phunsok Wangchuk, former Director, Health and Ayush, UT Ladakh, were among the distinguished dignitaries present on the occasion.

The dignitaries shared their experiences and perspectives on the development of Sowa Rigpa and its academic and research potential.

Following the valedictory function, participants visited the Trans-Himalayan Herbal Garden at Phey. They observed various medicinal plants cultivated and conserved in the garden, gaining practical exposure to the rich medicinal plant diversity of the Trans-Himalayan region. The visit complemented the academic deliberations of the workshop.
