item.title: ‘Bharat Taxi’ service launched in Uttar Pradesh; service also rolled out in Gorakhpur, Varanasi, Kanpur and Prayagraj along with Lucknow
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Cooperation
item.description: Ministry of Cooperation ‘Bharat Taxi’ service launched in Uttar Pradesh; service also rolled out in Gorakhpur, Varanasi, Kanpur and Prayagraj along with Lucknow ‘Mukhyamantri Krishak Samriddhi Yojana’ portal, Urvarak Setu mobile app and UPCDC mobile app of the Uttar Pradesh Cooperative Database Centre also launched Airport Authority, Lucknow Metro Rail and Lucknow Police sign Memoranda of Understanding with Bharat Taxi Cooperative sector continues to expand under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahkar Se Samriddhi’ and the leadership of Union Home and Cooperation Minister Shri…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Cooperation
‘Bharat Taxi’ service launched in Uttar Pradesh; service also rolled out in Gorakhpur, Varanasi, Kanpur and Prayagraj along with Lucknow
‘Mukhyamantri Krishak Samriddhi Yojana’ portal, Urvarak Setu mobile app and UPCDC mobile app of the Uttar Pradesh Cooperative Database Centre also launched
Airport Authority, Lucknow Metro Rail and Lucknow Police sign Memoranda of Understanding with Bharat Taxi
Cooperative sector continues to expand under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahkar Se Samriddhi’ and the leadership of Union Home and Cooperation Minister Shri Amit Shah: Shri Murlidhar Mohol
Based on the principle of “Driver is the Owner”, Bharat Taxi will make Saarthis the real stakeholders of their own service through the cooperative model: Union Minister of State for Cooperation Shri Murlidhar Mohol
More than 10 lakh Saarthis have joined Bharat Taxi in six months; around 20,000 rides being completed every day and more than Rs 100 crore credited to Saarthis’ accounts: Shri Mohol
Ministry of Cooperation has launched more than 160 new initiatives during the last five years: Shri Mohol
Computerisation of around 80,000 PACS underway across the country at a cost of approximately Rs 3,000 crore
Around 54 lakh new cooperative members enrolled in Uttar Pradesh; PACS membership campaign described as a model worth emulating across the country
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 6:31PM by PIB Delhi

Guided by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahkar Se Samriddhi’ and under the leadership and guidance of Union Home and Cooperation Minister Shri Amit Shah, a series of significant initiatives have been undertaken over the past few years to make India’s cooperative sector modern, transparent, technology-enabled and multidimensional. Cooperation is steadily expanding beyond its traditional domains into agriculture, rural economy, organic products, seeds, exports, storage, healthcare services and now emerging sectors such as mobility. Taking this vision forward, Union Minister of State for Cooperation Shri Murlidhar Mohol today addressed the formal launch programme of Bharat Taxi in Lucknow. Along with Lucknow, the service was also launched today in Gorakhpur, Varanasi, Kanpur and Prayagraj. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath, Deputy Chief Minister Shri Brajesh Pathak, Agriculture Minister Shri Surya Pratap Shahi, Cooperation Minister Shri J.P.S. Rathore, Transport Minister Shri Dayashankar Singh, Chairman of Uttar Pradesh Cooperative Gram Vikas Bank Shri Vivek Singh Tomar, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Cooperation, Shri Pankaj Bansal, advisers to the Chief Minister, senior officers of the Uttar Pradesh Government, public representatives and a large number of Bharat Taxi Saarthis were present on the occasion. More than 50,000 people from different districts of Uttar Pradesh also joined the programme through the online mode.

During the programme, Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath launched the ‘Mukhyamantri Krishak Samriddhi Yojana’ Portal. Along with this, the Urvarak Setu Mobile App, developed by the Cooperation Department of Uttar Pradesh, and the UPCDC Mobile App of the Uttar Pradesh Cooperative Database Centre were also launched. On the occasion, the Airport Authority, Lucknow Metro Rail and Lucknow Police exchanged Memoranda of Understanding with Bharat Taxi.

Recalling the establishment of a separate Ministry of Cooperation in July 2021, Shri Mohol underlined that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s historic decision gave a new direction and renewed momentum to the cooperative movement in the country. Under the leadership of Union Home and Cooperation Minister Shri Amit Shah, the Ministry of Cooperation has launched more than 160 new initiatives during the last five years, aimed at making cooperative institutions stronger, transparent, modern and economically capable. Highlighting the scale and reach of the movement, he noted that India today has around 8.5 lakh cooperative societies, with nearly 32 crore members associated with them, while the cooperative sector is presently active across around 30 different sectors.

Highlighting the technology-led transformation of grassroots cooperatives, Shri Mohol stated that the computerisation of around 80,000 Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) is underway across the country at a cost of approximately Rs 3,000 crore. The role of PACS, he emphasised, is no longer confined to agricultural credit, agricultural inputs, sugar and dairy businesses. PACS are now being linked with several new areas, including foodgrain storage, insurance, organic products, indigenous seeds, Common Service Centres, Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samriddhi Kendras, Jan Aushadhi Kendras and petrol-diesel distribution. With the reform of the Model Bye-Laws of PACS, they can now undertake more than 25 different economic activities, creating new opportunities for employment and income generation at the village level.

Elaborating on the Government’s effort to bring the entire ‘seed-to-market’ value chain within the cooperative framework, the Union Minister of State for Cooperation referred to the establishment of new national-level multi-State cooperative societies in line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s resolve of ‘Sahkar Se Samriddhi’. These include Bharatiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL) for quality seeds, National Cooperative Organics Limited (NCOL) for organic products and National Cooperative Exports Limited (NCEL) for promoting the export of cooperative products. Around 70,000 cooperative societies across the country have already become associated with these three organisations, directly benefiting farmers and cooperative institutions.

Highlighting the initiatives being taken in the dairy and human resource sectors, Shri Mohol stated that under White Revolution 2.0, efforts are underway to increase the country’s present milk production capacity by approximately 40 percent. At the same time, the country’s first cooperative university has been established to provide trained and capable human resources to cooperative institutions. Emphasising that a strong and transparent cooperative movement requires professionally trained youth, he said Tribhuvan Sahkari University will play an important role in developing nearly 17 lakh trained human resources for the cooperative sector in the coming years.

Illustrating the Central Government’s growing financial support to the cooperative movement, Shri Mohol highlighted the role of the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC). From its establishment in 1963 until 2014, over a period of nearly five decades, NCDC extended assistance of around Rs 45,000 crore to the cooperative sector, whereas during approximately the last 12 years, this assistance has increased to nearly Rs 4.5 lakh crore. He said this reflects the Central Government’s strong commitment towards financially strengthening the cooperative sector.

Referring to Bharat Taxi, Shri Mohol described it as an important new cooperative initiative in the mobility sector, built around the core principle “Driver is the Owner.” Explaining the significance of the model, he said the driver is not merely a service provider but also a stakeholder and owner in the cooperative ecosystem. Unlike conventional aggregator models, where drivers are required to pay a part of their earnings as commission, Bharat Taxi seeks to ensure that the maximum benefit from earnings goes directly to the Saarthis. Earnings from the service are credited directly to their accounts, while the cooperative structure also gives them a stake in ownership and participation in the decision-making process. Highlighting the rapid growth of the initiative since its launch in February 2026, he stated that more than 10 lakh Saarthis have joined Bharat Taxi within just six months and around 20,000 rides are being undertaken every day. Around 40 lakh passengers have also joined the service, while more than Rs 100 crore has been credited to the accounts of Saarthis during the last six months. Bharat Taxi is presently operating in various parts of the country, including Delhi, Gujarat, Mumbai, Jaipur and Chandigarh, and with the addition of Lucknow, Gorakhpur, Varanasi, Kanpur and Prayagraj, its presence in Uttar Pradesh has expanded significantly. Around 40,000 Saarthi brothers and sisters have already registered across these five cities and will soon begin providing services to passengers.

Commending the development trajectory of Uttar Pradesh under Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath, Shri Mohol noted the State’s rapid progress in areas including law and order, infrastructure development, public welfare and cooperation. He observed that Uttar Pradesh has always had a strong social and economic foundation for cooperation. From village chaupals to farms and fields, the tradition of moving forward collectively has remained an integral part of the State’s social fabric, with cooperation providing a modern institutional expression to this spirit. Appreciating the work being undertaken under the leadership of Uttar Pradesh Cooperation Minister Shri J.P.S. Rathore, he highlighted that around 42,000 cooperative societies are presently functioning across the State. He also lauded the Uttar Pradesh Government’s decision to observe 2025 as ‘Sahkarita Mahakumbh’, under which a comprehensive campaign was undertaken to expand the cooperative movement to villages across the State.

Highlighting the success of the M-PACS membership campaign, Shri Mohol stated that more than 54 lakh new members have been enrolled in Uttar Pradesh, including approximately 17.5 lakh farmers. Describing the initiative as a notable example for the cooperative sector across the country, he recalled that Union Home and Cooperation Minister Shri Amit Shah had also appreciated Uttar Pradesh’s membership campaign and recognised its potential as a model that could be considered for replication in other States. The membership campaign has also generated a contribution of around Rs 75 crore for the cooperative sector.

Highlighting Uttar Pradesh’s progress in PACS computerisation, Shri Mohol stated that around 6,300 PACS are being computerised in three phases across the State. In addition, work is being undertaken for the computerisation of approximately 750 agricultural and rural cooperative bank units. Since April 2026, more than 1,200 new M-PACS, dairy, fisheries and other cooperative societies have been formed in Uttar Pradesh, adding approximately one lakh new members. In addition, nearly 22 lakh new members have been enrolled in already operational cooperative societies.

Drawing attention to the growing role of PACS as multipurpose rural service institutions, the Minister noted that around 5,200 Common Service Centres are currently being operated through PACS in Uttar Pradesh. Approximately 7,000 M-PACS are functioning as Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samriddhi Kendras, while 161 M-PACS are providing services as Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras.

Referring to the strengthening of the cooperative banking ecosystem in the State, Shri Mohol highlighted that 16 District Cooperative Banks have been revived with assistance of around Rs 307 crore during the last few years, describing it as an important achievement for Uttar Pradesh’s cooperative sector. Another important milestone has been achieved by the Uttar Pradesh State Cooperative Bank, which has become the first cooperative bank in the country authorised to issue and update Aadhaar cards. In parallel, efforts are also underway towards the establishment of a Cooperative College in Uttar Pradesh to promote study, training and education in the cooperative sector.

Underlining the larger philosophy behind these initiatives, Shri Murlidhar Mohol described cooperation as a powerful means of making the common citizen self-reliant and ensuring dignity for his or her hard work. The expansion of the cooperative model into emerging areas such as mobility, he emphasised, reflects the widening horizons of the movement, with Bharat Taxi representing an important initiative in this direction.

Expressing confidence in the road ahead, Shri Mohol stated that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi at the Centre and Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath in Uttar Pradesh, the cooperative movement will continue to expand with greater momentum towards realising the vision of ‘Sahkar Se Samriddhi’. He further underlined that the cooperative sector will play an extremely important role in realising Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s resolve of ‘Viksit Bharat @2047’, with continued efforts to bring crores of farmers, workers, youth, women and small entrepreneurs into the mainstream of development through the power of cooperation.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Railways
Indian Railways Connects Remote Area of South Chhattisgarh; Track Reaches Taroki-Rowghat Section of Dallirajhara-Rowghat New Rail Line
New Rail Line to Facilitate Iron Ore Transportation to Bhilai Steel Plant and Support Growth of Steel Industry
Project to Strengthen Links with Raipur and Bhilai, Improving Access to Education, Healthcare, Employment and Trade
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 6:03PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Railways achieved a major milestone in the Dallirajhara-Rowghat New Rail Line Project under Raipur Division of South East Central Railway in Chhattisgarh with the completion of final section of the project, Taroki-Rowghat, a single-line electrified broad-gauge section. CRS inspection and speed trial was done on the section yesterday.      

The CRS (Commission of Railway Safety) inspection and speed trial are an important process towards the commissioning of the new railway line. During the inspection, the railway line, bridges and culverts, electrification, signalling and other safety and technical arrangements were examined. As per the prescribed procedure, the operational capacity and safety standards of the rail section were also tested.

The Taroki-Rowghat section, covering 17.5 km, is part of the 95 km long Dallirajhara-Rowghat New Line Project and is located at a remote area of south Chhattisgarh. At present, railway services are available to passengers from Dallirajhara to Taroki. Train operations in the Taroki-Rowghat section will strengthen rail connectivity in the surrounding areas and provide better and convenient transportation options to the citizens of the region.

The railway line will facilitate the transportation of iron ore to Bhilai Steel Plant which will give a boost to the steel industry in the country. The railway line will also help in the transportation of  agricultural products and local commercial goods and play an important role in connecting rural and remote areas with the wider railway network. It will significantly enhance connectivity of the region to the capital Raipur as well as to Bhilai which is an educational hub of the state. Hence, improved rail connectivity will facilitate citizens’ access to opportunities related to education, health, employment and trade.

Expansion of rail transport will also promote tourism, investment and other economic activities in the region. This will boost business activities and contribute to the economic and social development of the region.

The inspection and speed trial of the Taroki-Rowghat section mark important progress towards the commissioning of the Dallirajhara-Rowghat New Railway Line Project.

Dharmendra Tewari/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Vanshita Jaiswal/ Vikas Jha

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Fertilizers
Department of Fertilizers to participate in Special Campaign 6
initiatives from 2nd October to 31st October 2026
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 5:59PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) has issued guidelines to implement the Special Campaign 6 from 2nd October to 31st October, 2026 in order to achieve the goal of institutionalizing Swachhata and minimizing pendency in Government Offices. The focus of the Special Campaign 6 will be saturation of Swachhata by improving overall cleanliness of Government Offices and enhancing experience of common public. The Special Campaign 6 will emphasize 'Effective Collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste.

Department of Fertilizers (DoF), its attached offices and fertilizer PSUs had observed Swachhata Pakhwada from 01.09.2026 to 15.09.2026. The Swachhata Pledge led by Secretary was undertaken in the DoF on 01.09.2025 in which officers/officials actively participated in the event. Further, Shramdaan activities were undertaken by the Officers/officials of DoF in the office premises at Shastri Bhawan on 10.09.2026 as part of the cleanness drive. A bilingual Essay writing competition on the themes of Swachhata and elimination of single use of plastic was also held on 14.09.2026.

Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) Campaign 2026 is currently being observed from 17.09.2026 to 02.10.2026 in the Department of Fertilizers, its attached offices, PSUs, Joint Ventures, Societies and fertilizer Companies in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti and Department of Urban Development, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA). All fertilizer companies have been sensitized in this regard. A video conferencing (VC) meeting was also held on 22.09.2026 under the chairmanship of the Senior Economic Adviser, DoF, with fertilizer companies to review their preparedness for Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS)-2026. During the meeting, fertilizer companies were briefed on the campaign themes and designated activities, with a reiterated emphasis on key initiatives such as Kabaad Se Kala, Khel & Khel Bhawana, and Gyan Yatra.

Special Campaign 6 will be observed by the Department of Fertilizers, its attached offices and all fertilizer PSUs from 2nd October, 2026 to 31st October, 2026. All fertilizer PSUs, attached offices and Divisions under DoF have been sensitized to gear up for the Special Campaign 6 initiatives. Information regarding identification of campaign sites, details of e-waste etc under Special Campaign 6 are being compiled.

Besides, all efforts will be done by the Department of Fertilizers and its PSUs for making progress towards the review and weeding out of old files (both physical and e-files) as per the Record Retention Schedule, disposal of Public Grievances, References from VIPs/MPs, digitization of records, disposal of the e-waste, scrap material etc so that it can improve efficiency and space management. The progress of Special Campaign 6 will be monitored on a dedicated portal www.scdpm.gov.in by DARPG and updated information will be uploaded in the SCDPM portal by the Department of Fertilizers on a regular basis.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
A New Start Through Recovery and Family Support
Bihar Youth Rajveer’s Journey
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 5:41PM by PIB Delhi

The substance use profoundly affect a person’s well-being, relationships and daily life. With timely treatment and continued family support, recovery from substance use can help a person regain stability and take steps towards a healthier future.

Rajveer (name changed), a 28-year-old graduate from Darbhanga district, Bihar, received treatment and rehabilitation support at ROSHANI IRCA after substance use affected his behaviour, emotional well-being and family life. He now lives with his family and has started a small business with their support.

Concerned by changes in his behaviour and emotional state, Rajveer’s father brought him to the Centre on 8 March 2026. Rajveer was initially irritable and found it difficult to adjust to the treatment environment. His family remained supportive while he began receiving professional care.

At ROSHANI IRCA, Rajveer received medical detoxification, regular medication, individual counselling, group therapy, re-educative sessions and yoga activities. The centre also provided family counselling, home visits and follow-up support. As treatment progressed, he began sharing his concerns more openly during counselling sessions.

His family observed positive changes in his behaviour. Rajveer became more engaged in daily activities and, with their help, started a small business. Awareness programmes and continued intervention by the centre also supported his family through the recovery process.

Today, Rajveer is living with his family and working towards a healthy, substance-free life. His experience shows how treatment, counselling and family involvement can support recovery and help someone rebuild daily routines and livelihood.

The activities are being organised…
item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
ITRA Jamnagar Organises Public Awareness, Healthcare and Scientific Activities to Mark 11th Ayurveda Day
Over 2,500 Beneficiaries Reached Through Health, Nutrition and Awareness Activities
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 5:06PM by PIB Delhi

The Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda (ITRA), Jamnagar, is organising a month-long series of public awareness, healthcare, research and scientific activities to mark the 11th Ayurveda Day, focusing on Ayurveda, healthy lifestyles, nutrition, preventive healthcare and scientific research.

The activities are being organised under the guidance of Union Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, and Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, Padma Shri Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, with the efforts of Prof. Dr. Tanuja Nesari, Director, ITRA.

The outreach includes health check-up camps, nutrition awareness programmes, medical camps, senior citizen healthcare, school and Anganwadi programmes, medicinal plant plantation, scientific training, research presentations and workshops. Activities have covered schools, Anganwadis, old-age homes, girls’ homes, educational institutions, Armed Forces establishments and industrial areas.

At least 2,577 beneficiaries have participated directly in the activities so far. Health awareness programmes conducted from 7 to 22 September across Army, Air Force, Navy and CISF establishments, educational and women’s institutions and industrial establishments, along with Ayurveda diet awareness street plays at 11 public places, have further expanded the outreach.

ITRA has also organised scientific and academic activities, including research presentations, laboratory quality-control training, Qiaxcel Connect demonstration and training, a Microbiome workshop and Kayaprabodhini Webinar.

Youth-focused activities include the “Ancient Staple, Modern Plate” reel competition, Yuva Sansad, Student Ambassador Programme, National Essay and E-Poster competitions, Run for Ayurveda, Master Chef Cooking Competition and a seminar on New Media and Digital Communication in Ayurveda.

Prof. Dr. Tanuja Nesari, Director, ITRA, said the Ayurveda Day campaign is bringing together health, nutrition, research, education, environment and youth participation, while promoting Ayurveda as a holistic and preventive approach to health.

item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
RARI Patna Organises Mini Expo on Traditional Foods and Millets to Mark 11th Ayurveda Day
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 5:05PM by PIB Delhi

An Exhibition-cum-Mini Expo and Traditional Food Event was organised at the Regional Ayurveda Research Institute (RARI), Agamkuan, Patna, today on the occasion of the 11th Ayurveda Day, being observed under the theme “Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow”. The programme focused on promoting awareness about Ayurveda, traditional and nutritious foods, millets (Shri Anna) and healthy lifestyle practices.

The programme was inaugurated by Dr. Krishna Pandey, Director, ICMR-RMNIHR. Dr. Banamali Das, In-charge, RARI, highlighted the importance of traditional and nutritious foods described in Ayurveda and emphasised the role of local, seasonal and diverse food grains in a balanced diet.

The Mini Expo showcased traditional and nutritious food preparations, including local food items, millets and other health-promoting ingredients. Visitors were provided information on their nutritional significance, health-promoting properties and appropriate use in daily diets.

Health screening and medical examinations were also conducted for patients, attendants and members of the general public. Ayurvedic medicines were distributed wherever required, while books and Information, Education and Communication (IEC) materials on Ayurveda, nutrition, disease prevention and healthy lifestyles were also provided.

Participants were sensitised on the importance of balanced nutrition, regular daily routines, proper dietary practices, Yoga and healthy lifestyles. Emphasis was also laid on adopting diet and lifestyle practices according to the season and individual constitution (Prakriti), in accordance with Ayurvedic principles.

Dr. Balaji Potbhare, Nodal Officer, Ayurveda Day; Dr. Ashok Kumar Sinha, Research Officer (Ay.); Dr. Ritika Mishra, Research Officer (Ay.); Dr. Kumari Archana, Research Officer (Ay.); and officers and staff of the Institute contributed to the organisation of the programme.

The programme witnessed enthusiastic participation from patients, attendants and members of the general public, furthering awareness about wholesome and nutritious food, traditional dietary practices and an Ayurveda-based healthy lifestyle.

item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
National Institute of Siddha, Chennai, Organises Academic and Awareness Programmes to Mark 11th Ayurveda Day
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 5:03PM by PIB Delhi

The National Institute of Siddha (NIS), Chennai, an autonomous institute under the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India, is organising a series of academic and awareness programmes from 18 to 25 September 2026 to mark the 11th Ayurveda Day.

The week-long observance aims to promote awareness about Ayurveda, encourage interdisciplinary learning and strengthen academic knowledge among students, scholars, healthcare professionals and faculty members.

The celebrations commenced on 18 September with a seminar on “Healthy Skin, Stronger Tomorrow – A Skin Expert Seminar”, organised by the Department of Aruvai, Kan, Kaathu, Mooku, Thondai, Pal Matrum Thol Maruthuvam as part of Skin Awareness Month. The programme also marked the inauguration of the 11th Ayurveda Day celebrations at NIS.

On 21 September, faculty members and students of NIS visited the VHS Hospital Campus, Taramani, and the Dr. Achanta Lakshmipathi Regional Ayurveda Research Institute (ALRARI), Chennai, for institutional exposure and academic interaction.

On 22 September, NIS organised a seminar on “Sophisticated Instrumental Approaches to Drug Standardization” at the Yoga Hall, New OPD. Dr. T. Vinodh Kumar, Research Officer (Chemistry), Captain Srinivasa Murthy Central Ayurveda Research Institute (CCRAS), was the Chief Guest.

The programmes included a seminar on “Future Perspectives of Integrative AYUSH Practices” held on 23 September, followed by a seminar on “Unique Concepts of Ayurvedic Principles and Clinical Diagnosis” scheduled for 24 September.

The week-long observance will conclude on 25 September with a hands-on training programme on Ayurvedic Para-Surgical Procedures.

The programmes are being coordinated by faculty members of the Institute with the support of the organising committee. Undergraduate, postgraduate and Ph.D. scholars, along with faculty members, are participating in the scheduled activities.

Through academic sessions, practical demonstrations and institutional collaborations, NIS is promoting greater awareness and academic engagement around Ayurveda and integrative healthcare practices, in alignment with the vision of the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India.

item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
11th Ayurveda Day Celebrated at National Institute of Ayurveda, Jaipur
NIA, Jaipur Organises Awareness Programmes, Free Ayurveda Health Camps and Educational Activities
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 5:00PM by PIB Delhi

The National Institute of Ayurveda (NIA), Deemed to be University, Jaipur, organised a series of programmes to mark the 11th Ayurveda Day today. The celebrations included traditional worship of Lord Dhanvantari, along with various public awareness, educational and health-related activities.

Speaking on the occasion, Prof. Sanjeev Sharma, Vice-Chancellor, National Institute of Ayurveda, said that Ayurveda is not merely a system of medicine but a holistic way of life focused on healthy and balanced living. He emphasised the importance of greater awareness about preventive healthcare, appropriate diet and lifestyle and healthy daily routines.

Prof. Sharma said that NIA is working continuously to take the benefits of Ayurveda to the public by advancing its traditional knowledge systems through modern research and a scientific approach.

As part of the 11th Ayurveda Day observance, NIA organised various activities aimed at creating awareness about Ayurveda and promoting health protection through Ayurvedic practices. The Institute’s departments organised free Ayurveda medical and health awareness camps in Jaipur and other cities.

The camps provided information to the public on Ayurvedic healthcare, healthy lifestyles, diet and daily routines, and preventive health practices. The Institute also organised public awareness programmes, workshops and educational and health-related activities.

Doctors, faculty members, officers, staff and students of the Institute actively participated in the programmes and pledged to contribute towards wider dissemination of the message of Ayurveda.

On the occasion of the 11th Ayurveda Day, Prof. Sanjeev Sharma, Vice-Chancellor, NIA, along with other doctors from the Institute, also participated in the national-level celebration held in Nagpur.

Prof. P. Hemanta, Head, Department of Shalya Tantra; Shri J. P. Sharma, Joint Director (Administration); Shri Chandrashekhar Sharma, Deputy Director; along with doctors, faculty members, officers, staff and students of the Institute, were present during the programme.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
Competition Begins Today as India’s Largest-Ever Skill Contingent Takes the Global Stage at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026
Team India’s 70 competitors march at Opening Ceremony and begin competing across 63 skills
Indian delegation leadership joins the contingent as four days of competition get underway
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 4:45PM by PIB Delhi

Competition began today at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, with Team India’s largest-ever contingent of 70 young competitors taking to the competition floor across 63 skill categories. The four-day competition follows the Opening Ceremony held yesterday evening, where Team India participated in the Parade of Nations alongside contingents from across the world.

The Opening Ceremony at the Shanghai World Expo Cultural Center brought together nearly 1,400 competitors from more than 65 countries and regions. Carrying the national flag and dressed in Team India colours, the Indian contingent marched into the arena to resounding cheers, marking the formal start of the 48th WorldSkills Competition.

The 48th WorldSkills Competition officially opened in Shanghai, with Chinese President Xi Jinping sending a congratulatory letter to the event, which was read out at the opening ceremony. Chinese Premier Li Qiang attended the ceremony and formally declared the competition open, marking the beginning of the global skills competition that brings together young talent from across the world.

The Indian delegation leadership present at the ceremony included Ms. Manisha Sensharma, Official Delegate, WorldSkills India and Senior Economic Adviser, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Shri Dilip Kumar, Director General, DGT and CEO, National Skill Organization (NSO). They joined competitors, experts and mentors in supporting Team India as the global competition commenced.

Shri Dilip Kumar, Director General, DGT National Skill Organization (NSO) said that, "Our competitors have reached Shanghai after months of intensive technical preparation, repeated simulations and close mentoring by experts and industry partners. We are also happy to share that out of 70 candidates; 14 candidates are from our Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs). The focus now is on precision, composure and consistent performance over the four competition days. The entire delegation stands firmly behind Team India”.

Ms. Manisha Sensharma, Official Delegate, WorldSkills India and Senior Economic Adviser, MSDE, said, "Watching Team India march at the Opening Ceremony was a moment of immense pride. Each of our 70 competitors represents the aspirations of a skilled and confident India. As the competition begins today, they have the opportunity to benchmark their capabilities against the world’s best, learn from global peers and demonstrate the depth of talent emerging from India’s skilling ecosystem."

Team India’s participation this year represents a significant expansion in both scale and scope. For the first time, India will compete in 11 new skill categories: Dental Prosthetics, Digital Interactive Media Design, Intelligent Security Technology, Landscape Gardening, Optoelectronic Technology, Retail Sales, Unmanned Aerial Systems, Industrial Mechanics, Software Testing, Heavy Vehicle Technology and Aircraft Maintenance.

The contingent’s presence in the march-past reflected the diversity and strength of India’s skilling ecosystem. The competitors have progressed through rigorous selection and months of specialised training, intensive practice and international-standard preparation, supported by State Governments, Sector Skill Councils, training institutions, industry partners, experts and mentors.

The WorldSkills Competition, organised every two years by WorldSkills International, is the world’s largest international platform for vocational education, training and skills excellence. It enables young professionals to demonstrate technical expertise, precision, creativity, craftsmanship and innovation, while benchmarking their capabilities against global standards.

The skill competitions began at 9:00 a.m. today at the National Exhibition and Convention Center in Shanghai and will continue until 26 September, followed by the Closing Ceremony on 27 September. WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 also features the WorldSkills Expo and the WorldSkills Conference, bringing together young people, policymakers, educators and industry leaders to experience skills and exchange ideas on the future of technical and vocational education and workforce development.

As the competitions commence, Team India will seek to build on the country’s performance at WorldSkills Lyon 2024, where India secured four bronze medals and 12 Medallions for Excellence. The Shanghai campaign offers India’s young professionals an opportunity to test their abilities against the world’s best and showcase the depth, discipline and future-readiness of the country’s skilled talent.

 

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Major boost to ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’: MoD signs Rs 811 crore contract with BDL for 160 Satellite Smart Anti Airfield Weapons for IAF
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 4:45PM by PIB Delhi

Ministry of Defence has inked a contract with Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL) for the procurement of 160 Satellite Smart Anti Airfield Weapons (SAT-SAAW) along with associated equipment for Indian Air Force (IAF) with a total cost of Rs 810.79 crore under Buy (Indian - Indigenously Designed, Developed and Manufactured) category. The contract was signed in the presence of Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh in New Delhi on September 23, 2026.

SAT-SAAW is an air-to-ground precision guided glide bomb which can be launched from platforms like Jaguar, Hawk & Su-30 MKI, and has the capability to neutralise enemy airfields from a long stand-off range. Indigenously designed and developed by DRDO, the system will have an indigenous content of 60% along with indigenisation of sub-systems like Initial Measurement Unit, Long Impact Delay Fuse and Twin Store Carrier to further boost Aatmanirbharta in defence.

The delivery of SAT-SAAW is scheduled between 2027-2028 and 2028-2029. Its induction would certainly enhance the operational capability of IAF to continue their unhindered operations and strengthen defence preparedness of the country.

item.content:encoded:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES THE 75TH ANNUAL CONVOCATION CEREMONY OF MAHARAJA SAYAJIRAO UNIVERSITY OF BARODA
EDUCATION WILL BE MEANINGFUL IF IT BENEFITS THE COUNTRY AND THE SOCIETY: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 4:39PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu graced the 75th annual convocation ceremony of the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda at Vadodara, Gujarat today (September 23, 2026).

Speaking on the occasion, the President said that from the past 75 years, the university has been advancing by integrating diverse streams of knowledge.

The President underlined that in today's world, the solution to any problem is not confined to a single discipline. She emphasised that a multidisciplinary approach is necessary to address the critical challenges. We need the curiosity of a scientist, the sensitivity of an artist, the perspective of a historian, the insight of an economist, and the consciousness of a sociologist. She stated that higher education institutions like Maharaja Sayajirao University are expected to remain constantly alert and dynamic in this direction.

The President asked graduating students to reflect on the purpose of their education and knowledge. She said that when they move ahead in their professional field by prioritizing the interests of the nation and society, they will also progress, and that progress will bring them immense satisfaction.

The President said that education will be meaningful only if it benefits the country and society. She advised students that as engineers, they should develop technologies that improve people's lives; as doctors, they should view medicine not merely as a profession but as a form of service; as scientists, they should find solutions to problems in the interest of humanity; as artists or writers, they should enrich the sensitivity of society; as entrepreneurs, they should create not just wealth, but also employment and opportunities; as teachers, they should focus on nurturing a young generation that embraces both heritage and progress; and in public life, they should regard their position as a responsibility rather than a source of authority.

The President said that we are moving forward with the national goal of building Viksit Bharat by the year 2047 - a country where quality education and healthcare facilities reach everyone; where science and technology are utilized for human welfare; where there is equality of opportunity; where the full potential of women and the youth is harnessed; and a Bharat where every citizen has the opportunity to live a life of dignity. She said that universities and youth have to play an important role in achieving these goals.

Please click here to see the President's speech-

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
INDIA–SRI LANKA BILATERAL MARITIME EXERCISE SLINEX-26 CONCLUDED AT VISAKHAPATNAM
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 4:30PM by PIB Delhi

The 13th edition of the India–Sri Lanka bilateral maritime exercise, SLINEX-26, concluded at Visakhapatnam on 21 Sep 2026. Conducted from 17–21 Sep 26, the exercise provided opportunities for professional interactions, exchange of best practices and enhancement of interoperability between the two Navies.

The harbour phase of the exercise featured professional exchanges, cross-deck visits and sporting interactions between the Indian Navy and Sri Lanka Navy.

The Sea Phase featured coordinated maritime manoeuvres, air operations, night replenishment at sea and Special Forces drills, including Visit, Board, Search and Seizure (VBSS) and slithering operations. These activities provided valuable opportunities to hone operational coordination and interoperability between the participating forces.

SLINEX-26 reflects the strong maritime partnership between India and Sri Lanka and their shared commitment towards a secure and stable Indian Ocean Region. The exercise contributes to India’s vision of MAHASAGAR and the Neighbourhood First policy through enhanced maritime cooperation, interoperability and capacity building.

****

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
Kanda Express carrying onions from Government buffer stock to reach Kolkata on 24 September
Around 1,400 MT of onions already distributed in West Bengal at ₹35 per kg through NAFED and NCCF mobile vans
Onion distribution planned across Kolkata and adjoining districts to strengthen availability and moderate retail prices during festive season
Buffer stock onions supplied to over 100 cities across the country; retail prices stable or declined in 17 States/UTs in past week
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 4:29PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India is strengthening the supply of onions in West Bengal, with the Kanda Express carrying onions from the Price Stabilization Fund (PSF) buffer stock scheduled to reach Kolkata on 24 September 2026. The arrival is expected to facilitate faster movement of larger quantities of onions and further strengthen availability in Kolkata and adjoining districts, particularly ahead of the festive season.

The Government of India is stepping up the supply of onions in West Bengal, with the Kanda Express carrying onions from the Price Stabilization Fund (PSF) buffer stock scheduled to reach Kolkata on 24 September 2026. The arrival is expected to facilitate faster movement of larger quantities of onions and further strengthen availability in Kolkata and adjoining districts, particularly ahead of the festive season.

Around 1,400 MT of onions have already been distributed in West Bengal through NAFED and NCCF mobile vans at ₹35 per kg, mainly through road transport. With the arrival of Kanda Express, additional quantities will now be moved more efficiently, helping improve market availability and moderate seasonal price pressures.

The distribution of onions from the incoming consignment is being planned in Kolkata and adjoining districts, with the focus on ensuring that the intervention has maximum impact on prevailing retail prices. In Kolkata, retail sales are currently being undertaken at more than 25 locations, including major markets such as Koley Market, Mechua Mandi, Maniktala Market, Rampuria Market and Shyam bazar Market.

The Government is also exploring the possibility of retail sale of buffer stock onions through Sufal Bangla, which would provide consumers with additional points of access and help widen the reach of the intervention.

The Kolkata-bound Kanda Express is part of the Government's ongoing strategy of calibrated release of onions from the PSF buffer stock through a hybrid rail-and-road transportation network. The targeted disposal of buffer stock through NAFED and NCCF commenced on 24 August 2026, with supplies being progressively sent to different parts of the country based on market requirements.

So far, onions from the buffer stock have been supplied to more than 100 cities across the country. The use of both rail and road transport has enabled the Government to move onions in larger quantities while responding to regional requirements in a timely manner.

The increased availability has also started easing price pressures in several parts of the country. During the past one week, retail onion prices remained stable or declined in 17 States/UTs, indicating an improvement in market availability following the buffer stock interventions.

Among the States/UTs where onion prices declined during the past week are Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Tamil Nadu and Bihar.

The Government is continuing to monitor onion availability and prices across major consuming markets and is undertaking calibrated releases from the buffer stock, as required, to improve availability and moderate seasonal price pressures. Further supplies are likely to be sent to different markets based on local requirements, including during the ensuing festive season.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Rural Development

The interaction was held under the chairpersonship of Shri P. Narahari, Joint Secretary, Department of Land Resources, and focused on India’s experience in…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
India Shares Experience in Digitisation and Modernisation of Land Records with Sri Lankan Delegation
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 3:30PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Land Resources (DoLR), Ministry of Rural Development, today hosted a delegation of civil servants from Sri Lanka visiting India under an exposure programme coordinated by the National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG). The interaction was held under the chairpersonship of Shri P. Narahari, Joint Secretary, Department of Land Resources, and focused on India’s experience in digitising and modernising land records, with emphasis on the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP), computerisation of Records of Rights (RoRs), integration of registration with land records and the Unique Land Parcel Identification Number (ULPIN).

The Sri Lankan delegation was led by Ms. Pathirage Laxman Pathmakumari, Team Leader of the Delegation, Sri Lanka, and included Dr. Mukesh K. Bhandari, Course Coordinator, National Centre for Good Governance, LBSNAA, and Dr. A.P. Singh, Course Director, along with senior officials from Sri Lanka’s land, survey and administrative services.

Welcoming the delegation, Shri P. Narahari highlighted the close ties between India and Sri Lanka and the importance of sharing experiences in public administration. He said, “Land is not merely an administrative record; it is closely linked to livelihoods, economic activity, access to government benefits and citizens’ sense of security. India’s experience has been one of continuously modernising land administration through technology, while recognising the diversity of our States and their land systems. We are pleased to share these experiences with our Sri Lankan colleagues and equally look forward to learning from their institutional practices and reforms.”

During the interaction, Shri Amit Kumar Singh, Director (LR), DoLR, presented an overview of the macro reforms and technological framework powering DILRMP. He highlighted India’s transition from conventional paper-based records to integrated digital land information systems.

Shri Amit Kumar Singh said, “The transformation of land records is not merely about converting paper records into digital form. The larger objective is to create an integrated land information ecosystem where textual records, spatial information, registration data and geospatial technologies complement each other.”

Key DILRMP milestones shared with the delegation included:

  • 99.90% of textual Records of Rights (RoRs) computerised.
  • 97.43% of cadastral maps digitised and 76.16% of land parcels fully georeferenced.
  • 85.24% spatial-textual integration achieved between cadastral maps and RoRs.
  • 40.58 crore+ land parcels assigned the 14-digit alphanumeric Bhu-Aadhaar (ULPIN).
  • 98.96% of Sub-Registrar Offices (SROs) computerised.
  • 17 States/UTs adopting the centralised National Generic Document Registration System (NGDRS), while 17 States operate state-specific digital registration software.
  • 94.11% of Revenue Courts computerised under the Revenue Court Case Management System (RCCMS), enabling real-time litigation marking on property records.

The delegation was also briefed on the integration of cadastral maps and Records of Rights to ensure consistency in ownership details, parcel boundaries and area information.

The interaction covered the integration of property registration with land records through mutation, including ongoing reforms towards paperless registration and automated mutation. Under the emerging system, registration information can be electronically transmitted to the concerned revenue authority for updating land records, reducing delays and the need for repeated visits to government offices.

The delegation was also given a walkthrough of the Bharat Land Stack, an integrated, GIS-based federated architecture bringing together satellite and drone imagery, georeferenced cadastral boundaries, Records of Rights, property registration data, master planning and zoning regulations, building approvals, restrictions and litigation, circle rates and tenancy details. The architecture seeks to provide an integrated digital view of land-related information associated with a parcel.

The visiting officials were further briefed on ULPIN, or Bhu-Aadhaar, which assigns a unique 14-digit alphanumeric identity to land parcels based on their geospatial coordinates. The system facilitates linkage of land parcels with other land-related datasets and maintains linkages when parcels undergo subdivision.

Shri Sarvadanand Barnwal, Director (LR), DoLR, presented a comprehensive overview of the NAKSHA (National Geospatial Knowledge-based Land Survey of Urban Habitations) programme and its approach to modernising urban land records through advanced surveying and geospatial technologies.

The presentation detailed the end-to-end NAKSHA workflow, including:

  • Deployment of 2D Nadir cameras, 5-camera Oblique systems and LiDAR sensors mounted on aerial drones for centimetre-level positional accuracy.
  • Generation of Ortho-Rectified Imagery (ORI), Digital Elevation Models (DEM) and 3D Reality Models for complex urban landscapes.
  • RTK GNSS rover-based ground truthing, participatory ground validation and transparent claims and objections redressal.
  • Aerial flying completed across 145 of 150 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) under the pilot phase, progressing towards issuance of legally authentic Urban Property (UrPro) Cards.

Shri Sarvadanand Barnwal said, “NAKSHA is an important step towards strengthening urban land governance through modern geospatial technologies. By creating reliable and integrated urban land records, the programme can support better land administration, improve planning and contribute to greater ease of living for citizens.”

The interaction provided the Sri Lankan delegation with an overview of India’s experience in large-scale land governance reforms, spanning digitisation of land records, spatial-textual integration, digital registration, mutation, geospatial identification of land parcels, computerisation of Revenue Courts and modern urban land mapping.

The engagement underscored the importance of international knowledge-sharing in public administration and highlighted how digital and geospatial technologies can support transparent, integrated and citizen-centric land governance and improve public service delivery.

Written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks-and-balances are standard, ongoing practices designed to ensure complete transparency, legal compliance and…
item.content:encoded:
Election Commission
All decisions, including SIR, are the outcome of unanimous decisions of the full Commission: ECI
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 3:29PM by PIB Delhi
  1. The ECI is a constitutional body that functions under the strict mandate of Article 324 of the Constitution, statutory rules and established institutional conventions. The Commission operates as a multi-member constitutional body. Written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks-and-balances are standard, ongoing practices designed to ensure complete transparency, legal compliance and operational rigour. All actions of ECI have been in accordance of laws and instructions of the Commission.
  2. All official orders, decisions and administrative directions issued by the Commission carry full legal sanctions and follow established statutory procedures under The Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.
  3. Any operational queries or inputs raised by Commission members during draft stages are part of standard administrative practice aimed at safeguarding voter rights. The suggestions given by the Commissioners were for further improving the electoral processes.
  4. Differing views and observations are a normal part of deliberation in any institution. They are a part of the decision-making process before a final decision is taken. Not only the three Commissioners, but every officer of the Commission is fully authorized to give his suggestions to the Commission for improving the electoral system.
  5. Highlighting certain specific internal notes/observations spread over the period of 10 months while overlooking the much larger body of approvals, decisions, instructions and initiatives give only one part of the picture. In recent months, the Commission has taken numerous decisions, issued instructions, introduced around 40 new initiatives and undertaken many electoral reforms including the conduct of Electoral roll revision (including SIR) across the country. All these decisions are an outcome of the unanimous decisions of the full Commission in the past one year.
  6. The Commission has recently successfully conducted major elections of Bihar, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Assam and West Bengal and election-related exercises during this period. This work involved wide-ranging administrative and operational machinery and many Commission approvals and instructions.
  7. The Commission’s digital platforms, such as ECINet, operate under strict data security protocols to prevent unauthorized tampering, manipulation, etc. IT security checks and audit controls are standard cybersecurity measures implemented across national databases. Statutory authorities, including Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) and District Election Officers (DEOs), function as per statutory powers for registration and deletion under law.
  8. The Election Commission of India remains fully committed to executing its constitutional duties with complete integrity, recognizing its vital role in advancing our democracy.

**********

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Academia Industry collaboration traced the mechanism of how preservatives take down bacteria enabling smarter preservation
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 3:17PM by PIB Delhi

Scientists have captured, for the first time, the moment of bacteria succumbing to preservative attack. Using advanced imaging and chemical analysis, the team revealed how preservatives disrupt bacterial cells from within. The breakthrough opens the door to designing smarter and safer preservation technologies across home and personal care categories.

Both Sodium benzoate (SB) and Phenoxyethanol (POE) are effective preservatives. Sodium benzoate (SB) has been keeping foods such as pickles, ketchup and fizzy drinks safe since the early 1900s, being the very first food preservative approved by the US FDA, back in 1908. Phenoxyethanol (POE) is the newer addition, having been used in shampoo, moisturiser, sunscreen and even certain vaccines for decades. Despite more than a century of widespread use, the molecular mechanisms underlying the anti-bacterial activity of these two lead preservatives, SB and POE, remain poorly understood.

Researchers at Institute of Nano Science & Technology (INST) Mohali, an autonomous institute of the Department of Science and Technology, in collaboration with Unilever R&D Bangalore, addressed this knowledge gap by integrating transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with complementary biochemical analyses to elucidate the antimicrobial mode of action of preservative systems. The study investigated preservative-induced cellular and biochemical responses in two representative bacterial pathogens: the Gram-positive Staphylococcus aureus and the Gram-negative Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

Fig 1: The study revealed a dual mode of action: preservatives compromise the bacterial cell envelope while triggering internal biochemical damage, delivering a coordinated attack on multiple cellular targets.

The researchers found that preservatives attack bacteria on multiple fronts. The microbial cell envelope becomes physically compromised, while reactive aldehydes and oxygen-derived species accumulate inside the cell, disrupting essential proteins, genetic material, and other critical cellular functions. Rather than a single mode of action, the preservatives deliver a coordinated multi-target assault, providing one of the clearest views yet of how bacterial cells are inactivated.

Advanced imaging revealed that sodium benzoate and phenoxyethanol follow distinct pathways to bacterial inactivation. Sodium benzoate induced cellular shrinkage and collapse, whereas phenoxyethanol caused membrane expansion and eventual rupture. The researchers further showed that sodium benzoate becomes significantly more potent in acidic environments, exhibiting an approximately sixteen-fold increase in activity, while phenoxyethanol displayed consistent efficacy across a wide pH range. These findings provide important insights into how preservative performance can be optimized for different formulation conditions.

The team consisting of Ishani Sharma, S M Rose, Madhu Lata, Somnath Das, Nagaraja IS Acharya, Maheshwara Naik, Samiran Mahapatra and Sharmistha Sinha ran bacteria through a gauntlet of tests like inhibition zone and MIC assays to see how much preservative it takes to knock growth down, electron microscopy to literally watch cell shape fall apart, a dye leakage test to catch membranes springing leaks, and two biochemical assays (MBTH and DCFDA) to measure the internal chemical chaos, across two very different bacteria, and both neutral and acidic conditions. Together, these methods helped the researchers connect what a bacterium looks like on the outside to what's actually going wrong on the inside, at the same moment. It was published in the journal: Letters in Applied Microbiology

Fig 2: TEM images: Non-treated cells (P. aeruginosa-top and S. aureus-bottom) vs. cells treated with SB or POE, showing membrane rupture and cytoplasmic leakage (indicated with red arrow).

Knowing exactly how these preservatives work can help industry chose the correct one for a particular product format, (sodium benzoate is suitable for anything acidic and phenoxyethanol is suitable for cases where pH swings shouldn't matter), use just the right amount instead of guessing, cut down on spoilage and waste, and stay a step ahead of bacteria that might otherwise evolve resistance.

Publication link: 10.1093/lambio/ovag022

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
MY Bharat Crosses Landmark Milestone of 3 Crore + Registered Youth in less than 3 Years
Milestone reflects growing participation of young Indians in opportunities for leadership, experiential learning, volunteering and nation-building
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 3:00PM by PIB Delhi

Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) (mybharat.gov.in/),  the national youth engagement platform of the Department of Youth Affairs, Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, has crossed the landmark milestone of 3 crore +  registered youth. The achievement marks a significant expansion of India's largest youth engagement ecosystem, providing young people with opportunities to participate in experiential learning, volunteering, leadership, civic engagement and youth-led initiatives.

Launched by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 31 October 2023, MY Bharat was established with the vision of creating a technology-enabled platform through which young Indians can participate in the nation's development journey. At the launch, the Prime Minister emphasised the importance of bringing the country's youth together on a common platform and enabling their greater participation in nation-building. The platform was conceived as an important institutional mechanism for translating the energy, aspirations and potential of India's youth into meaningful participation towards Viksit Bharat @2047.

The journey of MY Bharat has witnessed rapid expansion since its launch. The platform crossed 2 crore + registrations in October 2025 and subsequently expanded its reach to more than 2.46 crore +  registered youth by August 2026. The crossing of the 3 crore + mark within the next phase of its expansion reflects the continuing growth of youth participation on the platform.

MY Bharat today serves as a common digital gateway through which young people can discover and participate in Experiential Learning Programmes, volunteering opportunities, quizzes, leadership initiatives, youth dialogues and community engagement activities. As of August 2026, more than 1.22 lakh youth had enrolled in nearly 25,000 Experiential Learning Programmes, providing opportunities for young people to gain practical exposure through participation beyond conventional classroom settings.

The platform has also continued to evolve technologically. An AI-enabled CV Builder has been introduced to help young people create professional profiles, while the platform is being strengthened through digital services and wider grassroots access..

A key initiative being driven through MY Bharat is the Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue (VBYLD) 2027, which is providing young Indians with multiple pathways to showcase their ideas, creativity, leadership and innovation towards the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047. The initiative began with the Viksit Bharat Quiz on 17 August 2026, which is open until 30 September 2026 on the MY Bharat platform. Under the flagship Viksit Bharat Challenge, participants progress through the Essay Challenge, District Championships and State/UT-level stages before culminating in the National Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue in New Delhi from 10–12 January 2027. Alongside this, VBYLD 2027 features five additional tracks—Cultural Track, Design for Bharat, Hack for Social Cause, Youth Entrepreneurs Challenge and Youth Parliament—providing platforms for young people to demonstrate their cultural talent, creative and design thinking, technology-led solutions, entrepreneurial ideas and leadership in parliamentary processes. Selected young participants across these tracks will get an opportunity to engage with policymakers and, at the national level, present their ideas before the Prime Minister.

The current MY Bharat ecosystem also hosts a range of youth-focused initiatives, including Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat, Viksit Vibrant Village Programme, Viksit Bharat Youth Parliament, Viksit Bharat Padyatra, Viksit Bharat Yuva Connect and Khelo India Dialogue, alongside Experiential Learning and volunteering opportunities.

Through the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat campaign, MY Bharat is also contributing to the nationwide effort to mobilise young people for a healthier and drug-free India. The 100 Weeks Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan commenced with the Rashtriya Sankalp Samaroh in September 2026, with youth participation through pledge-taking, signature campaigns, creative activities and discussions across the country.

The 3 crore + milestone therefore represents more than an increase in registrations. It reflects the expanding scale of a national platform through which young Indians can learn through experience, participate in community initiatives, develop leadership capabilities and contribute their ideas to the country's development journey.

As MY Bharat continues to expand its digital and grassroots ecosystem, the platform remains focused on strengthening Yuva Shakti, Jan Bhagidari and youth-led nation-building, in keeping with the vision of empowering India's young population to contribute meaningfully towards a Viksit Bharat @2047.

***

Pawan Singh Faujdar

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
Minister of State for Corporate Affairs and Road Transport & Highways Shri Harsh Malhotra Lays Foundation Stones for Two Foot Over Bridges on Delhi-Saharanpur-Dehradun Expressway in East Delhi
FOBs Equipped with Lift Facilities to Enhance Pedestrian Safety, Accessibility and Mobility; Third FOB Approved near Bhajanpura, Garhi Mendu
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 2:39PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Harsh Malhotra, Hon’ble Minister of State for Corporate Affairs and Road Transport and Highways and Member of Parliament, East Delhi Lok Sabha, today laid the foundation stones for two Foot Over Bridges (FOBs) at Geeta Colony/Gandhi Nagar (Km 5+100) and Ramesh Park, Laxmi Nagar (Km 2+800) on the Delhi-Saharanpur-Dehradun Expressway (NH-709B) in East Delhi.

The occasion was graced by Shri Arvinder Singh Lovely, MLA, Gandhi Nagar and Chairman, Trans Yamuna Development Board; Shri Abhay Verma, MLA, Laxmi Nagar and Chief Whip, Delhi Legislative Assembly; Dr. Anil Goyal, MLA, Krishna Nagar; local councillors and prominent citizens of the area.

The Minister said that the initiative reflects the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for modern, citizen-centric infrastructure that directly improves ease of living and safer mobility. He said that under his leadership and the guidance of Union Minister for Road Transport & Highways Shri Nitin Gadkari, India has witnessed rapid development of modern expressways, high-capacity road corridors and public safety initiatives.

Shri Harsh Malhotra stated that the initiative marks an important step towards enhancing pedestrian safety and improving everyday mobility for residents of East Delhi. He said that the Delhi section of the Expressway passes through densely populated areas and connects major residential, commercial and local movement corridors, making safe pedestrian infrastructure particularly important.

The FOBs will be equipped with lift facilities, providing safe, dedicated and convenient pedestrian crossings while reducing pedestrian-vehicle interaction and facilitating uninterrupted vehicular movement. The lifts will also improve accessibility for senior citizens, persons with mobility challenges, students, workers and other pedestrians.

In addition to the two FOBs, one more Foot Over Bridge has been approved at Km 10+800 near Bhajanpura, Garhi Mendu. The total cost of the three Foot Over Bridges will be ₹12.8 crore.

The Minister also highlighted that parking facilities under the elevated portion of the Delhi section of the Delhi-Dehradun Expressway have been started and the comprehensive beautification plan for the Delhi stretch of the Delhi-Saharanpur-Dehradun Expressway (NH-709B, Phase-I) is under progress.

These initiatives will enable optimal utilisation of the space beneath the elevated corridor, improve parking management and provide public amenities such as EV charging, toilets and other facilities. They would further support traffic decongestion and enhance the overall aesthetics of the corridor, benefiting residents, traders and daily commuters.

Shri Malhotra also highlighted that solar panels are being installed along the elevated stretch of the Delhi section of the Delhi-Saharanpur-Dehradun Highway. The initiative will promote the use of renewable energy for highway-related requirements, reduce dependence on conventional power sources and contribute towards lowering carbon emissions, in line with the vision of sustainable development and Net Zero by 2070.

Shri Harsh Malhotra said that from safer pedestrian crossings at Geeta Colony, Gandhi Nagar and Laxmi Nagar to the upcoming facility near Bhajanpura, Garhi Mendu, and the integration of renewable energy along the elevated highway stretch, these initiatives represent a focused effort to address the practical infrastructure needs of East Delhi and translate the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047 into visible, citizen-centric outcomes.

***

item.title: TDB-DST backs India’s next-generation air mobility ambitions with ₹285 crore RDI support to Ubifly Technologies
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Science & Technology
item.description: Ministry of Science & Technology TDB-DST backs India’s next-generation air mobility ambitions with ₹285 crore RDI support to Ubifly Technologies Support under the ₹1 lakh crore RDI Fund to take indigenous ePlane technology from TRL-6 to TRL-9 Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 2:27PM by PIB Delhi India’s push to build a globally competitive, private-sector-led deep-tech ecosystem is gaining momentum with the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, approving ₹285 crore financial support to Ubifly Technologies Private…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
TDB-DST backs India’s next-generation air mobility ambitions with ₹285 crore RDI support to Ubifly Technologies
Support under the ₹1 lakh crore RDI Fund to take indigenous ePlane technology from TRL-6 to TRL-9
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 2:27PM by PIB Delhi

India’s push to build a globally competitive, private-sector-led deep-tech ecosystem is gaining momentum with the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, approving ₹285 crore financial support to Ubifly Technologies Private Limited, Chennai under the Research Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund for advancing its indigenous ePlane Advanced Air Mobility Solution.

With a total approved project cost of ₹570 crore, the project will take the technology from Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 6 to TRL 9, marking a significant step towards the commercial deployment of an indigenous advanced air mobility platform. The TDB support will be provided through Optionally Convertible Debentures (OCD).

The e200X, being developed by Ubifly Technologies, is a three-seater, zero-emission advanced air mobility aircraft configured for one pilot and two passengers, with a targeted range of 110 km and an ideal speed of 160 kmph. The aircraft brings together multiple indigenous technology elements, including vertical rotors, forward propellers, proprietary flight-control algorithms, power-distribution controllers and battery-pack modules with integrated cooling systems. The company has also designed the complete airframe, including the fuselage, wings and booms, in-house.

A notable feature of the aircraft is its landing gear designed for both conventional and vertical landing, offering operational flexibility for advanced air mobility applications. Its compact architecture is intended to enable operations from relatively small spaces and facilitate multiple trips on a single battery charge. The project is categorised under Deep Technology, with Space Technologies as the sub-sector. Its advancement from TRL-6 to TRL-9 will involve further technology maturation, testing, validation and scale-up towards an operationally demonstrated system.

Sh. Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, TDB, said, “The RDI Fund represents a significant shift towards enabling private-sector participation in the development of high-impact technologies and taking promising innovations closer to deployment. TDB’s support to Ubilfy Technologies reflects the Government of India’s commitment to strengthening indigenous capabilities in deep technologies and creating pathways for Indian technologies to move from advanced development to commercialisation. The ePlane project brings together advanced electric propulsion, aerospace engineering and intelligent systems.”

Representative of Ubifly Technologies Private Limited said, “The support extended by TDB under the RDI Fund will provide important impetus to the continued development and validation of our ePlane technology. Taking the e200X from TRL-6 towards TRL-9 requires sustained investment in engineering, testing and technology maturation. We appreciate TDB’s support in enabling this transition and in strengthening indigenous advanced air mobility capabilities in India.”

***

Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 2:25PM by PIB Delhi

The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, has shared an article written by Union Minister, Shri Bhupender Yadav.

The Prime Minister noted that India's rhino story is one of remarkable recovery of the species. He added that with the rhino population showing sustained growth, India is now one of the world's most important custodians of the Greater One-Horned Rhinoceros, and protecting the grasslands and wetlands that sustain the species is central to its future. Shri Modi further pointed out that the must-read article by the Union Minister highlights how Government efforts are strengthening the conservation journey.

The Prime Minister’s Office posted on X:

“India's rhino story is one of remarkable recovery of the species.

With the rhino population showing sustained growth, India is now one of the world's most important custodians of the Greater One-Horned Rhinoceros. Protecting the grasslands and wetlands that sustain the species is central to its future.

This must-read article by Union Minister Shri @byadavbjp highlights how Government efforts are strengthening the conservation journey.”

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister congratulates Jay Meena on winning Bronze in Men's Individual event and becoming India's first-ever Asian Games medallist in Soft Tennis
Posted On: 23 SEP 2026 2:22PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today congratulated Jay Meena on winning a Bronze medal in the Men’s Individual event and becoming India’s first-ever Asian Games medallist in Soft Tennis, calling it a historic achievement for Indian Soft Tennis.

The Prime Minister stated that his achievement marks a memorable new chapter for the sport in India. He expressed hope that this medal will inspire many more youngsters to take up Soft Tennis and excel, and extended his best wishes to him for the journey ahead.

In a post on X, the Prime Minister's Office mentioned:

"A historic achievement for Indian Soft Tennis!
