Dignitaries present during the inauguration ceremony included Additional Director General…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Union Environment Minister inaugurates WWF Global Conservation Conference at Jaipur (Rajasthan)
Shri Bhupender Yadav calls for Global Action on Conservation and Coexistence by Involving Local Communities
Posted On: 21 SEP 2026 2:12PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today inaugurated the Global Conservation Conference of the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) at Jaipur. Dignitaries present during the inauguration ceremony included Additional Director General (Wildlife), MoEFCC, Shri Ramesh Pandey; Head of Forest Force and Principal Chief Conservator of Forest, Government of Rajasthan, Shri Arijit Banerjee; Chief Conservation Officer at WWF-International, Shri Daudi Samba; and, CEO of WWF-India, Shri Ravi Singh.

 

 

Addressing representatives from more than 100 countries, the Minister emphasised the need to act on conservation and coexistence, reconnect as a community, take confidence from the progress being made, and build a shared sense of hope and direction. Shri Yadav shared the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in the field of wildlife conservation and mentioned how the number of protected areas have gone up from around 750 to more than 1000 in the last decade. Similarly, the number of tiger reserves rose from 47 to 58 and elephant reserves from 30 to 33, while the number of Ramsar sites has gone up from 24 to 101 in the same period. He further narrated the success of Cheetah reintroduction in India, under the visionary leadership of the Prime Minister.

Shri Yadav informed the gathering that India's commitment to species conservation is both constitutional and cultural, rooted in a worldview that long predates modern protected-area law. India has built a substantial framework in its Constitution that makes protecting wildlife both a State directive and a citizen's duty, yet this formal architecture rests on a deeper ethos. India is also a party to CITES, CMS, CBD and the Ramsar Convention, and its recovery of tigers, elephants, rhinos and Asiatic lions shows what sustained political will can achieve.

 

 

The Minister also mentioned how scientific research and monitoring mechanisms in the country have led to conservation successes. He underlined the pan-India population estimation of species such as tiger, elephant, dolphin, lion and snow leopard have provided insights for habitat improvement, securing corridors and taking landscape approach in megafaunal species. He also narrated the success of conservation breeding of Great India Bustard (GIB) in Rajasthan and community led protection and conservation of sacred groves called Oran, helping in land degradation neutrality.

Shri Yadav emphasized the need of conservation of grasslands along with woodlands and wetlands. He shared India's approach towards conservation of grassland-based mega herbivores and informed the gathering about the ongoing conservation programmes on one-horned rhinoceros and the wild water buffalo. He concluded his address by giving a call to the wildlife conservationists to come together not only to reflect, but to move forward, learn from what works, and turn it into action.

Ltd., a Miniratna-I Central Public Sector Enterprise under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, continued to contribute to the Government of India’s vision of Viksit Bharat through its diversified operations spanning logistics, manufacturing, travel services, technology, skill development and sustainable business practices,…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas
Balmer Lawrie strengthens contribution to Viksit Bharat through logistics, manufacturing and sustainable growth
Posted On: 21 SEP 2026 2:00PM by PIB Kolkata

Kolkata; September 21, 2026

 

 Balmer Lawrie & Co. Ltd., a Miniratna-I Central Public Sector Enterprise under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, continued to contribute to the Government of India’s vision of Viksit Bharat through its diversified operations spanning logistics, manufacturing, travel services, technology, skill development and sustainable business practices, stated shri Adhip Nath Palchaudhuri, Chairman and Managing Director, Balmer Lawrie while interacting with the media here today. 

Marking its 160th year of service and nation-building, the Company recorded a net turnover of Rs.2,78,459.58 lakh in 2025-26, registering an 8.03% growth over the previous year, while Profit Before Tax strengthening to Rs.33,086.61 lakhs, up from Rs.31,378.99 lakhs in FY 2024-25 - driven largely by the exceptional performance of the Travel & Vacations and Logistics business, which capitalised on optimised operational efficiencies.

Strengthening India’s logistics and supply-chain ecosystem, Balmer Lawrie handled 1,80,479 TEUs through its Container Freight Stations during the year and commenced transportation of finished steel products from SAIL’s Rourkela Steel Plant using BFNS 22.9-tonne wagons on long-haul routes. The Company also modernised its Industrial Packaging Plant at Chittoor, while its Chemicals SBU achieved its highest-ever turnover and profit, supporting domestic manufacturing capabilities and value creation.

Technology and innovation remained integral to the Company’s growth strategy, the CMD said adding that Balmer Lawrie initiated the SAP S/4HANA migration project “HANAMAN” to strengthen digital transformation, automation and integrated business processes. Its research capabilities also received national recognition, with a paper on sustainable grease solutions from its Applications Research Laboratory winning the Best Paper Award at the 28th NLGI-IC Lubricating Grease Conference.

As part of the Government of India’s Skill India initiative, Balmer Lawrie contributed Rs. 85 lakh towards the operational expenditure of Skill Development Institutes during 2025-26 and continued apprenticeship training under the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme, he mentioned. The Company also rolled out Pragati, a women’s leadership development programme, while its CSR initiatives remained aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat, the UN Sustainable Development Goals and inclusive development, he added.
Shri Palchaudhuri said, Balmer Lawrie’s sustainability efforts included plantation of 5,270 trees at two critically polluted locations and adoption of indigenous sink reactor technology and circular scrubbing systems in its Chemicals SBU. Recognised for operational excellence, CSR and sustainability, corporate governance and inclusive workplace initiatives, the Company’s performance during 2025-26 reflects the continuing role of Central Public Sector Enterprises in strengthening India’s manufacturing, logistics, skills, technology and sustainable development ecosystem towards the broader objective of Viksit Bharat, the CMD added.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Railways
Preparations Underway for Special Campaign 6 for Institutionalizing Swachhata and Disposal of Pending Matters over Indian Railways
Focus on E-Waste Disposal, Scrap Disposal, Space Management and Clearance of Pending References
Over 150 Nodal Officers Designated for Monitoring and Coordinating Campaign Activities
Posted On: 21 SEP 2026 1:32PM by PIB Delhi

Special Campaign 6 for institutionalizing Swachhata and minimizing pendency in Government offices has been launched by the Government of India. The campaign is structured into two phases: the Preparatory Phase from 15th to 30th September 2026 for setting targets, followed by the main Implementation Phase from 2nd to 31 October 2026.

During the previous Campaign 5.0, the Ministry of Railways demonstrated significant progress by achieving 100% of the identified targets pertaining to disposal of public grievances, VIP references, and other pending matters. Remarkable achievements included the release of 6.06 lakh square feet of space and the generation of revenue amounting to ₹570 Crore.

The Ministry of Railways is fully prepared for the successful implementation of the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters 6 (SCDPM 6) across all its field units, attached and subordinate offices, PSUs, and autonomous bodies. The Railway Board is closely monitoring the preparations to accord highest priority to the campaign. Detailed guidelines from the Department of Administrative Reforms And Public Grievances (DARPG) have been communicated to all field units to mobilize ground functionaries, identify campaign sites, and plan for space management. A D.O. letter from the Secretary, Railway Board, to all General Managers and Heads of other Units has also been issued in this regard.

Detailed instructions have been issued to all Zonal Railways, Divisional Offices, Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), Production Units (PUs), and Central Training Institutes to ensure saturation-level participation. More than 150 nodal officers have been designated across Indian Railways to coordinate the effort and will collect progress information on a daily basis and will send it to the Railway Board enabling it to feed directly into DARPG's central SCDPM monitoring portal, facilitating real-time tracking and weekly high-level reviews.

As the preparatory phase is now underway, targets are being finalized with respect to key campaign parameters. In line with this year's focus, special emphasis is placed on "Effective Collection, Segregation, and Disposal of E-Waste" as per E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022, scrap disposal under General Financial Rules (GFR), office space beautification, process/rule simplification and including clearance of pending references.

Following the successful organisation of Rail Chaupal (SCDPM 4.0) and Amrit Samvaad (SCDPM 5.0), the Ministry will organise “Rail Jan Samvaad” during SCDPM 6 to further strengthen public engagement and foster meaningful dialogue with citizens.

Reaffirming its commitment to embedding cleanliness as a routine operational standard, the Ministry of Railways continues to prioritize seamless public engagement and the prompt disposal of pending references. With coordinated planning and dedicated participation across all units, the Ministry aims to make Special Campaign 6 a resounding success.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Council of Scientific and Industrial Research Hosts ‘CSIR SciQuiz’ on MY Bharat Portal
Posted On: 21 SEP 2026 1:12PM by PIB Delhi

The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), Ministry of Science and Technology, in collaboration with the Department of Youth Affairs, Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports has launched the CSIR Science & Innovation Quiz (CSIR SciQuiz) on the MY Bharat (Mera Yuva Bharat) Portal, as part of the activities marking CSIR’s 85th Foundation Day celebrations.

The quiz is being conducted from 20–26 September 2026 and is open to all Indian citizens. The quiz comprises multiple-choice questions and features questions based on CSIR’s scientific achievements, technologies, innovations, institutions and contributions to society and the nation.

The questions span diverse areas of CSIR’s work, including healthcare, agriculture, environment, infrastructure, energy, aerospace, biotechnology and strategic technologies, highlighting the ways in which CSIR research is being translated into solutions for society and industry.

The initiative seeks to promote scientific awareness, curiosity and public engagement with science, particularly among the youth, while providing an interactive platform to learn about India’s premier network of research laboratories. It offers participants an engaging opportunity to discover CSIR’s scientific achievements, technologies, innovations and contributions to nation-building.

As part of the initiative, participants also have an exciting opportunity to win a day visit to a CSIR laboratory of their interest, offering a first-hand exposure to the country’s scientific research and innovation ecosystem.

The CSIR SciQuiz series will continue beyond the September session, with more quiz sessions planned on the MY Bharat Portal in the coming months, featuring different facets of CSIR’s research, innovations and achievements.

The initiative invites citizens to Explore. Learn. Compete. and Win and become part of CSIR’s continuing journey of taking science and innovation closer to society.

Link to participate: https://mybharat.gov.in/quizzes/yuva/

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister & Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah to inaugurate 3rd National Conference of Heads of ANTF of States/UTs in New Delhi on 22nd September
Home Minister Shri Amit Shah to lay foundation stones for NCB Zone Complexes in Lucknow & Dehradun
Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the guidance of Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah, the Government of India is working in mission mode to protect the country's youth from the adverse effects of drugs
Prime Minister Modi has set the goal of a 'Viksit Bharat' by 2047, and building a developed India is not possible without creating a drug-free India
Two-Day national conference to focus on role of ANTFs in achieving the targets/ deliverables envisaged in Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029)
Dismantling drug cartels, tackling synthetic drugs & clan labs, darknet & crypto investigations are high on agenda of discussion
Posted On: 21 SEP 2026 12:53PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah will inaugurate 3rd National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) Heads of States/UTs in New Delhi on Tuesday, 22 September 2026. On the occasion, Shri Amit Shah will also release TVCs to spread awareness against drugs and lay the foundation stones for the new complexes of Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) Zones in Lucknow and Dehradun. The best-performing ANTF among the States/UTs will also be felicitated during the event, alongside the launch of the revamped NCB website. The two-day conference, being organised by the NCB, will be attended by the Heads of ANTFs from 36 States and Union Territories, along with representatives from other concerned government departments and stakeholders.

Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the guidance of Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah, the Government of India is working in 'mission mode' to protect the nation's youth from the adverse effects of drug abuse. Prime Minister Modi has set the goal of a 'Viksit Bharat' by 2047, and realizing this vision is not possible without building a drug-free India. This conference will serve as a powerful platform to safeguard future generations from the menace of drugs.

Based on the theme of the “United Resolve, Shared Responsibility”, the conference will focus on progress of targets assigned to State/UTs ANTFs in recently released Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-29) and initiatives and efforts undertaken by the concerned stakeholders in combating the menace of drug trafficking and substance abuse across the country. The issues pertaining to identification and adoption of appropriate strategies to further strengthen the supply reduction, demand reduction and harm reduction measures of the Government of India will also be deliberated upon.

Aligned with the four strategic pillars of the Vision Document- (I) Enforcement, Intelligence and Operations, (II) Precursors and Synthetic Drugs Control, (III) Demand and Harm Reduction and (IV) Capacity Building and Coordination - eight Technical Sessions have been lined up for the event, which will be as follows:

  1. Vision Document for Narcotics Control (2026-2029)- Part-I: Institutional Mechanisms
  2. Dismantling Network Linkages & Cartels – Part: I
  3. Vision Document for Narcotics Control (2026-2029)- Part-II: Demand Reduction, Prevention & Rehabilitation
  4. Dismantling Network Linkages & Cartels- Part: II
  5.  Improving Effectiveness of Enforcement
  6. Precursors, Synthetic Drugs & Clan Labs
  7. Destruction of Illicit Cultivation & Alternate Cropping
  8. Darknet & Crypto Investigation

Reiterating the need for a whole-of-government approach, the deliberations will enable participating states, departments and agencies to move forward with renewed commitment towards effectively combating drug trafficking across the country over the next three years. The discussions are expected to generate actionable strategies to further strengthen drug law enforcement and keep the youth of the country away from drugs. This national event will also seek to further deepen a future-ready partnership between NCB and State/UT ANTFs to combat drug abuse and realise the vision of a Drug-Free India.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Communications
item.description: Ministry of Communications Department of Telecommunications Cautions Citizens against fraudulent issuance of SIM cards, misuse of telecom identifiers, or tampering with IMEI numbers Misuse May Attract Up to Three Years’ Imprisonment and ₹50 Lakh Fine Citizens advised to use the Sanchar Saathi Portal and Mobile App to verify and secure their mobile connections and handsets Posted On: 21 SEP 2026 12:23PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) Madhya Pradesh (MP) LSA, has taken firm action against fraudulent SIM issuance. Recent cybercrime investigations…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
Department of Telecommunications Cautions Citizens against fraudulent issuance of SIM cards, misuse of telecom identifiers, or tampering with IMEI numbers
Misuse May Attract Up to Three Years’ Imprisonment and ₹50 Lakh Fine
Citizens advised to use the Sanchar Saathi Portal and Mobile App to verify and secure their mobile connections and handsets
Posted On: 21 SEP 2026 12:23PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) Madhya Pradesh (MP) LSA, has taken firm action against fraudulent SIM issuance. Recent cybercrime investigations have brought to light some instances in which a Point of Sale (PoS) agent in Chhattisgarh was found to have illegally activated 25 mobile connections (SIMs) using citizens’ identification documents without their knowledge or consent.

Following this, the DoT and Telecom Service Providers immediately blacklisted the concerned PoS, preventing it from issuing mobile connections (SIMs) in the future. These 25 mobile connections were examined on the Digital Intelligence Platform (DIP) of the DoT, and those identified as suspicious were subjected to re-verification. Numbers failing re-verification were subsequently deactivated.

DoT’s Advisory

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) reiterates that fraudulent issuance of SIM cards, misuse of telecom identifiers, or tampering with IMEI numbers is a punishable offence under the Telecommunications Act, 2023. Such violations may attract imprisonment of up to three years and fines up to ₹50 lakh. Compliance with the provisions of the Telecommunications Act, 2023 and the rules framed thereunder is essential for preventing telecom-related fraud, protecting citizens and ensuring a safe, secure and trusted telecommunication environment.

Citizens are cautioned not to share or transfer SIM cards issued in their name, as legal liability may extend to the original subscriber if the SIM is found to be misused. To safeguard themselves, citizens are advised to regularly verify their mobile connections through the Sanchar Saathi Portal (www.sancharsaathi.gov.in) and Mobile App. The platform enables users to check all mobile numbers issued in their name and block those that are unnecessary or not genuinely theirs. These measures are significant to prevent misuse of telecom resources in cyber frauds and to ensure a safe and secure communication environment. With the rapid expansion of mobile connectivity and digital services across India, the misuse of SIMs, telecommunication identifiers, including the International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) number of mobile devices, has emerged as a matter of serious concern. Such misuse can compromise the safety of citizens and pose risks to the security and integrity of telecommunication networks. The Government of India has put in place stringent legal provisions to prevent tampering with and misuse of unique telecommunication identifiers.

What Citizens Should Avoid

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) advises citizens to refrain from:

  • Using, procuring or assembling devices such as modems, modules, SIM Boxes or other equipment with configurable or tampered IMEIs;
  • Procuring SIM cards through fake documents, fraud, cheating or impersonation;
  • Transferring, selling or handing over SIM cards obtained in their name to others who may misuse them;
  • Using mobile applications, websites or any other means to modify Calling Line Identity (CLI) or other telecommunication identifiers;
  • Procuring SIM cards in their own name and subsequently loaning, renting or muling of SIM for misuse in cyber fraud or any other unlawful activity, that may result in legal liability for the original subscriber; and
  • Using devices with tampered IMEI numbers, obtaining SIM cards through fraudulent means, or transferring SIM cards to persons who misuse them and can have serious legal consequences.

Verification and Reporting through Sanchar Saathi

The Government has put in place robust measures to prevent the misuse of telecommunication resources and strengthen the safety and security of India's telecommunications ecosystem. Citizens can access various services available under the Sanchar Saathi initiative to verify and protect their mobile connections and devices. Citizens are urged to remain vigilant and make use of the digital tools available through the Sanchar Saathi initiative to verify and secure their mobile handsets.

The IMEI details of a mobile handset can be verified through the Sanchar Saathi platform by using Check Genuineness of Your Mobile handset facility. The service enables citizens to check details such as the brand name, model name and manufacturer information associated with the device.

Citizens are encouraged to visit the Sanchar Saathi Portal at www.sancharsaathi.gov.in or download the Sanchar Saathi Mobile App to access the various citizen-centric services available on the platform.

For Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.dot.app.sancharsaathi

For iOS:  https://apps.apple.com/app/sancharsaathi/id6739700695

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
INDIAN NAVAL SHIPS SAHYADRI AND KULISH ARRIVE AT SUBIC BAY, PHILIPPINES FOR ADMM-PLUS JCA
Posted On: 21 SEP 2026 11:37AM by PIB Delhi

As part of the Indian Navy’s Operational Deployment, Indian Naval Ships Sahyadri and Kulish arrived at Subic Bay, Philippines, on 20 Sep 2026 to participate in the ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting (ADMM)-Plus Joint Cooperation Activity (JCA).

The ADMM-Plus JCA brings together maritime forces from ASEAN Member States and eight Plus countries for professional and operational engagements aimed at enhancing interoperability, fostering mutual understanding and strengthening cooperation in the maritime domain.

The participation of Indian Naval Ships in the ADMM-Plus JCA is in consonance with the Government of India’s Act East Policy and the vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions), underscoring India’s continued commitment to multilateral maritime cooperation and constructive engagement with regional partners. The deployment will provide opportunities for the Indian Navy to interact with participating maritime forces through professional and operational engagements, contributing to greater understanding of shared maritime challenges.

The port call also reflects the growing maritime engagement between India and the Philippines. Building upon recent bilateral engagements and the establishment of the India–Philippines Strategic Partnership in Aug 2025, the deployment provides an opportunity to further strengthen professional linkages and maritime cooperation between the two countries.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Rashtriya Sankalp Samaroh Witnesses Participation of Over 4 Lakh Youth Across More Than 1,000 Locations Nationwide
Posted On: 20 SEP 2026 9:58PM by PIB Delhi

Rashtriya Sankalp Samaroh under The Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat – 100 Weeks Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan, was organised across more than 1,000 locations across India, witnessing the participation of over 4 lakh youth and citizens. The nationwide mobilisation brought together young people, partner organisations and communities in a collective expression of commitment towards building a Nasha Mukt Bharat.

The programme was organised across 460 MY Bharat Districts, 240 locations of partner organisations of MY Bharat, and more than 300 locations by Spiritual Organisations, Industry Associations and University Associations, creating a broad-based platform for youth and citizens to participate in the Nasha Mukt Yuva movement.

The Rashtriya Sankalp Samaroh centred on the spirit of collective resolve and youth-led participation, with participants coming together for the Nasha Mukt Pledge and Signature Campaign. The programme also encouraged creative and participatory forms of engagement, including youth-led discussions, awareness activities and other local initiatives that brought the message of a Nasha Mukt lifestyle closer to communities

The nationwide mobilisation reflects the growing participation of young people and partner organisations in the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat campaign, which seeks to promote awareness, prevention, healthy choices and positive youth engagement. By bringing together institutions, organisations and communities, the Sankalp Samaroh provided a common platform for reinforcing the importance of informed choices and healthier lifestyles among young people.

The programme forms part of the 100 Weeks Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan, conceived as a sustained youth movement with a focus on prevention, awareness, health, fitness and life skills. The initial activity cycle is structured around three themes—My Health, My Pride; Fit Youth, Addiction-Free Youth; and Life Skills Month—through which youth participation will continue to be encouraged through community-based and youth-centric activities.

 

The nationwide participation on 20 September follows the mobilisation undertaken on 18 September, when activities under the campaign were organised across institutions and communities. The two-day mobilisation has brought together youth and citizens through pledges, signatures, dialogue and community participation, giving a strong start to the sustained campaign.

The Rashtriya Sankalp Samaroh underscores that building a Nasha Mukt Bharat is a collective endeavour, requiring sustained awareness, positive choices and active participation from young people, institutions and communities.

The Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports will continue to facilitate youth-led engagement under the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat – 100 Weeks Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan, encouraging young people to carry the message forward through sustained participation and positive action..

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Corporate Affairs
IICA hosts important session on ‘IBC as an Evolving Law Through the Amendments’,.
M.S. Sahoo, former Chairperson, IBBI says markets evolve faster than litigation, making subordinate legislation and regulatory mechanisms important instruments for responding to emerging situations.
Posted On: 20 SEP 2026 8:36PM by PIB Delhi

Under the “Meet the Legend” programme, the Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), Manesar, hosted an insightful session on “IBC as an Evolving Law Through the Amendments” featuring Dr. M. S. Sahoo, former Chairperson of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) and a well-known figure in the development and evolution of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC).

The session commenced with a warm welcome and the setting of the context by Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh, DG & CEO, IICA, who highlighted the importance of learning directly from distinguished practitioners and thought leaders who have contributed significantly to the evolution of India's insolvency ecosystem.

Dr. M. S. Sahoo provided the participants with a comprehensive perspective on the evolution of the IBC through successive amendments and regulatory developments. Drawing upon his extensive experience, he discussed the concept of experimentation in economic laws, emphasising that economic legislation must continuously evolve in response to changing market realities.

He highlighted that markets evolve much faster than litigation can keep pace with, making subordinate legislation and regulatory mechanisms important instruments for responding to emerging situations.

He explained that regulations can be framed for the provisions of the Code and for achieving the purposes and objectives of the Code, thereby enabling the insolvency framework to respond more effectively to practical challenges.

The session provided the PGIP participants with valuable insights into the dynamic nature of insolvency law, the relationship between legislation, subordinate legislation and market developments, and the importance of continuously adapting the insolvency framework to address emerging economic and legal challenges.

The interaction offered the students an opportunity to understand the IBC not merely as a static statute, but as an evolving economic law shaped by market experience, judicial interpretation, regulatory interventions and legislative amendments.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Corporate Affairs
IICA’s Meet the Legend Programme Explores ‘PMLA–IBC Interface’
Hon’ble Member appellate tribunal Shri Balesh Kumar Highlights Synergy Between Insolvency Code and Anti-Money Laundering Law
PGIP Cohort Gains Practical Insights on Financial Investigation, Asset Tracing and Judicial Trends
Posted On: 20 SEP 2026 8:34PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), Manesar, under its ‘Meet the Legend’ programme, recently hosted an engaging session for the 8th Post Graduate Insolvency Programme (PGIP) cohort. The lecture on “PMLA–IBC Interface: Emerging Bonhomie” was delivered by Mr. Balesh Kumar, Hon’ble Member, Appellate Tribunal (PMLA, FEMA, PBPTA, NDPSA and SAFEMA), Government of India. 

Welcoming the dignitary, Mr. Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh, Director General & CEO, IICA, emphasised the importance of strengthening the interface between the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016 and the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002. He highlighted Section 32A of the IBC, noting that despite its precise drafting, harmonised implementation continues to face challenges. 

 

Mr. Kumar provided an extensive overview of the PMLA framework, explaining the stages of money laundering—Placement, Layering and Integration—and the relevance of hawala transactions in financial investigations. He discussed key provisions including Sections 3, 4, 5, 8, 44 and 45, illustrating their practical implications through judicial precedents. 

 

Special focus was placed on the PMLA–IBC interface, particularly the complexities when corporate debtor assets face attachment under PMLA during insolvency resolution. The evolving judicial approach towards harmonising insolvency objectives with anti-money laundering enforcement was explained in detail. 

 

The session reinforced the need for a multidisciplinary understanding of insolvency law, financial investigation, asset tracing and regulatory enforcement. The ‘Meet the Legend’ programme continues to enrich PGIP participants by connecting them directly with eminent members of the judiciary, tribunals, regulators and the corporate ecosystem.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
President of India addresses Valedictory Session of NGT’s International Conference on ‘The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics’ in New Delhi
Conference concludes with emphasis on translating Commitments into Effective Action and sustained International Cooperation for a Sustainable, Resilient and Equitable Future
Posted On: 20 SEP 2026 7:02PM by PIB Delhi

President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, today addressed the valedictory session of the National Green Tribunal’s (NGT) two-day International Conference on ‘The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics’ in New Delhi. The valedictory session was attended by Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs, and Power, Shri Manohar Lal; Judge (Supreme Court of India), Justice B.V. Nagarathna; Chairperson (NGT), Justice Prakash Shrivastava; and Solicitor General of India, Shri Tushar Mehta.

 

In her keynote address, the President lauded the National Green Tribunal for its role in strengthening environmental governance, and laid stress on strengthening climate resilience through people-centric and community-based adaptation approaches rooted in traditional knowledge.

(Press Release Link: https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasepage.aspx?PRID=2312728&reg=3&lang=1)

Addressing the occasion, Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal highlighted India’s efforts to balance rapid development with environmental sustainability, noting that non-fossil sources account for nearly 55 per cent of installed generation capacity. He said India had achieved its 50 per cent non-fossil capacity target five years ahead of schedule. He also highlighted initiatives in sustainable urban development, water security, public transport, green mobility and electric vehicles, stressing the need for positive collective action to address climate change.

In her speech, Justice B.V. Nagarathna said environmental governance must balance development and conservation, present needs and future interests, while accounting for differentiated impacts across communities and generations. She highlighted the Supreme Court of India’s shift towards an ecocentric approach and stressed effective institutions, enforcement, transparency, accountability and access to justice. She said interconnected challenges such as climate change, biodiversity loss, pollution and water scarcity require cooperation among jurisdictions, knowledge-sharing and equitable responsibility among nations.

NGT Chairperson Justice Prakash Shrivastava, in his valedictory address, said the discussions over the two days had highlighted the need to move beyond identifying environmental challenges towards building laws, institutions and partnerships capable of responding to them. He said climate action must be inclusive and equitable, particularly attentive to vulnerable communities and future generations, while environmental law must remain responsive and forward-looking, embracing technology, innovation, sustainable finance and just transition.

In his remarks, Solicitor General of India Shri Tushar Mehta said environmental challenges require the combined wisdom of law, governance, science, economics and society. He emphasised the need to balance biodiversity protection with climate action and development, supported by scientific assessment, innovation and sustainable development. He said environmental protection is not an impediment to human progress but a condition for enduring progress, requiring stronger institutions, effective implementation and responsible governance.

On the occasion, Shri Manohar Lal released NGT’s Souvenir titled ‘Harit Nyayam’ and presented its first copy to the President of India. The document chronicles the establishment, growth and achievements of the Tribunal. It is also an important repository for policy makers, legal fraternity and the citizens of the country as it is a lasting reflection of ideas, perspectives and collective resolve that have shaped the two-day conference.

The two-day Conference, inaugurated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 19.09.2026, brought together jurists, academicians, policymakers, scientists, environmental experts and other stakeholders from 17 countries, along with the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and the Asian Development Bank (ADB). The Conference provided a platform for dialogue and knowledge exchange on judicial, scientific, policy and institutional best practices, while encouraging collaborative action on pressing environmental and climate challenges.

The second day featured two technical sessions, as below:

  1. ‘Planetary Environmental Challenges and Cooperation’, focusing on interconnected environmental and climate challenges, shared natural resources, competing national interests, transboundary cooperation and regional and international best practices.
  2. ‘Forests for the Future: A Dialogue on Forest Protection & Restoration’, focused on forest governance, sustainable forest management, community participation, biodiversity conservation, emerging threats to forests, legal and institutional mechanisms, and the use of technology and scientific and satellite-based monitoring. The session also featured reflections on the way forward, including a shared vision, priority actions, regional cooperation, institutional partnerships and measurable goals.

The deliberations over the two days provided an opportunity for judicial, scientific, policy and institutional perspectives from different jurisdictions to converge on common environmental challenges. The Conference emphasised the need for stronger environmental governance, climate justice, institutional cooperation, knowledge exchange and practical approaches to addressing transboundary environmental challenges.

The Conference concluded with a shared emphasis on translating environmental principles and commitments into effective action, stronger institutions and sustained international cooperation for a sustainable, resilient and equitable future.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia inspects site identified for Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior along with Secretary, Department of Telecommunications and senior officials
24 Companies Propose ₹5,500 Crore Investment for Asia’s First Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior: Union Minister Shri Scindia
TMZ expected to create over 18,000+ direct and indirect employment opportunities
Proposed investment of ₹5,500 crore to give fresh impetus to telecom equipment manufacturing and industrial development in Gwalior
170 acres identified for the first phase; 24 global companies have initiated the application process
Posted On: 20 SEP 2026 6:49PM by PIB Delhi

Gwalior is set to emerge as a major hub for India’s telecom manufacturing sector with the establishment of Asia’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ). Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia today, inspected the site identified for the proposed TMZ at Shrimant Madhavrao Scindia Counter Magnet City (SADA, Gwalior) along with the Secretary, Department of Telecommunications, Government of India, and other senior officials.

The proposed TMZ will be established with an investment of approximately ₹5,500 crore and is expected to create over 18,000 direct employment opportunities.

The Union Minister said that the project is not about setting up a single industrial unit, but about creating a complete industrial ecosystem comprising 24-25 telecom manufacturing units in Gwalior. These units will manufacture telecom equipment and a range of components, strengthening the city’s position as an emerging telecom manufacturing hub.

170 Acres Identified for First Phase

Approximately 90+ acres in SADA and 70+ acres in the IT Park, approx. 170 acres, have been identified for the proposed TMZ.

Shri Scindia said the interest from investors has been significant, with applications currently exceeding the land available. Accordingly, additional land will be identified for expansion of the first phase of the TMZ, with land allocation to be increased as required.

SADA was originally established as a Counter Magnet City with the vision of developing Gwalior as a new industrial centre and a counter-magnet to Delhi. The proposed TMZ takes this industrial vision forward by creating Asia’s first dedicated Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior.

24 Companies Initiate Application Process for ₹5,500 Crore Investment

In July 2026, the Department of Telecommunications, under Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia, and the Government of Madhya Pradesh, under Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav, signed an MoU for establishing the TMZ. This was followed by investor roadshows in Delhi and Mumbai in August, led by Union Minster Shri Scindia and Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav. The Delhi roadshow witnessed investment commitments of approximately ₹3,500 crore, with the potential to generate around 14,000 employment opportunities. The Mumbai roadshow, held in August, saw commitments of approximately ₹2,000 crore, with around 4,000 employment opportunities.

Shri Scindia clarified that these investments are not merely verbal commitments. Companies that expressed interest were asked to participate in the application process at the time of land allocation. As a result, 24 companies have now initiated the application process for setting up units in the TMZ.

Attractive Incentive Package from Madhya Pradesh and the Centre

Shri Scindia thanked Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav and the Government of Madhya Pradesh for developing an attractive incentive package for the telecom manufacturing industry. The package includes incentives linked to land lease, power, employment and production, as well as incentives focused on environmental sustainability and green development. In addition, the Department of Telecommunications has proposed a Common Testing Lab package of approximately ₹500 crore.

Connectivity, Infrastructure and Skilled Talent to Drive Gwalior’s Growth

Shri Scindia highlighted Gwalior’s connectivity, infrastructure and skilled human resources as key strengths for the development of the TMZ. The approximately 120-km Agra-Gwalior High-Speed Corridor is being developed to strengthen Gwalior’s connectivity with Delhi and major markets across North India, bringing the city closer to key industrial and commercial centres.

Gwalior is also located on major railway routes, facilitating the movement of goods and human resources to different parts of the country. The city’s airport has been developed at a cost of approximately ₹650 crore in a record 16 months, further strengthening air connectivity with major cities including Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru.

Gwalior also has a strong base of engineering institutions, with approximately 25,000 engineering students graduating every year. This will help ensure the availability of the technical and skilled workforce required by the telecom manufacturing sector.

The TMZ is being planned as a complete ecosystem covering six key verticals of telecom manufacturing. Shri Scindia said that the Government of India, the Government of Madhya Pradesh and all concerned departments are fully prepared to provide investors with the necessary support to establish their manufacturing units in Gwalior.

The establishment of Asia’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior marks a new chapter in the city’s industrial development and carries forward the industrial vision and legacy of Shrimant Madhavrao Scindia Counter Magnet City.

Shri Scindia also announced that following his two-day visit to Gwalior, he will travel to Bengaluru on 22 September to participate in a roadshow with investors from the telecom sector.

item.content:encoded:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES THE VALEDICTORY SESSION OF THE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON ‘THE FUTURE OF ENVIRONMENT AND CLIMATE DYNAMICS’
STRENGTHEN CLIMATE RESILIENCE THROUGH PEOPLE-CENTRIC AND COMMUNITY-BASED ADAPTATION APPROACHES ROOTED IN TRADITIONAL KNOWLEDGE: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
Posted On: 20 SEP 2026 6:09PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu graced the valedictory session of the International Conference on ‘The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics’, organized by the National Green Tribunal, in New Delhi today (September 20, 2026).

Speaking on the occasion, the President said that climate change creates imbalances across multiple levels of human existence. Issues such as biodiversity loss, water stress and land degradation are deeply intertwined with it. Climate change is also having serious repercussions on food security, health, and livelihoods.

The President said that a well-structured framework of policies and actions is essential to effectively address such a complex challenge. The framework must ensure the active participation of not only governments and legal experts but also the communities most affected by climate change. Special sensitivity towards the needs of rural and forest-dwelling societies, small farmers, women, and other vulnerable communities is crucial, as they bear the brunt of natural disasters.

The President underlined that traditional knowledge systems, along with the practices and lived experiences of local communities, play a vital role in enhancing climate adaptation capacity. She said that we must strengthen climate resilience through people-centric and community-based adaptation approaches rooted in traditional knowledge. She stated that sustainable afforestation can also play a significant role in enhancing climate resilience. Afforestation efforts that nurture biodiversity and are aligned with local conditions can be instrumental in this regard. She stated that the true objective of sustainable afforestation is not merely planting trees, but rather restoring healthy and self-sustaining ecosystems.

The President said that developing countries should chart a path that enhances resilience while maintaining the pace of development. Commitments to responsible climate action must align with the country's development needs and economic aspirations. They must also be technically feasible. She was happy to note that many such aspects have been discussed at the Conference.

The President said that India has done commendable work in fostering environmental awareness by engaging common citizens, especially the youth. The Government of India's 'Mission LiFE' initiative has demonstrated that meaningful strides towards ecological restoration can be achieved through public participation and community ownership.

The President appreciated the National Green Tribunal for bringing experts, judges, jurists, and key stakeholders from various countries, who are active in environmental issues, on one platform. She expressed confidence that deliberations and action plans from this Conference will contribute to paving the way for building climate-resilient societies, grounded in inclusive policies and effective actions.

item.content:encoded:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA TO VISIT GUJARAT FROM SEPTEMBER 21 TO 23
Posted On: 20 SEP 2026 6:01PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu will visit Gujarat from September 21 to 23, 2026.

On September 22, the President will grace the presentation ceremony of the 72nd National Film Awards at Ekta Nagar, Kevadia.

On September 23, the President will grace the 75th annual convocation ceremony of the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda at Vadodara. On the same day, she will launch Brahma Kumaris’ campaign ‘Spiritual Awakening for World Renewal’ and inaugurate the ‘Global Spiritual Palace’ Retreat Centre at Vadodara. She will also virtually launch the campaign ‘Youth for Viksit Bharat: Awakening Inner Strength for Nation Building’ of Brahma Kumaris Nadiad on the occasion.
